In an increasingly uncertain global 
landscape, unprecedented 
disruptions have become the new 
normal. The West Asia crisis is 
posing signiﬁcant risks to the Indian 
economy, due to rising energy 
prices and disruptions in key supply 
chains. While the Indian economy 
remains resilient, recent trends 
have underscored the need for a 
comprehensive roadmap to 
strengthen the country’s economic 
security over the medium to 
long term.
Amidst these external shocks, CII 
has sought to ensure that India 
remains steadfast in its journey 
towards Viksit Bharat, with Industry 
playing a pivotal role in driving 
resilience and growth. CII has 
articulated a comprehensive 
12-point agenda for Industry and a 
20-point agenda for the 
Government, addressing both 
operational and strategic 
dimensions while enhancing India’s 
global competitiveness.
India has retained its position as the 
world’s fastest-growing major 
economy for the fourth consecutive 
year, despite ongoing geopolitical 
tensions, rising protectionism, tariﬀ 
uncertainties, and a changing world 
order. Real GDP growth for 
2025–26 is estimated at 7.6 per 
cent (base year 2022–23), higher 
than the 7.1 per cent recorded in FY 
2024-25.
A key focus of CII’s work has been 
strengthening the policy 
ecosystem, with over 1200 policy 
suggestions submitted to the Union 
and State Governments, resulting in 
the acceptance of around 93 
recommendations. CII’s 
recommendations found strong 
resonance in key reform measures. 
The new Labour Code is an example 
of this, which consolidates 29 laws 
into a uniﬁed framework, bringing 
greater clarity and consistency. 
While their full impact will depend 
on eﬀective implementation, they 
represent a decisive step towards a 
modern, future-ready labour 
market.
Under GST 2.0, the rationalisation 
of slabs into a dual-rate structure of 
5 per cent and 18 per cent is 
expected to be a masterstroke in 
simpliﬁcation, making compliance 
easier, reducing cascading eﬀects, 
and most importantly, 
strengthening the competitiveness 
of the Indian Industry.
The Government’s continued focus 
on regulatory simpliﬁcation and 
ease of doing business has sent 
positive signals to investors. The 
passage of the Jan Vishwas 
Amendment Bill, 2026, is a 
milestone that CII has long 
advocated for. The review of FEMA 
(Non-Debt Instruments) Rules, the 
extension of customs advance 
rulings, and the rationalisation of

compliance frameworks will 
enhance predictability and reduce 
transaction costs for businesses.
In alignment with the 
Government’s reform agenda, CII 
has focused on key pillars, including 
next-gen reforms, manufacturing, 
technology and Artiﬁcial 
Intelligence (AI), sustainability and 
energy transition, livelihoods, 
and trust.
CII advocated making Advanced 
Manufacturing a core focus under 
the National Manufacturing 
Mission to accelerate adoption 
of cutting-edge practices and 
improve productivity, quality, and 
energy eﬃciency.
The CII Centres of Excellence have 
made sustained eﬀorts to enhance 
the competitiveness of the Indian 
Industry across sectors through 
training programmes and special 
initiatives. The CII Centre for 
Artiﬁcial Intelligence, launched last 
year, is continuing to accelerate AI 
adoption across Industry by 
fostering innovation, building 
capacity, and enabling responsible 
regulation. Building on over two 
decades of the Centre of 
Excellence for Sustainable 
Development’s work in advancing 
sustainable growth, CII also 
launched ‘/uni0927/uni0930/uni093E’, its sustainability 
mascot, symbolising the next phase 
of its sustainability journey.
The year 2025 marked a turning 
point for the defence sector, 
anchored by Operation Sindoor and 
its designation as the Defence 
Reform Year. Over the past year, 
the Society of Indian Defence 
Manufacturers has advanced key 
policy reforms, including 
improvements in trial and quality 
assurance procedures aligned with 
the Government’s self-reliance 
mission.
Engagement with the global 
economy remains a key driver of 
seamless trade. CII led several 
high-level delegations across 
regions, fostering meaningful 
partnerships, and advancing Free 
Trade Agreements, opening new 
avenues for the Indian Industry.
The Government of India’s 
transformative agreement with the 
UK is set to enhance market access 
for employment-intensive sectors 
such as agriculture, marine 
products, textiles, and gems and 
jewellery, while creating 
opportunities for both large 
enterprises and MSMEs.
Another signiﬁcant milestone is the 
India–EU Agreement, which 
progressed with notable speed and 
collaboration, and strengthens 
strategic ties, boosts investment, 
enhances export competitiveness, 
and expands consumer choice.
A key forward-looking initiative has 
been the India-Oman 
Comprehensive Economic 
Partnership Agreement (CEPA), 
which enables deeper economic 
engagement with the Gulf region 
through reduced tariﬀs and 
streamlined trade norms.
The recently concluded CII 
delegation to China oﬀered 
valuable insights into the scale and 
pace of industrial transformation. 
Covering key sectors, the 
delegation engaged in high-level 
interactions, gaining a deeper 
understanding of the rapid 
advancements shaping global 
competitiveness.
At the ﬂagship CII Partnership 
Summit, high-level deliberations 
with Indian policymakers, over 30 
international ministers, and 
Industry leaders outlined key 
imperatives for Viksit Bharat. The 
summit reinforced global 
partnerships through MoUs and 
strategic engagements.
India stands at a deﬁning juncture, 
with strong macroeconomic 
fundamentals and bold reforms 
shaping its growth trajectory. As 
we move forward, sustained 
collaboration between 
Government, Industry, and key 
stakeholders will be critical to 
unlocking the next phase of 
growth. CII remains committed to 
enabling this transformation.
Rajiv Memani 
President, CII
2025-26
The role of Indian Industry in 
advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat 
has become even more critical in 
the current context of geopolitical 
tensions. Due to the West Asia 
crisis, sectors such as chemicals, 
fertilisers, metals, and aviation, 
among others, have been aﬀected 
through higher input costs, logistics 
delays, and tighter working capital 
conditions, with MSMEs and 
export-oriented manufacturing 
being particularly aﬀected.
Amid these ongoing disruptions, 
the resilience of the Indian Industry 
is being tested, underscoring the 
need for continued policy support 
to sustain momentum and growth.
Over the past year, CII has worked 
extensively to strengthen the Indian 
Industry through a wide range of 
initiatives.
Manufacturing lies at the heart of 
India’s long-term growth and 
strategic autonomy. With the 
potential to raise its share to over 
25 per cent of GDP, it can position 
India as a leading global hub for 
advanced manufacturing. In this 
context, CII has undertaken several 
initiatives and advocated for key 
policy recommendations, including 
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) 
schemes with lower investment 
thresholds for employment- 
intensive sectors such as leather, 
footwear, and furniture.
Equal emphasis has also been 
placed on leveraging the potential 
of the services sector, including 
integrating strategies that can 
unlock the next phase of expansion 
across hospitality, travel, and 
tourism services. A key ask for the 
hospitality sector is GST 
rationalisation to enhance price 
competitiveness and promote 
formalisation.
In healthcare, CII’s engagement 
focused on strengthening service 
delivery while enabling care models 
that enhance longevity and quality 
of life. Key priorities included 
responsible digital health adoption, 
improved alignment between 
providers and payers, and deeper 
international collaboration to build 
a resilient, future-ready healthcare 
ecosystem. The CII Centre for 
Health will drive multi-stakeholder 
collaboration and low-cost 
innovation in the sector.
CII advanced a cohesive education 
agenda spanning school and higher 
education. The focus was on 
improving the quality of education 
and research, strengthening faculty 
capacity, promoting responsible

integration of technology, and 
deepening Industry engagement 
aligned with the National 
Education Policy 2020 to build a 
globally competitive, 
Industry-ready talent pipeline.
A comprehensive MSME reform 
agenda was presented to the 
Government, covering regulatory 
simpliﬁcation, public procurement, 
access to ﬁnance, and technology 
adoption. Key recommendations 
included decriminalising minor 
compliance lapses, enabling 
self-certiﬁcation and digital dispute 
resolution, amending the MSMED 
Act 2006, and rationalising Quality 
Control Orders and labour 
compliance.
The 6th CII International Energy 
Conference and Exhibition 
addressed structural barriers and 
leveraged global partnerships. The 
event highlighted that India’s 
pathway to Net Zero is not only a 
climate imperative but also a 
cornerstone of long-term 
prosperity and energy security.
The Centre of Excellence (CoE) on 
Skills continued to bridge the skills 
gap and cultivate a future-ready 
workforce. CII Model Career 
Centres (MCCs), operating as 
Industry-led employment 
exchanges, provide aptitude-based 
career counselling, soft skills 
training, and placement support. 
With the addition of ﬁve new 
centres, 59 MCCs are now 
operational across 23 States, 
having counselled over 19.14 lakh 
candidates and placed more than 
12.86 lakh candidates.
The CoE on Employment and 
Livelihoods impacted over 2,500 
micro and small entrepreneurs 
across 36 districts in 11 States. 
These enterprises employ over 
43,000 people and generate a 
combined turnover exceeding INR 
13,000 crore.
The Indian Green Building Council, 
part of the CII Green Business 
Centre, has achieved a green 
building footprint of 15.25 billion 
sq ft, with over 18,600 registered 
projects. As IGBC marked its Silver 
Jubilee this year, it further 
strengthened its contribution to 
India’s Net Zero 2070 goals.
The CII Mission on Water catalysed 
Industry-led collective action to 
promote water-neutral practices. 
Twenty-four industrial plants were 
certiﬁed as ‘Aspiring Water Neutral’ 
and two as ‘Water Positive’, taking 
the cumulative total to 43 certiﬁed 
‘Water Neutral’ plants. These serve 
as lighthouse examples of scalable 
solutions for water security.
Training programmes conducted by 
the CII Centre for Manufacturing 
Excellence reached over 1,500 
organisations, 4,000 professionals, 
and 450 MSMEs, strengthening 
technical capabilities and improving 
business performance.
EXCON, in its 13th edition, 
witnessed over 1.2 lakh business 
visitors and more than 1,250 
exhibitors, including 134 
international participants from 20 
countries, showcasing India’s 
growing capabilities across sectors. 
The 16th edition of International 
Railway Equipment Expo was 
spread across approximately 
40,000 sq mtr, with more than 450 
companies representing over 15 
countries.
As India continues its growth 
journey, a strong and 
forward-looking Industry will be 
central to sustaining its 
momentum. I look forward to my 
tenure as President, CII and to 
leading the Industry ahead with 
purpose and direction.
R Mukundan
President Designate, CII
2025-26
Annual Report 2025-2614
CII has worked across the length 
and breadth of the country, 
through regional, state and zonal 
oﬃces, to support policy 
formulation and strengthen the 
business environment.
A key highlight from the East was 
the 4th edition of the East India 
Summit, which highlighted Eastern 
India’s emergence as an economic 
growth hub, where policymakers 
and Industry leaders from Bihar, 
Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and West 
Bengal outlined their development 
visions, showcasing reforms, startup 
momentum, and new-age 
investments.
CII North East undertook an 
extensive and multi-layered policy 
advocacy agenda during the year.
A major focus was CII’s 
comprehensive set of 
recommendations on the UNNATI 
2024 Scheme, including extension 
of the registration window, easing 
of compliance requirements, 
recognition of past investments, 
expansion of eligible sectors, and 
enhanced ﬁnancial outlay to 
accelerate industrial uptake. 
Parallel interventions were made to 
strengthen MSME ecosystems.
With representation across seven 
States and three Union Territories, 
CII Northern Region focused on 
enhancing industrial 
competitiveness, enabling ease of 
doing business (EoDB), 
strengthening infrastructure and 
skills, and fostering inclusive and 
sustainable growth through 
structured Government engagement 
and member-led initiatives.
CII Southern Region achieved 
signiﬁcant progress in advancing 
Industry priorities through 
structured policy dialogue and 
sectoral consultations. As many as 
121 policy recommendations were 
submitted to policymakers, of 
which 22 were accepted and 
implemented.
CII Western Region collaborated 
with the Governments of Goa, 
Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and 
Maharashtra, conducting over 40 
discussions with policymakers. 
Numerous Union and State 
Ministers, Chief Ministers, and 
senior secretariat oﬃcials 
participated in these engagements 
aimed at promoting investments 
and driving growth and 
development across States.

During 2025–26, the CII Foundation 
strengthened its initiatives for 
India’s inclusive development. 
Under the crop residue 
management programme, over 
two lakh farmers were enabled to 
adopt sustainable agricultural 
practices through machinery 
support, technical 
capacity-building, and farm straw 
management. The Foundation also 
strengthened early childhood 
education through Anganwadi 
centres in Andhra Pradesh, 
Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.
Translating dialogue into 
recognition and action, CII launched 
the CII Awards for Excellence in 
Disability Inclusion, marking a 
landmark step towards 
mainstreaming disability inclusion 
within the Industry. The Awards 
celebrate organisations that go 
beyond compliance to embed 
accessibility, equity, and 
opportunity into their 
organisational ethos, serving as 
exemplars and catalysts for 
systemic change.
The CII Centre for Women 
Leadership strengthened policy 
discourse on gender inclusion in 
India and globally through 
platforms such as the Alliance for 
Global Good – Gender Equity and 
Equality, and launched the ﬁrst 
Gender Parity Business Awards. 
These Awards recognised 
companies that integrated 
inclusion into their business 
strategy, operations, and 
decision-making processes. They 
also celebrated leaders advancing 
equity and inclusion, creating 
incentives for companies to adopt 
and expand gender-responsive 
policies.
The CII Family Business Network 
(FBN) – India Chapter continues to 
strengthen India’s family business 
ecosystem. The 24th CII-FBN India 
Annual Convention convened 
leaders from across the country for 
two days of reﬂection and dialogue 
on the core theme of stewardship.
CII actively strengthened India’s 
sports ecosystem through 
initiatives focused on promoting 
inclusivity, sparking innovation, and 
achieving excellence. CII supported 
grassroots talent development and 
celebrated key successes across the 
sports sector. Eﬀorts focused on 
enhancing corporate wellness 
programmes through sports 
participation.
Through structured policy dialogue, 
national platforms, and measurable 
social impact, Young Indians (Yi) 
reinforced the role of youth as 
partners in policy making, 
innovation, and implementation, 
contributing meaningfully to India’s 
long-term development agenda.
During the year, CII accelerated its 
outreach and deepened member 
engagement through focused, 
high-impact initiatives and service 
support. Through the Outreach 
Initiative, as many as 3,975 
members were engaged via virtual 
and in-person meetings at their 
premises.
These eﬀorts reﬂect CII’s continued 
commitment to strengthening 
India’s economic and social 
landscape through collaborative 
action and forward-looking policy 
engagement. I look forward to 
working with key stakeholders to 
navigate emerging opportunities 
and challenges, while contributing 
meaningfully to the nation’s 
development journey.
Dr Suchitra K Ella
Vice President, CII

ACCELERATING COMPETITIVENESS: GLOBALISATION, INCLUSIVITY, 
SUSTAINABILITY, TRUST
CII THEME FOR 2025-26
In a world undergoing rapid shifts due to 
geopolitical tensions, economic fragmentation, and 
the weaponisation of trade, trust has re-emerged as 
the bedrock of economic relationships. It is shaping 
trade and investment ﬂows, guiding policy choices, 
and providing the conﬁdence needed for long-term 
growth. At the same time, competitiveness, 
anchored in productivity, innovation, and 
operational eﬃciency, has become a deﬁning factor 
for economies seeking to lead in this uncertain 
landscape. As global priorities shift and trade 
strategies evolve, resilience, adaptability, and 
credibility are critical to maintaining economic 
momentum.
India stands out as a beacon of stability and growth 
in this dynamic context. With its robust 
macroeconomic fundamentals, reform-oriented 
governance, and diverse industrial capabilities, India 
is well-positioned to accelerate its economic rise.
The country’s future, however, will be deﬁned not just by 
the pace of its growth, but by the quality, how 
competitive, inclusive, sustainable, and trusted its 
economic model becomes.
With this backdrop, the Confederation of Indian Industry 
(CII) would further accelerate its focus on building 
competitiveness. It would work to accelerate the 
capability to compete better, not just in traditional sectors 
but in emerging high-tech, green, and digitised industries. 
CII this year will set in place actions for the immediate 
term, medium term and horizon strategies across the 
areas of competitiveness, globalisation, inclusivity, 
sustainability and building trust.
The CII Theme for 2025-26 has been conceptualised as 
Accelerating Competitiveness: Globalisation, Inclusivity, 
Sustainability, Trust.

ECONOMIC POLICY AND
RESEARCH
Amid global uncertainty, India remains the 
fastest-growing major economy, underpinned by 
macroeconomic stability and bold reforms, with CII 
closely partnering with Government to shape the 
reform agenda.
CII’s work on economic policy and research through 
the year was premised on the following four pillars:
- Boosting macroeconomic stability
- Employment generation
- Catalysing private investments
- Building competitiveness and boosting growth.
CII IndiaEdge 2025: Policies for a 
Competitive India
The event convened leaders from Government, 
Industry, policy institutions and representatives from 
65 CII aﬃliated associations to discuss India’s reform 
priorities ahead of the Union Budget and the 
Government’s ongoing strong reform push.
It brought together over 100 speakers and 1200 
participants across 22 sessions, covering 
macroeconomics, manufacturing competitiveness, 
sustainability, sectoral strategies and human capital. The 
deliberations reinforced CII’s role in advancing an inclusive 
reform agenda aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat. 
CII REPORTS AND PAPERS
Policy advocacy on a variety of issues was taken up 
through multiple reports and papers.
Reports
• Policies for a Competitive India
 Developed through extensive stakeholder 
consultations, the report presents a 
comprehensive reform agenda to strengthen 
India’s global competitiveness.

 Aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, it

• Boosting Growth & Employment in India’s 
Apparel Sector
 The report examines the apparel sector, a highly 
employment-intensive sector, through extensive 
Industry consultations, identifying structural barriers 
and competitiveness gaps. It evaluates the sector’s 
growth potential from an employment-generation 
perspective and proposes targeted reforms across 
trade policy, labour regulations, skilling, 
infrastructure and clusters to unlock large-scale job 
creation and strengthen global competitiveness.
• CII-IMD Reports on Future Readiness of Indian 
Industry
 CII partnered with IMD Business School, Lausanne, 
Switzerland to prepare ﬁrst-of-their-kind Future 
Readiness Reports for three sectors in India: 
automotive, pharmaceuticals and food & 
beverage. These reports, based on IMD’s 
proprietary methodology, assess the strength and 
resilience of each sector.

framework that are required to accomplish the 
goal of a ‘Swarna Andhra’.

Secretary, Department of Expenditure; Dr Arunish Chawla, Secretary, Department of Investment and Public Asset Management; Nagaraju Maddirala, 
Secretary, Department of Financial Services and Rajiv Memani at the Union Budget 2026-27 an Interactive Session with Ministry of Finance in New Delhi

pages.text:
Against the backdrop of global uncertainty and the vision of Viksit Bharat, CII’s policy proposals for the Union Budget 
2026–27 focused on mitigating tariﬀ shocks, ﬁscal pressures and external risks, while sustaining high, inclusive and 
sustainable growth. The proposals covered economic reforms, investment, infrastructure (physical and digital), 
human capital, technology and innovation, trade, micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), manufacturing, 
agriculture and sector-speciﬁc issues. 
CII engaged closely with the Government through a series of consultations, including discussions with Smt Nirmala 
Sitharaman, Minister of Finance and senior oﬃcials of the Ministry of Finance, to present these recommendations.
79 CII Budget recommendations were accepted; the key ones have been captured in the table below:
Debt Glide Path CII recommended reducing Central Government 
debt by 0.4–0.8% of GDP in 2026-27.
The Budget reduced Central Government debt 
by about 0.5% of GDP.
CII Policy Proposals for Union Budget 2026-27
CII Recommendations vs Union Budget 2026–27 Announcements
Subject CII Recommendations Budget Announcements
Fiscal Deﬁcit CII suggested a ﬁscal deﬁcit target of 4.2% 
(±0.1%) of GDP.
The ﬁscal deﬁcit was set at 4.3% of GDP.
Central Public 
Capex
CII proposed raising central capex by 
about 12% to INR 12.6 lakh crore.
Central capex was increased by about 11.5% to 
INR 12.2 lakh crore.
State Capex 
Support
CII recommended a 10% increase in capex 
loans to states under Special Assistance to 
States for Capital Investment (SASCI).
Capex support to states was increased by 33.3% 
to INR 2 lakh crore.
Government 
Receipts
CII suggested leveraging Public Sector 
Enterprises (PSEs) for resource mobilisation.
Miscellaneous capital receipts were sharply 
increased to INR 80,000 crore.
Infrastructure 
Finance
CII proposed a National Infrastructure 
Guarantee Corporation for Public Private 
Partnership (PPP) projects.
An Infrastructure Risk Guarantee Fund was 
announced for partial credit guarantees.
Logistics CII recommended faster development of 
multimodal logistics parks.
A Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme was 
announced to encourage modal shift.
Freight Corridors CII sought expedited development of three 
new freight corridors.
One new East–West Dedicated Freight Corridor 
was announced.
Blended Finance CII proposed a blended ﬁnance platform for 
priority sectors.
Asset recycling, municipal bond incentives and Viability 
Gap Funding-based measures were announced.
Special Economic Zone 
(SEZ) Ecosystem
CII recommended allowing SEZ units to sell into 
Domestic Tariﬀ Area (DTA) on equal terms.
Limited SEZ-to-DTA sales were allowed at 
concessional duty.
Pharma CII recommended mission-mode R&D 
funding and faster drug approvals.
An INR 10,000 crore Biopharma Shakti initiative 
was announced.
Chemicals CII suggested strengthening domestic 
chemical manufacturing.
Three dedicated Chemical Parks were 
announced.
Electronics and 
Semiconductors
CII recommended sectoral blueprints 
and supply chain resilience measures.
Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme 
outlay was increased and India Semiconductor 
Mission 2.0 was announced.
A. Economic Policy
Container 
Manufacturing
CII proposed a Production Linked Incentive 
scheme for container manufacturing.
An INR 10,000 crore container manufacturing 
scheme was announced.
Textiles CII suggested Textile Mega Clusters alongside 
Prime Minister Mega Integrated Textile Region 
and Apparel parks.
Mega Textile Parks were announced in 
challenge mode.
Annual Report 2025-2626
B. Direct Taxes
Subject CII Recommendations Budget Announcements
MSMEs CII proposed credit, equity and compliance 
support for MSMEs.
Credit guarantees, funds and compliance 
support measures were announced.
Corporate 
Governance
CII suggested reforms to build large Indian 
accounting ﬁrms.
The deﬁnition of ‘accountant’ was rationalised 
under tax rules.
Trade and Exports CII proposed a National Digital Trade Platform. A digital single-window clearance system was 
announced.
Financial Sector CII suggested next-generation banking and 
bond-market reforms.
A high-level banking committee and bond- 
market measures were announced.
Minimum Alternate Tax 
(MAT) For Startups
CII recommended MAT exemption during the 
tax-holiday period.
MAT rates were reduced and credits restricted, 
but no startup exemption was given.
Buyback Taxation CII suggested taxing buybacks as capital gains 
beyond accumulated proﬁts.
Buyback proceeds were proposed to be taxed as 
capital gains.
C. Indirect Taxes
Input Duty Structure CII recommended keeping low duties on non- 
domestic inputs.
Customs exemptions were extended and 
rationalised till 2028.
Customs 
Simpliﬁcation
CII suggested simplifying customs law and 
procedures.
Tariﬀ lines and eﬀective rates were simpliﬁed.
Digital Customs CII proposed Application Programming Interface 
(API)-based digital data ﬂows across systems.
Phased digitalisation of customs processes was 
announced.
Dispute 
Reduction
CII recommended strengthening dispute 
resolution architecture.
Tariﬀ rationalisation and clariﬁcation measures 
were announced.
Withholding 
Taxes
CII suggested rationalising withholding 
tax rates.
Several Tax Deducted at Source and Tax Collected 
at Source rates were reduced or clariﬁed.
Lower Tax Deducted at 
Source (TDS) Certiﬁcates
CII recommended strict timelines and 
deemed issuance.
Automated, rule-based lower or nil TDS 
certiﬁcates were proposed.
Dispute 
Resolution
CII suggested negotiated settlement of 
tax disputes.
Decriminalisation and immunity-based dispute- 
resolution measures were announced.
Non-residents CII sought compliance relief and exemptions 
for non-residents.
Multiple exemptions and simpliﬁcations for non- 
residents were announced.
Safe Harbour CII suggested aligning safe harbour margins 
with Advanced Pricing Agreements.
Safe harbour thresholds for IT services were 
sharply increased and automated.
Advanced Pricing 
Agreement (APA) Regime
CII recommended faster and more eﬃcient 
APA processes.
Unilateral APAs were proposed to be concluded 
within two years.
Ferrous Scrap CII recommended extending duty exemption 
on scrap imports.
Duty exemption on ferrous scrap was extended 
to March 2028.
Space and 
Defence
CII sought extending exemptions to Tier 1 and 
Tier 2 contractors.
Customs duty exemption was extended to 
Tier 1 and Tier 2 contractors.
Income Computation 
and Disclosure 
Standards (ICDS)
CII recommended abolishing ICDS. A joint Ministry of Corporate Aﬀairs-Central Board 
of Direct taxes committee was proposed to 
integrate ICDS into Indian Accounting Standards.
Battery Capital 
Goods
CII recommended duty exemption on battery 
manufacturing capital goods.
Import duty exemption was granted for 
speciﬁed battery capital goods.
Re-Imports and 
Couriers
CII suggested easing re-import and 
reverse-logistics rules.
Re-import procedures were simpliﬁed and 
courier export limits relaxed.
Advance Rulings CII suggested extending advance ruling validity 
to ﬁve years.
Advance ruling validity was extended from 
three to ﬁve years.
Duty Deferment CII recommended extending duty deferment 
for Authorised Economic Entity-T1 entities.
Duty deferment was extended from 
15 to 30 days.
Annual Report 2025-26 27
Annual Report 2025-2628
EASE OF DOING
BUSINESS
Enhancing ease of doing business (EoDB), one of the 
key priorities of the Government, was advanced under 
the aegis of the CII Task Force on Ease of Doing 
Business. CII focused on collaborative eﬀorts with 
Government authorities, including Department for 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), NITI 
Aayog, Cabinet Secretariat, Ministry of Law & Justice 
and several states to facilitate an enabling business 
environment.
ADVOCACY
• Aligned with the reform agenda announced in the 
Union Budget 2025–26, CII engaged with the 
High-Level Committee on Non-Financial 
Regulatory Reforms constituted under NITI Aayog 
(for central ministries/departments) and inputs 
were given for the deregulation exercise led by 
Cabinet Secretariat (for state-level reforms) across 
ﬁve themes - land, labour, environment, 
construction permits and utilities
• Recommendations were made to streamline 
procedures, enhance predictability and improve 
implementation eﬃciency
• Suggestions were provided to ease procedural 
requirements and promote transparency in land 
acquisition and labour compliance frameworks
• Inputs were shared from the perspective of the 
World Bank’s B-READY survey, emphasising on 
improving judicial eﬃciency and commercial 
dispute resolution systems
• Structural reforms were proposed to reduce the 
fear of criminal liability for procedural lapses and 
promote trust-based governance.
These reform proposals were advanced through 
several platforms, including the Government–CII Task 
Force on EoDB, chaired by the Secretary, DPIIT, with 
representation from key line ministries, Industry 
leaders and experts. CII also submitted detailed 
recommendations on decriminalisation of business 
oﬀences, dispute resolution, minimising regulatory 
compliance burden and the need for implementation 
of the labour codes to the Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Commerce.
Several structural suggestions were either adopted or 
are under active consideration. Notably, the Ministry 
of Law & Justice and the e-Committee of the Supreme 
Court acknowledged CII’s recommendations on 
strengthening the National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG). 
The proposal for establishing a centralised oversight 
mechanism for tribunals in the form of a National 
Tribunal Commission also received policy attention.
ACTION 
Advancing Trade Facilitation
To strengthen trade facilitation advocacy, CII 
organised the CBIC–CII National Conference on 
Authorised Economic Operators (AEO) to deepen 
awareness and uptake of the AEO scheme, focusing 
on clarifying application, validation and accreditation 
processes, highlighting programme beneﬁts and 
sharing implementation experiences for eﬃcient and 
trusted trade practices.
Driving Regulatory Simpliﬁcation Dialogue
At CII IndiaEdge 2025, a high-level panel was 
convened to advance consensus on regulatory 
streamlining. The discussion reinforced the need for 
digital governance through single-window systems 
and stronger Centre–State coordination, contributing 
to CII’s broader advocacy on harmonised and 
technology-enabled reform implementation.
Annual Report 2025-26 29
GOVERANCE REFORMS
CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
AND REGULATORY AFFAIRS
The CII Corporate Governance and Regulatory Aﬀairs 
Council engaged with the Ministry of Corporate 
Aﬀairs (MCA), Securities and Exchange Board of India 
(SEBI), Competition Commission of India (CCI), 
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) and 
NITI Aayog to streamline and simplify the regulatory 
framework for ease of compliance by Industry.
ADVOCACY
• Detailed representations were made to the MCA 
to enhance ease of doing business and 
compliance, covering notice of meetings, postal 
ballot, Board’s report, buyback, registration of 
charges, unspent corporate social responsibility 
(CSR) timelines, directors retiring by rotation, audit 
committee approval for related party transactions, 
Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority 
Rules, directors’ remuneration in private 
companies and fast-track mergers. Discussions 
with MCA included additional National Company 
Law Tribunal and National Company Law 
Appellate Tribunal benches, creation of a common 
e-platform under IBBI, fast-track mergers and the 
Jan Vishwas Bill 2.0
• CII submitted consolidated inputs to SEBI on 
simplifying dematerialisation of securities, aspects 
of the Secretarial Compliance Report, etc. As a 
member of SEBI’s Industry Standards Forum (ISF), 
CII contributed to formulation of Industry 
standards on ‘Minimum Information to be Provided 
to the Audit Committee and Shareholders for 
Approval of Related Party Transactions’
• CII interacted with SEBI Chairman, to discuss 
corporate governance, regulatory impact assessment 
and investor protection. Submissions were made on 
listing obligations and disclosure requirements, issue 
of capital and disclosure requirements and Business 
Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR)
• CII engaged with IBBI and MCA by making 
representations to the Parliamentary Standing 
Committee on Finance, chaired by Shri Bhartruhari 
Mahtab, MP, during its review of the Insolvency and 
Bankruptcy Code. A representation was made to the 
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Commerce, 
chaired by Smt Dola Sen, MP, on ‘Doing Business in 
India: The Way Forward’, emphasising insolvency as 
a key factor in ease of doing and exiting business.
CII appeared before the Select Committee of Lok 
Sabha examining the IBC (Amendment) Bill, 2025, 
chaired by Shri Baijayant Panda, MP.
L - R: Zia Mody, Chairperson, Sub-Group on Regulatory Issues under the CII 
Corporate Governance and Regulatory Aﬀairs Council and Co-Founder & 
Managing Partner, AZB & Partners; Ravneet Kaur, Chairperson, CCI and 
Unnikrishnan AR, Chairman, CII Tamil Nadu State Council and Managing 
Director - Glass & Glass solutions, Saint-Gobain India Pvt Ltd at the CII 
Annual Conference on Competition Law and Practice in Mumbai
L-R: Sanjiv Bajaj, Past President, CII & Chairman, CII Corporate 
Governance Council & Chairman and Managing Director, Bajaj Finserv 
Ltd; Tuhin Kanta Pandey, Chairman, SEBI and Chandrajit Banerjee, 
Director General, CII launching the CII Publication on The Shared 
Responsibility of Building & Strengthening Trust at the 18th CII 
Corporate Governance Summit in Mumbai
ACTION
• CII curated the following publications to promote 
good governance and build trust among 
corporates:
 - The Shared Responsibility of Building and 
Strengthening Trust
 - Guidebook on Eﬀective Adoption and 
Governance of AI for Board Leaders
• Under the CII Governance Series, Industry experts 
deliberated on emerging corporate governance 
trends
• CII Corporate Governance Summit was organised 
to discuss regulatory and governance priorities
• The Annual Competition Law Conference was led 
by Smt Ravneet Kaur, Chairperson, CCI to discuss 
the new era of competition laws and merger 
control.
NATIONAL FOUNDATION 
FOR CORPORATE GOVER-
NANCE (NFCG) 
NFCG was set up by the MCA in partnership with CII 
and other institutions - Institute of Company 
Secretaries of India (ICSI), Institute of Chartered 
Accountants of India (ICAI), Institute of Cost 
Accountants of India (ICoAI), National Stock Exchange 
of India (NSE), Indian Institute of Corporate Aﬀairs 
(IICA) and selected 50 National Institutional Ranking 
Framework (NIRF) ranked institutes. The Foundation 
builds capacity of corporate professionals by 
conducting academic research and promoting 
voluntary adoption of corporate governance as the 
key to sustainable wealth creation. Since 2003, more 
than 425 programmes and 65 research projects have 
been conducted. In 2025, NFCG undertook 5 research 
projects and events.
JUDICIAL REFORMS
The CII Task Force on Judicial Reforms made 
submissions on Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) 
Bill, 2025. A representation was made before the 
Parliamentary Standing Committee on Commerce.
LEGAL SERVICES
The CII National Committee on Legal Services 
undertook policy advocacy on legal reforms. Eﬀorts 
were made to pave the way for a robust legal 
framework in the country. 
ACTION
A roundtable was organised on India-European Union 
(EU) contracts and key aspects of contract 
enforcement and institutional arbitration in India and 
the EU in association with Vienna Arbitration Law 
Centre (VIAC). Submission was made to MCA on the 
draft ‘Prevention of Corruption (Guidelines for 
Preventing Bribery of Public Servants by Persons 
Associated with Commercial Organisation) Rules 
2025’ under Section 9 of the Prevention of 
Corruption Act, 1988. Webinars titled ‘General 
Counsels’ Perspective to Navigating the Digital 
Personal Data Protection Act Framework’ and 
‘Changes in the Competition Act: An Impact on the 
Industry’ were also organised.
During the National Conference on Legal Services, 
discussions revolved around India’s legal landscape 
supporting businesses and economy.
L - R: Dr Manoj Kumar, Additional Secretary, Legislative Department, 
Ministry of Law & Justice; Justice Sanjay Karol; Dr Lalit Bhasin, 
Chairman, CII National Committee on Legal Services, Managing Partner, 
Bhasin & Co at the National Conference on Legal Services in New Delhi

pages.title: CII Annual Report 2025-26 (pages 31-37)
pages.description: CII Annual Report 2025-26 — theme: Accelerating Competitiveness: Globalisation, Inclusivity, Sustainability, Trust.
pages.text:
FINANCIAL REPORTING 
CII National Committee on Financial Reporting 
engaged with policymakers on a range of issues 
impacting Industry. This involved continuous 
dialogues with Ministry of Corporate Aﬀairs (MCA), 
National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA), 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), 
Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), 
Stock Exchanges and other regulatory bodies revolved 
around strengthening Financial Reporting ecosystem 
in the country.
ADVOCACY
During the year, CII engaged extensively with MCA, 
NFRA, SEBI, ICAI, International Financial Reporting 
Standards Foundation (IFRS Foundation) and global 
accounting bodies such as the Association of 
Chartered Certiﬁed Accountants (ACCA) and the 
Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and 
Wales (ICAEW) on corporate ﬁnancial reporting, 
regulatory streamlining and ease of doing business in 
ﬁnancial reporting.
Detailed representations were submitted on key 
regulatory issues, including establishment of Indian 
Multi-Disciplinary Partnership (MDP) ﬁrms, review of 
accounting standards and audit reforms as per 
provisions under the Companies Act. 
Key audit reforms addressed issues such as brand 
choices of accounting ﬁrms, global aﬃliations, 
multi-disciplinary practices, minority participation of 
non-Chartered Accountants in audit practices and 
enforcement/settlement mechanisms.
CII’s representation on SEBI’s digital assurance mandate 
led to a hold on implementation due to practical 
challenges for corporate auditee or auditor. 
Representations were also made to NFRA for adjusting 
one-time accounting impacts of labour codes. 
Other signiﬁcant policy engagements included Industry 
Standards Forum (ISF)-Business Responsibility and 
Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) core assessments, 
technical issues in online ﬁlings, guidelines for overseas 
networks, recognition of intangible assets and 
submissions to SEBI on Secretarial Compliance Reports, 
auditor appointments, related party transactions and 
requirements under Section 129A of the Companies 
Act relating to periodical ﬁnancial results.
ACTION
Deliberations at the Conference on Financial Reporting 
& Governance Framework focused on issues pertinent 
to Indian and global corporate reporting. The day-long 
conference deliberated on vital topics including 
ﬁnancial governance, building trust in ﬁnancial 
reporting, strengthening corporate communication, 
sustainability reporting and harnessing technology in 
strengthening reporting and governance.
An interactive session with NFRA was organised in New 
Delhi, followed by an intensive workshop for 
independent directors and audit committee members 
with senior NFRA oﬃcials. Various aspects were 
discussed in the sessions ‘Building Future Ready 
Organisations’ and ‘CFO 2.0: Driving Business Growth 
and Transformation’ held in Delhi and Mumbai.
L - R: Vidhu Sood, Secretary, NFRA; P Daniel, Full-Time Member, NFRA; Richard Rekhy, Vice Chairman, Grant Thornton Bharat; Nitin Gupta, Chairperson, 
NFRA; Smita Jhingran, Full-Time Member, NFRA and Sushil Kumar Jaiswal, Member, NFRA during the CII-NFRA Interactive Session in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26 31
Annual Report 2025-2632
PUBLIC POLICY
With the emergence of ‘geo-techno-politics’ and 
artiﬁcial intelligence (AI)-disrupting policy initiatives by 
the Government, CII diversiﬁed its leadership 
engagements with sector-wise policy advocacy for 
Parliamentarians. With India signing a record number 
of free trade agreements (FTAs) amidst unpredictable 
tariﬀ wars, CII’s brieﬁngs to Members of Parliament 
(MPs) and other public leaders helped formulate and 
implement strong policies for a Viksit Bharat.
ACTION
SECTOR-WISE ENGAGEMENTS WITH 
PARLIAMENTARIANS
CII facilitated multiple interactive sessions between 
Parliamentarians and Industry leaders, focusing on 
energy, skills, employment and livelihoods, women 
and child health. These sessions provided platforms 
for sharing information regarding each sector, future 
needs and policy reforms required. These 
engagements encouraged Industry leaders and MPs to 
work closely on policy reforms, with 68 MPs 
participating in the sector-wise engagements.
ONE-ON-ONE ENGAGEMENTS
WITH MPs
CII continued one-on-one engagements, interacting 
with 422 MPs. Through these engagements, CII 
undertook policy advocacy, highlighting sectoral issues 
aligned with the Standing Committees on which the 
MPs serve. These interactions also facilitated 
discussions on policy initiatives and reforms required 
for industrial development and for creating jobs and 
livelihoods in respective states and constituencies. 
STATE-WISE ENGAGEMENTS WITH 
PUBLIC LEADERS
CII interacted with 57 MPs from four states and the 
North-East region on policy reforms for industrial and 
economic development for their respective states and 
constituencies. This dialogue helped align regional 
economic priorities with Industry capabilities, 
supporting states’ economic ambitions through 
greater investment, job creation and stronger regional 
development. 
INTERNATIONAL ENGAGEMENTS
CII engaged with international Parliamentarians to 
deepen global policy dialogue and collaboration.
CII hosted a delegation comprising Brazilian 
Parliamentarians, Indian MPs and Members of 
Legislative Assembly (MLAs) to showcase India’s 
leadership in climate action and sustainable growth.
In addition, CII, in partnership with the Sasakawa 
Peace Foundation, organised a four-member Indian 
Parliamentarians’ delegation to Japan. Over the past 
two decades, this initiative has provided a global 
outlook to around 100 MPs and strengthened India’s 
partnership with Japan.
CII hosted a delegation of MPs from the North-East in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26 33
TAXATION
The CII National Committee on Taxation, along with its 
subcommittees on direct taxes, indirect taxes and tax 
dispute resolution, engaged actively with the 
Government and Industry stakeholders to support 
Member enterprises and address key taxation 
challenges faced by Industry. Several 
recommendations on critical issues were accepted by 
the Government, while many others are under 
consideration by policymakers.
ADVOCACY
Comprehensive proposals were submitted to the 
Government for the Pre-Budget Memorandum 
2026–27 on direct taxes promoting certainty, 
simplicity and growth, while removing disputes and 
bringing ease of paying taxes.
To ease compliance, promote fairness & consistency 
and reduce tax litigation, Central Board of Direct 
Taxes (CBDT) created three committees under Income 
Tax Systems and Faceless Scheme division. 
Representations were made and meetings held with 
the committees to resolve the systems and faceless 
scheme-related issues of Members.
Detailed presentations were made to the Select 
Committee of the Lok Sabha on the Income Tax Bill, 
2025, articulating Industry perspectives on legislative 
and procedural aspects. Representations were 
submitted to the Government suggesting 
interpretational clarity, transitional issues and 
alignment with existing jurisprudence.
Similarly, inputs were submitted for simpliﬁcation of 
Income Tax Rules and Forms, in order to align with the 
Income Tax Act, 2025, once the same was enacted. 
Suggestions were submitted for simpliﬁcation and 
rationalisation of Income Tax Return forms to improve 
taxpayer experience and compliance eﬃciency.
Interactions were held and proposals submitted on 
Transfer Pricing Safe Harbour Rules to reﬂect global 
best practices, including sector-speciﬁc and 
margin-related recommendations. Recommendations 
were also submitted on Organisation for Economic 
Co-operation and Development Base Erosion and 
Proﬁt Shifting (OECD BEPS) Pillar Two provisions, 
assessing implications for Indian Industry and global 
competitiveness.
Inputs were submitted to the Government on service 
delivery standards under the Taxpayers’ Charter, 
2020, emphasising accountability, transparency and 
timeliness. Representations were made on the Direct 
Tax Vivad Se Vishwas Scheme, 2024, suggesting 
measures to enhance eﬀectiveness of the scheme.
Following the Union Budget 2026-27, detailed inputs 
were sent, highlighting Industry concerns on issues 
arising out of Budget proposals on direct taxes for 
consideration in Finance Act, 2026.
As part of its reform agenda, CII recommended a 
strategic overhaul of India’s customs and indirect tax 
framework to enhance competitiveness and ease of 
doing business (EoDB). It proposed signiﬁcant 
measures to simplify tax structures, reduce compliance 
burdens, dispute resolution, promote domestic 
manufacturing and fully digitalise customs processes. 
CII GST 2.0 recommendations included rationalising 
GST rates into three slabs, bringing petroleum 
products under the GST framework, streamlining the 
Input Tax Credit (ITC) process and introducing uniﬁed 
audits.
Key proposals under customs included rationalising 
import tariﬀs into a three-tier structure – nil or 
minimal duty on raw materials, moderate on 
intermediates and higher on ﬁnished goods.
This phased approach aimed at maintaining the tax 
chain, reducing costs and simplifying compliance. 
Additionally, recommendations for the customs tariﬀ 
framework to be streamlined by consolidating 
exemption notiﬁcations into a single 
mega-notiﬁcation and expanding ‘Other Categories’ 
to eight-digit codes to minimise classiﬁcation disputes 
were given.
To address the backlog of legacy customs disputes, CII 
suggested introducing a one-time amnesty scheme 
allowing settlement upon payment of duty and nominal 
interest or penalty. Extending the validity of Advance 
Rulings from three to ﬁve years with renewal options 
was proposed to provide long-term tax certainty.
Digital transformation of the Indian Customs 
Electronic Data Interchange Gateway (ICEGATE) portal 
hrough Application Programming Interface 
(API)-based ﬁling and integration with licensed GST 
Suvidha Providers (GSPs) were recommended to 
reduce manual errors and improve eﬃciency. CII 
suggested allowing single appeals for multiple Bills of 
Entry involving common issues to further ease 
compliance. Automation between Customs and 
Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) for 
automatic release of bonds and guarantees upon 
Export Obligation Discharge Certiﬁcate (EODC) 
submission were also proposed.
During the year, interactive meetings were organised 
pan-India to gather support of states in the GST 
Council for recommending CII suggestions to move 
towards GST 2.0 reforms. The GST Council and the 
Government accepted CII suggestions on GST rate 
rationalisation majorly by bringing goods and services 
under 5% and 18% slabs, introducing speedy payment 
mechanism of refunds and easing GST registrations 
for small businesses. Daily needs products were 
placed under the 5% tax slab. These mega reforms 
simpliﬁed the GST rate structure along with the lower 
slabs, eased working capital to great extent and 
enhanced EoDB.
ACTION
Union Budget 2026-27 considered several CII 
recommendations submitted through tax proposals.
A ‘Post Budget Interactive Session 2026-27’ was held 
with senior oﬃcials of the Ministry of Finance. Senior 
oﬃcials of the CBDT and Central Board of Indirect 
Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Department of Revenue, 
Ministry of Finance highlighted the technical tax 
aspects of the Union Budget and mentioned that the 
Budget proposals were focused on certainty and 
reduced compliances to promote ease of paying taxes 
and economic growth.
L - R: Uday Pimprikar, Chairman, CII Core Group on Indirect Taxes, Tax Partner, EY India; Garima Pande, Partner, EY India; Piruz Khambatta, Chairman, CII 
National Committee on Taxation, Group Chairman, Rasna Pvt Ltd; Anupam Prakash, Joint Secretary (Customs), CBIC; Surjit Bhujabal, Member (Customs), 
CBIC; Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC; Prasenjit Singh, Member (Legislation), CBDT; Pitambar Das, Joint Secretary(TPL-II), CBDT; Pankaj Jindal, Joint 
Secretary (TPL-I),CBDT and Jainendra Singh Kandhari, Joint Secretary (TRU-I), CBIC at the Union Budget 2026-27 an Interactive Session with Ministry of 
Finance in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-2634
TECHNOLOGY
Technology, R&D and Innovation 
Telecom and Broadband 
Tamil Nadu Technology Development and Promotion Centre
Industry Academia Partnership 
Artiﬁcial Intelligence 
Space
Intellectual Property Rights
Technologies Enabling Waste to Worth Transformation
Centre for Digital Transformation
TECHNOLOGY, R&D
AND INNOVATION 
As India advances its mission toward Atmanirbhar 
Bharat, technology continues to open new pathways 
for national transformation. CII remains committed to 
shaping this journey fuelling innovation-led growth, 
cultivating talent and strengthening industrial 
capability. For over three decades, the CII National 
Committee on Technology, Research & Development 
(R&D) and Innovation has provided direction and 
momentum, ensuring India moves decisively toward 
global leadership in technology and innovation.
ADVOCACY
CII deepened its engagement with Government and 
research stakeholders to strengthen India’s innovation 
and R&D ecosystem. The evaluation of ‘Innovation 
Excellence Indicators of Public-Funded R&D 
Organisations – Round 2’, undertaken with the Oﬃce 
of the Principal Scientiﬁc Adviser to the Government of 
India, benchmarked nearly 250 public R&D laboratories 
across 25 ministries. The study assessed labs against 62 
indicators spanning socio-economic impact, scientiﬁc 
excellence and organisational capability. Insights 
generated through this eﬀort will support policy 
reforms to enhance performance and enable public 
research to deliver stronger national outcomes.
CII contributed structured policy inputs toward 
the INR 1 lakh crore Research, Development and 
Innovation (RDI) Fund, approved in July. 
Recommendations provided through the CII 
Committee on Technology shaped governance 
design, priority areas and collaborative delivery 
mechanisms for this ﬁrst-of-its-kind fund to 
catalyse private-sector R&D with Department of 
Science and Technology (DST) as the nodal 
ministry and Anusandhan National Research 
Foundation (ANRF) anchoring implementation.
Complementing these eﬀorts, CII advanced a 
national study supported by Department of 
Scientiﬁc and Industrial Research (DSIR) to 
strengthen industrial R&D ﬁnancing frameworks. 
Three high-level roundtables in New Delhi and 
Bengaluru engaged over 75 Industry and academic 
leaders and gathered insights from more than 300 
companies across sectors like manufacturing, 
energy, automotive, electronics and technology. 
These inputs will form actionable policy direction 
for expanding industrial research and innovation 
investment.
CII felicitated India’s leading innovative companies and research institutions at the Global Summit on Technology, R&D and Intellectual Property held 
in New Delhi

pages.title: CII Annual Report 2025-26 (pages 38-42)
pages.description: CII Annual Report 2025-26 — theme: Accelerating Competitiveness: Globalisation, Inclusivity, Sustainability, Trust.
pages.text:
ACTION
CII advanced initiatives to deploy technology, enable 
capability building and foster collaborative innovation. 
National discourse on genomics was strengthened 
through the CII Global Genomics Summit, which 
positioned genomics as a transformative multi-sector 
technology spanning healthcare, agriculture and 
biotechnology while highlighting opportunities in 
precision medicine, bioinformatics, regulation and 
talent development.
To support technology adoption and competitiveness 
in emerging domains, CII released a ﬂagship study on 
robotics, drones and automation during the 15th CII 
Global Technology, R&D and IP Summit. The report 
analysed adoption trends and ecosystem readiness, 
underscoring the role of automation in improving 
productivity, resilience and global competitiveness 
across industrial and strategic sectors. 
The same platform also hosted the Industrial 
Innovation Awards, recognising nearly 100 
organisations demonstrating excellence in products, 
processes and business model innovation. 
Strengthening inclusion within India’s innovation 
ecosystem, CII presented the Women in STEM Awards, 
conferring around 50 recognitions and launching a 
coﬀee-table publication ‘Organisations Empowering 
Women in STEM’, showcasing institutional models 
that are enabling gender diversity and leadership.
Culminating its initiatives, CII led the development of 
a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) Framework, 
endorsed by the Oﬃce of the Principal Scientiﬁc 
Adviser to the Government of India. The framework 
provides a structured approach to assessing the 
maturity of technologies, reinforcing the importance 
of Government–Industry–Academia convergence in 
accelerating innovation.
To foster global technology collaborations, CII 
expanded India’s innovation footprint internationally. 
The CII Annual Technology and IPR Mission to Japan 
connected Indian Industry with leading R&D 
institutions, opening avenues for joint research, 
technology transfer and IP cooperation. Building 
bilateral momentum, CII participated in the India–UK 
Summit, reinforcing collaboration on frontier 
technologies. Further strengthening international 
partnerships, CII, in collaboration with the Embassy of 
the Kingdom of the Netherlands and IIT Delhi, 
organised the Indo-Dutch Tech Summit, advancing 
cooperation in areas such as water management, 
clean hydrogen, bioeconomy, advanced materials and 
med-tech.
Together, these sustained advocacy and action eﬀorts 
reﬂect CII’s commitment to translating India’s 
technological aspirations into measurable outcomes 
shaping Government policy, enabling Industry 
adoption, empowering diverse talent, strengthening 
global linkages and advancing the nation’s journey 
toward a conﬁdent, innovation-led Viksit Bharat.
L - R: Vaishali Nigam Sinha, Chairperson, CII Women in STEM Initiatives and Co-Founder & Chairperson, Sustainability, ReNew; Dr Chandrika Kaushik, 
Distinguished Scientist & Director General, Production Coordination & Services Interaction, DRDO; Inge Buﬀolo, Director, EUIPO and Tito Kishan, Founder 
& CEO, Proinn Consultancy felicitating winners at the CII Women in STEM Awards
Annual Report 2025-2638
TELECOM AND
BROADBAND
Through its National Committee on Telecom and 
Broadband, CII drives structured 
Industry–Government engagement to address 
challenges across the telecom and digital ecosystem.
Aligned with the vision of the National Digital 
Communications Policy (NDCP), the Committee acts 
as a key interlocutor between Government and 
Industry to advance the ‘Connect India, Propel India 
and Secure India’ missions. Its work focuses on 
strengthening ease of doing business (EoDB), 
promoting domestic telecom and digital 
manufacturing, enhancing digital connectivity and 
embedding cybersecurity and artiﬁcial intelligence (AI) 
risk mitigation frameworks to ensure a secure and 
future-ready digital backbone.
ADVOCACY
The Committee actively engaged with stakeholders on 
regulatory consultations for the telecom sector. Key 
submissions and engagements included:
• National Telecom Policy (NTP), 2025: 
Recommended accelerating tower ﬁberisation by 
enforcing Right of Way (RoW) Rules (uniform 
charges, faster approvals via portals) and 
supporting rollout through Digital Bharat Nidhi and 
Universal Service Obligation (USO)-backed 
schemes, alongside levy rationalisation and 
litigation amnesty to improve sector viability to the 
Department of Telecommunications (DoT)
• Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) 
Pre-Consultation Paper on Interconnection 
Regulations: Recommended modernising 
interconnection to reﬂect Internet Protocol 
(IP)-based networks and new traﬃc patterns, 
sought measures to curb spam/scam traﬃc and 
ensure fair, reciprocal interconnect terms including 
International Termination Charges (ITC) review, etc
• Draft Telecommunications (Telecom Cyber 
Security) Amendment Rules, 2025: Suggested a 
risk-based cyber security compliance approach with 
clear roles and responsibilities, ﬂagged the need to 
avoid duplicative reporting and recommended 
enabling practical implementation for operators 
and supply chain
• Draft Telecommunications Rules (G.S.R. 606(E)) – 
Authorisation for Provision of Main 
Telecommunications: Provided suggestions on the 
notiﬁcation which included reforms under the 2025 
Telecom Authorisation Rules, where it was 
requested that the reforms should not 
disadvantage existing licensees - any EoDB or scope 
or fee relaxations must be extended to current 
operators as well, to ensure a level playing ﬁeld
• TRAI Consultation Paper on Review of Tariﬀ for 
Domestic Leased Circuits (DLCs): The submission 
reﬂected collective feedback from Industry 
stakeholders aimed at supporting a transparent, 
competitive and forward-looking tariﬀ framework 
aligned with current market developments.
Annual Report 2025-26 39
Annual Report 2025-2640
TAMIL NADU TECHNOLOGY
DEVELOPMENT AND
PROMOTION CENTRE
The Tamil Nadu Technology Development and 
Promotion Centre (TNTDPC) anchored CII’s technology 
agenda in Tamil Nadu and the southern region by 
promoting emerging technologies, building digital 
capabilities and enhancing artiﬁcial intelligence (AI) 
readiness. The Centre focused on enabling micro, small 
and medium enterprises (MSMEs), manufacturing units 
and automotive players to become digitally resilient, 
sustainable and globally competitive.
ACTION
TNTDPC delivered a portfolio of capacity-building 
programmes designed to equip business leaders with 
future-ready skills. Notable interventions included 
virtual training programmes and workshops on 
generative AI and Retrieval Augmented Generation 
(RAG), Internet of Things (IoT) integrated with GenAI 
and AI lifecycle governance. These initiatives 
facilitated the application of intelligent automation, 
predictive analytics, responsible AI frameworks and 
strategic digital roadmaps.
To provide immersive exposure to global best 
practices, TNTDPC organised learning missions to 
benchmark manufacturing facilities, providing direct 
exposure to smart manufacturing systems, digital 
twins, advanced automation and Industry 4.0 
deployment while strengthening peer benchmarking 
and knowledge transfer.
On the thought leadership front, TNTDPC convened 
sectoral conferences that promoted the adoption of 
advanced technologies. The Conference on Industrial 
Metaverse showcased simulation-driven 
transformation through digital twins, extended reality, 
AI and advanced simulation tools. The Conference on 
Emerging Technologies, underlined digital resilience, 
cybersecurity and agile organisational capabilities. The 
second edition of the AI-Powered Summit served as a 
platform to explore responsible AI deployment across 
supply chains, sustainable manufacturing, digital 
commerce and workforce transformation.
TNTDPC advanced Tamil Nadu’s aspiration to become 
a future-ready, low-carbon mobility hub through the 
Conference on Automotive R&D Trends and the fourth 
edition of the EV Summit. These initiatives addressed 
digital innovation in automotive research & 
development (R&D) and scalable electric mobility 
ecosystems. The Conference on Building a Resilient 
Rare Earth Elements Supply Chain Through Technology 
Localisation reinforced India’s focus on secure, 
localised critical mineral capabilities.
The Centre’s two key forums – the CTO Forum and the 
IP Forum – served as platforms for sustained 
engagement and knowledge exchange. The CTO 
Forum advanced the adoption of emerging 
technologies through discussions, learning missions 
and workshops, while the IP Forum brought together 
senior professionals to deliberate on critical intellectual 
property issues and evolving strategies. Strengthening 
its role as a thought leadership platform, the IP Forum 
also hosted the Digital IP Summit, which explored 
commercialisation, data-driven IP and global innovation 
frameworks in the digital era. TNTDPC facilitated 
Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) ﬁlings and 
prosecution of 65 matters including four Industrial 
Designs, 35 Indian Trademarks, 15 Indian Patents and 
11 International Patents. Among 11 International 
Patents, two International Patent grants were received 
from Japan and the United States.
Through this integrated approach, TNTDPC strengthened 
Tamil Nadu’s position as a leading hub for responsible 
digital innovation, Industry 4.0 adoption, sustainable 
mobility and technology-enabled industrial growth.
Dr Suresh D, Summit Chairman and CEO & Group CTO, Spark Minda 
Technical Centre, Minda Corporation Ltd and Dr T Prabhushankar, Managing 
Director, Metropolitan Transport Corporation Ltd at the 4th edition of the 
CII-TNTDPC EV Summit in Chennai
Annual Report 2025-26 41
L-R: Vaishali Nigam Sinha, Chairperson, CII Women in STEM Initiatives and Co-Founder & Chairperson, Sustainability, ReNew; Dr Jitendra Singh, Minister of 
State (I/C) of Science and Technology and Earth Sciences and Minister of State, Prime Minister’s Oﬃce; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Space and 
Atomic Energy; Dilip Sawhney, Managing Director, Rockwell Automation; Prof V Ramgopal Rao, Vice-Chairman, CII Industry Academia Partnership and Group 
Vice-Chancellor, Birla Institute of Technology & Science releasing the CII Industry-Academia Partnership Compendium at the Global Summit on Industry 
Academia Partnership in New Delhi
INDUSTRY–ACADEMIA
PARTNERSHIP 
The CII Industry–Academia Partnership (CII-IAP) 
reﬂects CII’s long-standing commitment to 
strengthening collaboration between Industry, 
Academia, Government and the innovation ecosystem 
to drive research-led growth. Aligned with Viksit 
Bharat@2047, the initiative focused on enabling 
translational research, deep-tech innovation and 
technology commercialisation through structured, 
outcome-oriented engagement. The Partnership 
sought to move beyond fragmented interactions 
towards institutionalised models that convert research 
excellence into deployable, Industry-ready solutions.
ADVOCACY
Key advocacy priorities included addressing 
information asymmetry between Industry and 
Academia, enabling clearer articulation of Industry 
problem statements and aligning academic research 
agendas with national and industrial priorities. CII 
advocated the creation of joint research platforms, 
shared R&D infrastructure and Industry-aligned 
doctoral and talent development pathways to build a 
sustained pipeline of skilled researchers and 
innovators.
ACTION 
CII operationalised its advocacy agenda through a set of 
ﬂagship initiatives aimed at strengthening collaboration 
outcomes and global engagement.
To deepen international collaboration, CII led a Global 
Industry–Academia Partnership Mission to the United 
Kingdom, comprising senior representatives from 
Industry, Academia and ed-tech organisations.
Deliberations at inaugural edition of the CII Global Summit 
on Industry–Academia Partnership focused on aligning 
Industry challenges with academic research, establishing 
joint research programmes, strengthening IP and 
technology transfer frameworks and accelerating 
commercialisation through Industry-led pilots and scale-up 
pathways. The Summit reinforced the shift towards 
scalable, institutionalised co-creation models.
An Innovation and Technology Exhibition, held alongside the 
Summit, showcased India’s growing capability in translating 
research excellence into deployable solutions. As part of its 
action agenda, CII also organised the 2nd edition of the CII 
Industry–Academia Partnership Awards, recognising 60 
outstanding collaborations across 10 categories.
Annual Report 2025-2642
ARTIFICIAL
INTELLIGENCE
The CII Centre for Artiﬁcial Intelligence (AI) along with 
CII National AI Forum drove continuous improvement 
in Indian Industry by promoting adoption of AI, 
fostering innovation and enabling responsible 
regulation, focusing on:
• AI adoption and capacity building
• AI regulation and leadership development
• AI innovation.
ADVOCACY
The session ‘AI for Viksit Bharat’ served as a strategic 
dialogue aligning national AI ambitions with 
implementation pathways. Discussions focused on 
scalable data infrastructure, workforce readiness and 
cross-sector collaboration. Key policy 
recommendations included:
• Establishment of a high-level Centre–State 
coordination mechanism anchored by a National AI 
Apex Council
• Introduction of AI regulatory sandboxes for 
sectors such as banking, ﬁnancial services and 
insurance (BFSI), agriculture and health
• Development of an AI maturity certiﬁcation 
framework for micro, small and medium 
enterprises (MSMEs) linked with Government 
procurement incentives
• Expansion of AIKosh, open-source Indian language 
models and sustainable data centre capacity to 
strengthen national AI infrastructure.
ACTION
The CII National Forum on AI fostered collaboration 
between Industry, Academia, startups and 
policymakers through AI Awards, sectoral sessions, 
roundtables, B2B meetings and workshops. The 
second edition of the CII National AI Awards 
recognised 54 impactful AI implementations from 
over 120 nominations across solution innovation, 
Industry application and Industry–Academia 
collaboration. 
CII partnered with the Ministry of Electronics & 
Information Technology (MeitY) and the IndiaAI 
Mission at the India AI Impact Summit 2026, 
organising 20 sessions to bridge policy intent with 
L-R: Ipsita Dasgupta, Managing Director, HP India; Chandrajit Banerjee; Director General, CII; Sanjiv Puri, Immediate Past President, CII and CMD, ITC Ltd; 
Piyush Goyal, Minister of Commerce and Industry; Rajiv Memani, President, CII and Regional Managing Partner of EY Africa India Region, Chair – EY 
Growth Markets Council and R Mukundan, President Designate, CII and Managing Director & CEO, Tata Chemicals Ltd at the launch of CII Centre for AI 
during CII Annual Business Summit in New Delhi
