Annual Report 2025-26 43
L - R: Sandeep Gupta, Grand Jury – CII AI Awards & Managing Director Protiviti; Puneet Chandok, Chairman, CII National AI Forum, President, Microsoft 
India & South Asia; Abhishek Singh, then Additional Secretary and CEO, MeitY; Rajan Navani, Chairman, CII AI Awards and Managing Director Jetline 
Group and Prateek Garg, Chairman, CII Regional Committee(NR) on Startups and Founder & Managing Director, Progressive Infotech, releasing the report 
‘Vision AI: Trends and Strategic Insights’at the Global AI Summit in New Delhi
industrial execution. Key takeaways included ensuring 
trustworthy AI systems, creating national shared AI 
compute infrastructure, establishing regulatory 
sandboxes for responsible innovation, sustained 
investment in AI talent and promoting lightweight, 
India-centric AI models to enable aﬀordable and 
scalable adoption.
The Global AI Summit, organised in collaboration with 
MeitY, the IndiaAI Mission and Software Technology 
Parks of India (STPI), as a precursor to the India AI 
Impact Summit 2026, enabled strategic discussions on 
AI governance and sectoral adoption.
CII released the report ‘Vision AI: Trends and Strategic 
Insights’, highlighting perspectives on AI adoption and 
governance.
CAPACITY BUILDING
AI Immersion Weeks strengthened AI literacy and 
adoption across 21 cities, training over 10,000 MSMEs 
on AI fundamentals, generative AI applications and 
business implementation frameworks.
A Study Mission to Singapore was organised in 
collaboration with the National University of Singapore 
(NUS), which trained over 50 board members and 
business leaders on AI and governance. In partnership 
with IIT Bombay, the AI for Business Leadership 
programme equipped over 65 Industry leaders with 
strategic AI insights, while the AI for Finance Leaders 
programme with IIM Udaipur trained more than 20 senior 
ﬁnance professionals on AI-driven decision-making.
L- R: Tejpreet S Chopra, Co-Chair, CII National AI Forum and CEO, Industry.AI, BLP Group; Puneet Chandok; Dr Jasdeep Kaur Dhanoa, Dean & Professor, 
Indira Gandhi Delhi Technical University For Women; Harish Krishnan, Managing Director, Cisco Systems India and Prateek Garg at the Conference on 
Democratizing AI Resources for AI Growth and Social Good in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-2644
SPACE 
India’s space sector has seen remarkable growth over 
the past decade, driven by sustained eﬀorts of Indian 
Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and the 
expanding participation of Industry and startups.
CII works closely with ISRO, Indian National Space 
Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) and 
NewSpace India Limited (NSIL). Through its National 
Committee on Space, it actively advances the sector 
through policy advocacy, Industry development and 
international collaboration.
ADVOCACY
CII focused on three key policy areas - demand 
creation, strengthening space assets in defence and 
tax and regulatory reforms for advancing the space 
sector. The Committee formulated and submitted key 
policy recommendations to the Department of Space 
(DoS), IN-SPACe, Defence Space Agency (DSA) and the 
Ministry of Defence, as outlined below:
• Strengthening demand creation within the space 
sector
• Rationalising GST rate on parts of Launch Vehicles 
(LVs) and aligning India’s GST framework with the 
Indian Space Policy 2023 for LVs and Launch Services
• Strengthening Indian space ecosystem via demand 
creation, funding & cost optimisation, tax reforms 
& regulatory and supply chain
• Drafting guidelines for Space Situational 
Awareness and Space Safety & Security 
• Enhancing demand of space assets in defence 
applications and dedicating a chapter in the Defence 
Acquisition Procedure 2020 for space-defence systems.
ACTION
CII, in partnership with IN-SPACe, organised a conclave - 
‘Adoption of Space Applications across Businesses’ to 
accelerate the adoption of space technologies in key 
sectors including agriculture, food processing, banking, 
ﬁnancial services and insurance, logistics, energy and 
urban planning.
Further strengthening India’s global space leadership, 
CII, in collaboration with ISRO, IN-SPACe, NSIL and 
Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers, hosted the 
Space Conference 2025 to foster innovation, enhanced 
indigenous capabilities and advanced international 
collaboration. Key highlights included the felicitation of 
Indian astronauts-Group Captains Shubhanshu Shukla 
and Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair along with release of the 
CII Space Industry Directory and report ‘Propelling India 
into a New Era of Space and Innovation.’
Recognising the importance of global partnerships in the 
space sector, CII also led international space delegations 
to Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Focused roundtables were 
organised on topics like ‘EU–India Cooperation in the 
Space Security’ and ‘Building a Celestial Bridge between 
India and Denmark’, along with a session on ‘Exploring 
India–Japan Space Collaboration’ in partnership with 
Japan’s Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI).
L - R: Rohan Ganapathy, Co-Chairman, CII National Committee on Space and CEO and CTO, Bellatrix Aerospace; Peter Winther-Schmidt, Consul General and 
Head of Trade & Innovation, Embassy of Denmark, India; Grp Capt Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Astronaut, India; Grp Capt Shubhanshu Shukla, Astronaut, 
India; Dr V Narayanan, Secretary, DoS and Chairman, Space Commission; Air Marshal Tejinder Singh, AVSM VM, Air Oﬃcer Commanding-in-Chief, HQ 
Training Command, Indian Air Force; M Mohan, CMD, NSIL; Rajeev Jyoti, Director, IN-SPACe Technical and Apparao Mallavarapu, Chairman, CII National 
Committee on Space and CMD, Centum Electronics Ltd at the International Conference on Space in Bengaluru
Annual Report 2025-26 45
INTELLECTUAL
PROPERTY RIGHTS
To foster an Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) culture 
in the country, CII set up the National Committee on 
Intellectual Property (IP) 16 years ago. Recently, CII 
launched the ‘One Company at least One IP’ drive to 
encourage Members to invest in generating, 
protecting and monetising IP.
ADVOCACY
CII actively contributed to policy formulation and 
stakeholder dialogue on IP during the year. Annual 
statements and recommendations were submitted to 
the United States Trade Representative (USTR) to 
provide a holistic picture of India’s IPR ecosystem. Key 
advocacy eﬀorts included submission of Union Budget 
2026–27 recommendations, highlighting gaps in IP 
commercialisation, the need for incentives for 
international IP ﬁlings, facilitation of cross-border 
licensing, recognition of IP as acceptable collateral and 
enhanced promotion of Geographical Indications (GIs).
CII also released two thought leadership reports 
addressing emerging and strategic IP themes. These 
included ‘CII–TCS: Artiﬁcial Intelligence and Intellectual 
Property’, examining IP challenges in the Artiﬁcial 
Intelligence landscape and ‘CII–Qualcomm: A 
Comprehensive Report on Indian Deep-Tech Startup IP 
Ecosystem’, providing data-driven insights into IP 
creation and management by Indian deep-tech startups.
CII supported international cooperation and 
knowledge exchange through joint initiatives with 
global IP organisations, strengthening awareness of 
international IP frameworks and best practices among 
Indian stakeholders.
ACTION 
CII organised ﬂagship events, training programmes 
and international engagements to build IP capacity 
and strengthen global linkages. Winners of the 11th 
edition of the CII Industrial IP Awards were felicitated 
at the CII Global Summit on Technology, R&D and IP in 
December that brought together Industry leaders, 
policymakers, researchers and IP professionals. This 
edition marked a signiﬁcant milestone, with more 
than 30 key parameters used to evaluate IP portfolios 
across patents, trademarks and industrial designs. The 
Industrial IP Awards recognised 50 outstanding 
organisations for exemplary contributions to a strong 
IP-driven culture in India, setting benchmarks for 
excellence in innovation and IP management.
Building on this legacy, CII introduced a dedicated 
‘Law Firms’ category under the CII Industrial IP Awards 
to recognise law ﬁrms demonstrating outstanding 
performance in Intellectual Property and their role in 
strengthening India’s IP-driven economy.
L - R: Masood Mallik, Managing Director & Group CEO, Re Sustainability Ltd; Lekhan Thakkar, Joint Secretary, National Security Council Secretariat (NSCS), 
Government of India; Debjani Ghosh, Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog; Dr Naushad Forbes, Co-Chairperson, Forbes Marshall; Vaishali Nigam Sinha, Chairperson, CII 
Women in STEM Initiatives and Co-Founder & Chairperson, Sustainability, ReNew and Ramesh Rao, Senior Director, Qualcomm at the CII Global Summit on 
Technology, R&D and IP in New Delhi
World Intellectual Property Day was observed through 
the CII Global Innovation & Intellectual Property 
Summit in April, reinforcing the role of IP in driving 
inclusive and sustainable growth.
INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY 
FACILITATION CENTRES
CII’s Intellectual Property Facilitation Centres (IPFCs) 
delivered end-to-end IP services and GI promotion in 
partnership with Central and State Governments. To 
date, CII has catered to more than 6000 IP matters, 
including support for ﬁling over 887 patents (India and 
abroad), approximately 2100 trademarks, 2257 
industrial designs and 387 copyrights.
Under the One-District–One-Product framework, CII 
strengthened its GI Tourism movement by facilitating 
GI tagging for more than 57 products while work is 
ongoing with 21 additional products. In collaboration 
with the World Intellectual Property Organisation 
(WIPO), CII is conducting a research-cum-survey to 
assess the socio-economic impact of non-agricultural 
GI products on the Indian economy.
Ambaji Marble, a GI product facilitated by CII, received 
a national GI certiﬁcation award, highlighting the 
tangible impact of sustained GI promotion and 
stakeholder engagement.
CII remained committed to promoting diversity and 
inclusion within India’s Intellectual Property 
ecosystem by recognising exceptional women in IP.
By celebrating women inventors, innovators, legal 
professionals and entrepreneurs, CII aimed at 
enhancing visibility, inspiring future talent and 
reinforcing the vital role of women in building a 
strong and inclusive IP-driven economy. This initiative 
was supported by the launch of the ‘Women in IP 
Compendium – Driving India’s Knowledge-Powered 
Economy’, highlighting women’s contribution to 
India’s IP ecosystem.
In partnership with the European Union Intellectual 
Property Oﬃce (EU-IPO), CII conducted ‘Invest in Your 
Future: An Intellectual Property Masterclass for Indian 
Entrepreneurs Expanding into Europe’. The 
masterclass provided practical guidance on protecting 
and commercialising IP in European markets.
CII led the Annual Technology & IP Mission to Japan in 
September, facilitating collaboration on technology 
development, research partnerships and IP best 
practices. 
During the year, CII conducted Value IPR 3.0, the third 
edition of the professional course on IP valuation and 
licensing, with participation from 25 professionals 
across Industry and advisory roles.
Felicitation of the CII Industrial Intellectual Property Awardees
Annual Report 2025-2646
CII’s Waste to Worth Movement reﬂects its strong 
commitment to advancing circularity across the Industry. 
The initiative supports organisations in managing and 
reducing the environmental impact of their operations 
by promoting technologies that enable waste-to-worth 
transformation. Through this movement, CII facilitates 
collaboration among Industry, Government and other 
stakeholders to develop and implement strategies that 
contribute to a sustainable future.
ADVOCACY
CII submitted recommendations to 10 ministries 
covering 16 waste streams to strengthen India’s waste 
ecosystem. Inputs were also provided for the Union 
Budget 2026–27, highlighting stakeholder challenges 
and proposing measures to enhance the national 
waste management framework.
CII released the National Circular Economy Framework 
(NCEF) - Edition Three, expanding coverage to 20 
priority materials. The framework deﬁnes clear 
milestones, targets and timelines focused on 
implementation, measurable outcomes and 
accountability to operationalise circularity at scale.
ACTION 
The 10th International Conference on Waste to Worth 
Technologies brought together Government, Industry 
and Academia to deliberate on the role of technology, 
policy and public–private partnerships in sustainable 
development.
At the 6th CII 4R Awards, nearly 50 organisations were 
recognised for leadership in ‘Reduce, Reuse, Recycle 
and Repair’. The Awards received over 80 applications, 
with 27 winners selected across six categories and top 
25 industries recognised nationwide. A new CII Young 
4R Award was launched to encourage young 
innovators. A ‘Compendium of Best Practices’ 
showcasing innovative and scalable waste-to-worth 
models was also released.
On World Environment Day, CII hosted its ﬁrst 
Symposium on Technologies Enabling Waste to Worth 
Transformation, featuring discussions on circular 
solutions across waste streams including plastics, 
e-waste, batteries, municipal waste, textiles, scrap 
metal, liquid waste, solar panels, tyres, gypsum and 
end-of-life vehicles.
The Second Annual Mission on Waste to Worth 
Technologies to Singapore engaged 20 delegates with 
leading companies, technology providers, incineration 
facilities and the Indian High Commission to explore 
bilateral collaboration.
CII also launched ProWISE (Professional Certiﬁcation 
on Waste Innovation for Sustainable Economy), a 
professional development programme delivered by 
global faculty to build advanced capabilities in waste 
management, resource eﬃciency and sustainable 
innovation.
TECHNOLOGIES ENABLING
WASTE TO WORTH
TRANSFORMATION
CII 4R (Reduce-Reuse-Recycle-Repair) Awardees felicitated at CII 10th International Conference on Waste to Worth Technologies in New Delhi

pages.text:
Annual Report 2025-2648
The Centre for Digital Transformation (CDT) drives the 
holistic digital evolution of India Inc by enabling 
structured digital adoption, strengthening 
cybersecurity, data governance and promoting 
leadership excellence. Through targeted training 
programmes, Industry engagements and recognition 
platforms, CDT supports organisations in enhancing 
competitiveness and aligning digital transformation 
with national priorities.
ADVOCACY
CDT actively engaged with the Ministry of Electronics 
and Information Technology (MeitY) by submitting 
policy recommendations on key draft regulations, 
including:
• Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023: 
Recommended a transition period of at least 24 
months before ﬁnal enforcement to enable 
orderly implementation
• Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming 
Rules: Recommended designating one 
independent Judicial Member to the Authority
• Information Technology (IT) Rules, 2021: 
Recommended a clear, risk-based deﬁnition of 
synthetically generated information focused on 
deceptive or harmful AI-generated audio-visual 
content, with ﬂexible, technology-neutral 
disclosure (such as provenance or metadata) and 
feasible, phased compliance obligations aligned to 
the actors who publish or distribute content
• Mandatory In-Country Testing Requirements: 
Recommended avoiding mandatory in-country 
testing for consumer devices given current lab 
capacity constraints.
ACTION 
Following the operationalisation of the DPDP Act in 
November, CDT conducted a webinar and workshop 
to create awareness on compliance across data 
governance, consent management and cross-border 
data ﬂows. The deliberations included insights into 
the legal provisions, best practices and technological 
solutions necessary for eﬀective compliance and to 
navigate the evolving landscape of data privacy.
The Cybersecurity 360o Summit was organised with 
MeitY, Indian Computer Emergency Response Team 
(CERT-In), National Critical Information Infrastructure 
Protection Centre (NCIIPC), Society of Indian Defence 
Manufacturers (SIDM) and National Security Council 
Secretariat (NSCS), focusing on national cyber 
readiness, artiﬁcial intelligence (AI)-driven threats, 
zero-trust frameworks, quantum-safe technologies 
and secure multi-cloud operations.
Recognising excellence and scaling best practices, the 
DX Awards & DX Summit 2025 received 204 
nominations and recognised 75 organisations from 
multiple sectors for their innovative and scalable 
practices. The Compendium of Digital Transformation 
Best Practices was released to support Industry-wide 
capability building.
Further, the third edition of Chief Information Oﬃcer 
Awards recognised 60 leaders for their exceptional 
work and benchmark leadership excellence and digital 
innovation across enterprises. 
Supported by NITI Frontier Tech Hub and All India 
Council for Technical Education (AICTE), the Dx-EDGE 
initiative accelerated digital transformation of micro, 
small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) through 
Industry–Academia collaboration and emerging 
technology adoption, resulting in:
• 116 trained Digital Transformation Mentors
• 1056 trained Digital Transformation Fellows 
• Partnerships with State Governments
• MSME digital maturity assessments and sectoral 
roadmaps.

INDIA AND THE WORLD
India stands at a deﬁning inﬂection point, stepping 
conﬁdently into a new phase of economic 
transformation that is redeﬁning its role in the global 
order. As one of the fastest-growing major 
economies, India’s rise is measured by its capacity to 
lead in innovation, inclusivity, sustainability and global 
problem-solving. With a resilient domestic economy, 
forward-looking reforms and a strong digital and 
manufacturing backbone, India is emerging as a 
trusted partner and a key driver of global growth.
Indian Industry and CII remained engaged with the 
world, reinforcing India’s global integration. 
Throughout the year, CII convened and participated in 
high-impact international platforms, including the 
20th India-LAC Conclave, the 20th India-Africa 
Business Conclave, the 30th Partnership Summit and 
India’s engagement at the World Economic Forum 
Annual Meeting in Davos. These forums enabled 
meaningful dialogue, strengthened partnerships and 
positioned Indian Industry at the centre of global 
economic conversations.
CII’s international engagement played a catalytic role 
in connecting Indian enterprises with global 
opportunities. Through sustained outreach and 
structured platforms, CII supported Indian 
companies in building overseas networks, accessing 
new markets and forging strategic collaborations. 
The CII International Council acted as a vital bridge 
between Indian Industry and the global ecosystem, 
advocating Industry interests abroad, facilitating 
investment ﬂows and shaping India’s external 
economic interface.
AFRICA
CII, in cooperation with Embassy of Angola and 
Angola’s Agency for Private Investment and 
Promotion of Exports (AIPEX), organised the CII India 
Angola Business Forum during H.E. João Lourenço, 
President, Republic of Angola’s visit to India. 
Furthermore, with focused discussions covering 
diﬀerent tracks, the 20th CII India-Africa Business 
Conclave witnessed attendance of over 80 speakers 
and close to 2000 business delegates. Participation 
included over 35 senior Government dignitaries 
including the Vice President of Zimbabwe and 22 
Ministers from both Africa and India, reaﬃrming the 
conclave as the leading platform for G2B and B2B 
engagements between India and Africa.

(NSC) and dignitaries at Washington D.C.

NORTH AMERICA
Members of the CII India Business Forum, United 
States (US) convened for their Spring Meeting in 
Washington D.C., providing a platform for dialogue on 
India-US economic engagement. The meeting 
featured an interaction with Ricky Gill, the then 
Special Assistant to the President and Senior Director 
for South Asia at the National Security Council, White 
House and focused on strengthening collaboration 
between Indian Industry and US policymakers.
CII along with US-India Business Council (USIBC) 
hosted a Roundtable with Kim Reynolds, Governor of 
Iowa which underscored the growing momentum in 
US-India relations, particularly Iowa-India engagement, 
reﬂected in Iowa’s second trade mission to India and 
the continued implementation of the CII-Iowa 
Economic Development Authority Memorandum of 
Understanding (MoU). 
CII-USIBC also hosted a roundtable with Phil Murphy, the 
then Governor of New Jersey which highlighted New 
Jersey as a strategic gateway for India’s engagement 
with the US, underpinned by one of the largest Indian 
diaspora communities and a trade relationship 
exceeding USD 11 billion. The discussion emphasised 
opportunities in artiﬁcial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, 
ﬁntech, life sciences and advanced manufacturing.
An interaction with a US Congressional Delegation 
was organised to discuss resilience and friction points 
in the US-India economic relationship across trade, 
technology and energy. 
LATIN AMERICA & CARIBBEAN
The CII Latin America & Caribbean (LAC) Desk 
advanced India’s strategic economic engagement with 
the region. Engagements emphasised South-South 
cooperation, resilient and diversiﬁed supply chains, 
technology-led collaboration and shared growth 
priorities.
The 10th edition of the CII India-LAC Conclave brought 
together over 600 delegates from 23 LAC countries, 
including 15 Ministers, alongside senior Indian 
policymakers, State Governments, Industry leaders 
and think tanks. Organised in partnership with the 
Ministry of External Aﬀairs and the Ministry of 
Commerce and Industry, Government of India, the 
conclave reaﬃrmed political and business 
commitment to deepening bilateral cooperation.
The Chile-India Business Forum was held in New Delhi 
during the State Visit of H.E. Gabriel Boric, President of 
Chile (as on February 2026). A key outcome was the 
announcement of the commencement of negotiations 
for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement 
(CEPA), signalling a shared commitment to deeper 
market integration and long-term economic cooperation.
CII facilitated an interaction in New Delhi with H.E. 
Santiago Peña Palacios, President of Paraguay and a 
high-level ministerial delegation, focusing on Paraguay’s 
transformation into an investment-friendly economy. 
An interaction was also organised with H.E. Geraldo 
Alckmin, Vice President of Brazil and the Brazilian 
Minister of Health, bringing together select Indian 
Industry leaders in New Delhi.

The CII Core Group on Singapore concluded a visit to 
Singapore, reinforcing bilateral trade, investment and 
industrial collaboration. The delegation engaged with 
key Singaporean ministers, policymakers, Industry 
leaders and diplomats, discussing economic 
opportunities and key areas for expanding 
collaboration.

Shanmugaratnam; Prime Minister Lawrence Wong;

Shanmugam; Minister for Transport Chee Hong Tat;

Wong, where he highlighted the importance of India

supporting the early conclusion of the ASEAN-India 
Trade in Goods Agreement (AITIGA) Review.

Philippines, was co-hosted by the Philippine-Japan

CEOs and members of IJBLF, marking an important 
milestone in advancing the India-Japan Special 
Strategic and Global Partnership.
CII in partnership with the Mongolian National 
Chamber of Commerce and Industry (MNCII) and the 
Embassy of Mongolia in India, organised the 
India-Mongolia Business Forum which brought 
together senior Government oﬃcials, business leaders

avenues for enhancing bilateral trade, investment and

business delegations, accompanied Shri Piyush Goyal to 
Sweden and France.

Harini Amarasuriya, Prime Minister of Sri Lanka which 
focused on advancing India-Sri Lanka cooperation in

meeting, the CII leadership had an exclusive

CII coordinated a high-powered Indian Industry 
delegation to the United Kingdom (UK), coinciding 
with the visit of Shri Narendra Modi to the UK. The 
delegation, led by Sunil Bharti Mittal, Past President, 
CII and Founder & Chairman, Bharti Enterprises 
Limited, comprised 16 captains of Indian Industry 
representing a variety of sectors and business 
interests in the UK.
The engagements began with the India-Oman 
Business Dialogue, jointly organised by CII, the 
Embassy of India in Muscat and the Oman Chamber 
of Commerce and Industry (OCCI) that provided a 
focused platform for Indian and Omani businesses to 
interact through sector-speciﬁc B2B and B2G 
meetings. Key sectors covered included 
manufacturing, services, healthcare, chemicals and 
energy, information and communication technology, 
agri-tech and power. As part of the visit, an MoU was

institutional cooperation.

for Business and Trade and President of the Board of 
Trade, Government of the UK signed a 
Comprehensive Economic Trade Agreement (CETA).

Shri Narendra Modi and H.E. The Rt Hon Sir Keir 
Starmer, Hon’ble Prime Minister of the United 
Kingdom. Dr S Jaishankar, Minister of External Aﬀairs,

Chancellor of the Exchequer, Government of the UK; 
The Rt Hon Wes Streeting MP, Secretary of State for 
Health and Social Care, Government of the UK were 
also in attendance.

ministerial and business delegation, the Rt Hon Sir 
Keir Starmer undertook his ﬁrst oﬃcial visit to India 
accompanied by Rt Hon Peter Kyle MP, Secretary of 
State for Business and Trade and President of the 
Board of Trade; the Rt Hon Douglas Alexander MP, 
Secretary of State for Scotland; Lord Stockwood, 
Minister of State (Minister for Investment). CII served 
as the lead Industry partner, facilitating a series of 
high-level business interactions, including the 
India-UK CEOs Forum.

CII PARTNERSHIP SUMMIT 2025
The 30th edition of the CII Partnership Summit, 
organised by CII in collaboration with the Government 
of Andhra Pradesh and the Ministry of Commerce and 
Industry in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh 
reaﬃrmed India’s growing inﬂuence in shaping global 
economic discourse.
The summit hosted 46 sessions, facilitated over 1500 
B2B meetings and welcomed over 3000 delegates, 
including 600 international participants from 62 
countries. The presence of 20 overseas Ministers, 
global CEOs, policymakers and thought leaders 
underscored the summit’s stature as a premier 
platform for international dialogue. Several MoUs 
were signed, strategic reports launched and 
investment commitments worth INR 11 lakh crore 
(USD 132.5 billion) were announced for Andhra 
Pradesh, signalling a transformative moment for the 
state and the nation.
DAVOS 2026
For over four decades, CII has maintained a strong and 
consistent presence at the World Economic Forum 
(WEF) Annual Meeting in Davos, positioning India and 
India Inc as credible partners in the global economy. 
Aligned with the WEF 2026 theme, ‘A Spirit of 
Dialogue’, CII curated a comprehensive set of 
engagements under its campaign theme ‘Partner with 
India, Subscribe to the Future’.
This year marked one of India’s most substantive 
representations at Davos, with over 100 registered 
participants and more than 200 attendees overall, 
spanning Union and State Governments, Industry, 
startups, social enterprises, institutions and media. 
The central delegation was led by Shri Ashwini 
Vaishnaw, Minister of Railways, Information & 
Broadcasting and Electronics & Information 
Technology, Government of India; Shri Pralhad Joshi, 
Minister of Consumer Aﬀairs, Food & Public 
Distribution and New & Renewable Energy, 
Government of India; and Shri Kinjarapu Rammohan 
Naidu, Minister of Civil Aviation, Government of India. 
There was strong participation from Indian states, 
with Chief Ministers representing Andhra Pradesh, 
Maharashtra, Assam, Telangana, Madhya Pradesh and 
Jharkhand, alongside Deputy Chief Ministers and 
State Ministers from Gujarat and other states.
A major highlight of CII’s engagement was the 860 
sqm India Pavilion, jointly designed by CII and DPIIT, 
Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of 
India. The Pavilion served as a uniﬁed national 
showcase for India’s investment potential, functioning 
as a hub for structured interactions between global 
investors, policymakers and Indian Industry.
During the visit, Shri Piyush Goyal and The Rt Hon 
Jonathan Reynolds MP, the then Secretary of State 
for Business and Trade and President of the Board of 
Trade, Government of the UK signed a 
Comprehensive Economic Trade Agreement (CETA).

accompanied by Rt Hon Peter Kyle MP, Secretary of

MARKET FACILITATION
SERVICES
CII’s Market Facilitation Services (MFS) aims at 
strengthening India’s manufacturing ecosystem, 
furthering the interests of Indian Industry in 
overseas markets and attracting foreign 
investment by leveraging CII’s long-standing 
alliances and extensive networks with global 
Governments, businesses and associations by 
oﬀering targeted trade and investment facilitation 
services to build the ‘Global Indian Corporation’.
As a fee-based trade and investment consultancy 
service, MFS undertakes customised company-and 
product-speciﬁc projects focusing on 
export/import market assessments, sectoral 
analyses, market entry advisory, operational cost 
optimisation and potential partner/ buyer search 
for inbound as well as outbound companies.
ACTION
• The ‘CII MSME Export Helpdesk’, a query-and 
credit-based subscription platform oﬀering 
resolution for speciﬁc export-related queries to 
micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), 
including information on potential buyer 
connects in foreign markets was launched at 
the Annual Business Session 2025.
• Key projects, across sectors and geographies, were 
delivered for outbound and inbound companies:
 - India steel sector landscape assessment with 
product line diversiﬁcation and PLI opportunity 
identiﬁcation
 - Operational cost optimisation and go/no-go 
advisory for an Indian industrial goods 
manufacturer, alongside a sectoral diversiﬁcation 
study on the India Medical Devices market 
 - Import market assessments across APAC and 
Africa for the chemicals segment of a diversiﬁed 
public sector enterprise 
 - Import market assessments across Middle East and 
Africa for an engineering and capital goods 
manufacturer
 - Saudi Arabia import market analysis for an Indian 
LPG cylinder manufacturer
 - Electrical equipment export shipment analysis 
including identiﬁcation of Indian exporters to Africa 
 - Metals and auto sector analyses for Indonesia
 - Export market assessment and US market and 
sectoral analyses for a refrigeration equipment 
manufacturer
 - Identiﬁcation of potential buyers in 16 countries 
across North America, Europe, Oceania and Middle 
East for a packaged food products manufacturer
 - India market and sectoral analysis across key 
healthcare domains for a Japanese enterprise.

Mathur, Managing Director & CEO, Siemens Ltd; Dr Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME; R Mukundan, Vice 
President, CII and Managing Director & CEO of Tata Chemicals Ltd; Sunil Chordia, Chairman and Managing Director, Rajratan Global Wire Ltd and

INTERNATIONAL
TRADE POLICY
CII’s International Trade Policy Department (ITPD) 
supported Indian Industry through a combination of 
capacity-building programmes, policy research and 
practical knowledge tools aimed at enhancing trade 
readiness, competitiveness and regulatory compliance. 
CII actively organised stakeholder consultations with 
Industry on India’s ongoing and prospective Free Trade 
Agreement (FTA) negotiations with key economies, 
including the United States (US) and the United 
Kingdom (UK). In addition to country-speciﬁc 
consultations, thematic consultations were organised 
on emerging trade-related issues in both goods and 
services such as sustainability, critical minerals with a 
focus on rare earth elements (REEs), Government 
procurement, Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism 
(CBAM), digital trade, animation, visual eﬀects, gaming 
and comics (AVGC), Global Capability Centres (GCCs) 
and artiﬁcial intelligence (AI). These engagements 
facilitated consolidations of concerns, opportunities 
and recommendations in a structured manner.
Eight capacity-building workshops on FTAs and 
emerging trade issues were organised in Jaipur, 
Guwahati, Mumbai, Kolkata, Hyderabad and 
Bengaluru each and two in Delhi. CII along with 
amfori, also organised a workshop and conference on 
trade and sustainability which explored how evolving 
trade policies and modern FTAs are integrating green 
and responsible trade provisions.
Several reports and strategy papers were prepared 
and submitted to relevant stakeholders on key issues 
of interest to Industry, including a potential Bilateral 
Trade Agreement (BTA) with the US, the impact of 
reciprocal tariﬀs, REEs, CBAM and outward foreign 
direct investment (OFDI). In addition, a dedicated 
report on the Industry input on the European Union’s 
(EU) CBAM was submitted to the delegation of the EU 
in India.
CII, Japan External Trade Organisation (JETRO) and 
the Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry in India 
(JCCII) jointly launched a Japan-India Economic 
Security Cooperation report. The study examined 
India–Japan economic security relations with a focus 
on their strategic complementarities and shared 
vulnerabilities arising from economic dependence on 
certain countries, particularly in trade and technology.

INTERNATIONAL RESEARCH 
CII International Research undertook a comprehensive 
and methodical research initiative aimed at deepening 
the understanding of India’s evolving global economic 
partnerships. Through extensive data analysis, 
stakeholder consultations and sectoral assessments, 
CII International Research produced a series of 
in-depth research reports that examine India’s trade, 
investment and collaboration potential with key 
regions and partner countries. These publications 
include India and EU: Expanding Future Horizons, 
2025; India–Latin America & Caribbean: Advancing 
Economic Alliances for Collaborative Growth, 2025; 
Scaling New Heights in India–Peru Business Relations, 
2025; Advancing India–Norway Cooperation, 2025; 
India–Africa Momentum: A Purpose-Driven 
Partnership; and Trade, Technology and 
Transformation: India–Europe Charting Newer Path 
Together.
Each of these reports encapsulates the trade and 
commerce landscape between India and the 
respective regions or countries. They analyse existing 
trade ﬂows, investment patterns and policy 
frameworks, while also identifying emerging trends 
that shape bilateral and multilateral economic 
engagement. Particular emphasis is placed on 
high-growth sectors such as technology, renewable 
energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture, 
healthcare and digital services.
Beyond presenting data and analysis, the reports 
highlight actionable insights into bilateral investment 
opportunities and outline strategic pathways for 
deeper cooperation. They explore potential areas of 
collaboration, including innovation partnerships, 
supply chain integration, sustainable development 
initiatives and knowledge exchange. By addressing 
both opportunities and challenges, the studies serve 
as practical reference documents for policymakers, 
businesses, investors and academic institutions.
Together, these research outputs reﬂect CII 
International Research’s continued eﬀort to support 
informed dialogue and strategic decision-making. 
They also contribute to strengthening India’s 
economic diplomacy by providing a clear, 
forward-looking perspective on how partnerships can 
advance inclusive growth, mutual beneﬁt and 
long-term economic resilience.

MULTINATIONAL COMPANIES
Under the aegis of its National Committee on 
Multinational Corporations (MNCs), CII worked 
towards fostering a stable, predictable and globally 
competitive investment climate for foreign 
multinational corporations in India. The committee 
serves as a cross-sectoral platform representing 
diverse industries and Focuses on structured policy 
engagement to strengthen investor conﬁdence, 
enhance foreign direct investment (FDI) inﬂows and 
deepen MNC integration into India’s growth trajectory.
Eﬀorts during the year were anchored around the 
following key strategic policy pillars:
• Ensuring a stable and predictable business 
environment through policy clarity and minimising 
abrupt regulatory or trade disruptions
• Deepening integration into global value chains 
(GVCs) by promoting export-oriented 
manufacturing and upstream value addition
• Enhancing FDI inﬂows with emphasis on sustaining 
long-term and quality capital ﬂows
• Improving the tax and regulatory regime to ensure 
certainty, transparency and global competitiveness
• Providing a thrust to digitisation to improve 
eﬃciency 
• Reducing regulatory compliance burden to enable 
scale, operational ﬂexibility and ease of expansion.
ADVOCACY
In consultation with its Members, CII developed a 
comprehensive research-based policy paper on 
revitalising FDI inﬂows, which was submitted to the 
Ministry of Finance. The paper assessed India’s recent 
FDI performance and outlined a structural reform 
roadmap to sustain and deepen foreign investment.
Key recommendations included revamping ease of 
doing business through greater tax certainty and 
streamlined land processes; modernising labour 
frameworks to enable scale; strengthening 
infrastructure through public–private partnerships; 
expanding and redesigning incentive schemes such as 
production-linked incentive (PLI) with calibrated 
localisation norms; promoting innovation, research & 
development and upstream GVC participation; 
developing a comprehensive GVC strategy; and 
strengthening free trade agreements with robust 
investment provisions.
ACTION
CII served as a member of a high-level Government 
Task Force on FDI reforms, co-led by the Secretaries of 
the Department of Economic Aﬀairs and Department 
for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). 
CII provided structured Industry inputs on improving 
policy predictability, addressing sectoral bottlenecks 
and enhancing India’s competitiveness as a long-term 
investment destination.
An interactive session with the Secretary, DPIIT, 
brought together select MNC leaders to discuss 
drivers of capital repatriation and strategies to attract 
sustained, export-oriented FDI. In addition, CII-MNC 
members participated in a focused virtual consultation 
with DPIIT to address visa-related issues aﬀecting 
FDI-linked technical personnel and operational ease.
The committee’s reform agenda was reinforced 
through a ﬂagship session, ‘Making India a Global 
Foreign Investment Magnet’, at CII IndiaEdge 2025. 
The discussion emphasised attracting long-term 
institutional and infrastructure-focused FDI, 
strengthening alignment between Industry and 
Government on positioning India as a preferred global 
investment hub.

EXIM
India continues to advance with a well deﬁned long-term 
vision of emerging as Viksit Bharat. Central to this 
aspiration is a robust and competitive export sector, 
which remains a key driver of economic expansion and 
global integration. In 2024-25, India achieved a record 
USD 825 billion in total goods and services exports, 
reﬂecting strong performance and resilience amid a 
challenging global environment. 2025-26 represented a 
signiﬁcant inﬂection point in India’s export ambitions.
Throughout the year, the EXIM Desk played an active and 
constructive role in policy advocacy, Industry– Government 
engagement and the development of actionable 
recommendations aimed at enhancing India’s trade readiness. 
Several representations were made to the appropriate 
authorities in the areas of extension of Interest 
Subvention Scheme, a dedicated scheme to help 
exporters access essential certiﬁcations and obtain 
ﬁnancing to meet these requirements and establishing 
an information portal to help Industry understand, 
anticipate and comply with emerging environmental, 
social and governance (ESG) norms.
In monthly meetings with Shri Piyush Goyal, Minister of 
Commerce and Industry, Government of India, CII 
presented key recommendations across tariﬀs, logistics, 
digital facilitation, ﬁnancing and branding which are 
areas critical for sustaining the momentum of India’s 
export growth.
A dedicated forum was established to deliberate on 
building resilient export logistics to strengthen trade 
and connectivity. It served as a platform for deep 
insights, strategic collaboration and practical 
recommendations aimed at enhancing India’s export 
growth and global competitiveness.
A key stakeholder platform was convened to focus on 
the strategic branding of India’s exports. The forum 
brought together Industry leaders, policymakers and 
subject experts to explore actionable strategies for 
elevating India’s global trade presence through 
stronger brand positioning and adherence to 
international quality and sustainability standards. 
Discussions also covered trade ﬁnancing and 
emphasised the need for transformative policies and 
strategic trade agreements to deepen India’s 
integration into global value chains.
The 5th CII National Exports Competitiveness Summit 
2026 brought in policymakers, Industry leaders, 
export-oriented businesses and global experts to 
identify actionable pathways for strengthening India’s 
export performance.
Several interactions with appropriate authorities were 
organised on important topics including tariﬀ and 
non-tariﬀ barriers, integration into global value 
chains, geopolitical developments and sectoral 
opportunities.

TRADE FAIRS
As the country’s largest trade fairs organiser for over 
ﬁve decades, with around 50 exhibitions, CII holds the 
largest portfolio ranging from automotive to 
engineering and technology, railways, artiﬁcial 
intelligence (AI), mining, space, construction, 
agriculture & food processing technology, gaming, 
healthcare and chemicals.
These platforms deliver large-scale exhibitions bringing 
together leading B2B brands for business connections, 
product showcase and dealmaking, facilitating 
face-to-face interactions between buyers and sellers to 
drive business growth and trade opportunities.

GLOBAL VALUE CHAINS
To support Government of India's ambition of 
enhancing participation in Global Value Chains (GVCs), 
CII’s specialised Task Force on GVCs, an apex body 
comprising prominent Industry leaders and domain 
experts, helped in advancing India's strategic 
integration while bolstering supply chain resilience. 
Throughout the year, the focus remained on 
pinpointing competitiveness drivers across key capital- 
and labour-intensive sectors to maximise value 
addition, exports and export-oriented foreign direct 
investment (FDI). Strategic alignment with the 
Government remained a cornerstone of the Task 
Force's activities.
ADVOCACY
During the year, CII’s advocacy on GVCs focused on 
the following key areas:
• Attracting diversiﬁed global investments and 
lead ﬁrms: CII engaged with the Department for 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) 
and relevant line ministries to leverage FDI inﬂows 
to enhance India’s participation in GVCs and 
attract lead ﬁrms to establish domestic 
manufacturing bases
• Strategic sector-speciﬁc research and 
deep-dive analysis: In-depth research served as 
the foundation for the Task Force’s expansion. 
Eﬀorts focused on four sectors - electronics, 
automotive, textiles & apparel and 
pharmaceuticals - to drive deliberations and build 
consensus. Building on foundational NITI Aayog 
reports, a disaggregated product-level analysis 
was initiated for the automotive sector. 
Additionally, a major study analysing capital 
equipment for electronics manufacturing was 
undertaken to provide strategies for self - 
reliance, GVCs integration and technology 
leadership. As recommended, several of these 
sectors received signiﬁcant policy impetus
• Monitoring trade and economic partnerships: 
Advocacy focused on navigating evolving 
geopolitical dynamics and supply chain 
restructuring through regular consultations 
between domain experts and Industry Members. 
CII completed studies on deepening GVC linkages 
of India with Korea and Japan
• Rationalisation of GVC Barriers: CII voiced Industry 
concerns regarding trade barriers, including the 
challenge of Quality Control Orders (QCOs) on raw 
materials and intermediate goods. This advocacy 
led to the successful removal of several restrictive 
orders. The Task Force also acted as a bridge to 
relevant ministries for tariﬀ rationalisation.
ACTION 
The GVC Task Force meeting was convened in a 
workshop format in August to analyse the inﬂuence of 
US-China policies. The session, featuring the Chief 
Economic Advisor to the Government of India, focused 
on shaping strategies for stronger backward and 
forward linkages and robust export-led growth. NITI 
Aayog provided critical inputs on strengthening India’s 
manufacturing role, particularly in electronics and 
automotive sectors.

Through targeted skill development and capacity- 
building programmes, CII-IL enhanced professional 
competencies across the logistics ecosystem. A total of 
6520 professionals completed specialised training and 
certiﬁcations, contributing to greater eﬃciency, 
competitiveness and institutional resilience.
INTERNATIONALISATION
CII-IL advanced internationalisation through initiatives 
such as the Indo–Japan Logistics Kaizen programmes, 
which introduced global best practices in eﬃciency 
and continuous improvement as well as joint 
international certiﬁcation programmes that provided 
globally recognised credentials. These eﬀorts 
strengthened cross border collaboration, aligned 
Indian logistics with international standards and 
enhanced global competitiveness.
ADVISORY SERVICES 
CII-IL delivered comprehensive advisory services 
including logistics consulting, supply chain maturity 
assessments and customised in-house programmes 
that enhanced eﬃciency and competitiveness. 
Forty-two organisations were supported through its 
supply chain maturity model framework.
CERTIFICATION
CII-IL oﬀered certiﬁcations such as Supply Chain 
Professional Certiﬁcation, SCM Data + AI Certiﬁcation 
and the Warehouses Excellence Rating (WAREX). 
Seven lakh sq ft of warehouse space was awarded the 
CII WAREX certiﬁcation, reﬂecting Industry excellence.
SECTORAL STUDIES AND PROJECTS
CII-IL undertook sectoral studies and projects that 
addressed logistics skill gaps, conducted regional 
logistics assessments and promoted green logistics 
initiatives. These provided actionable insights to 
strengthen capabilities, improved regional 
performance and drove sustainability across the 
logistics ecosystem.
The Indian logistics sector is projected to expand from 
USD 350 billion to USD 450 billion by 2030. As one of 
the top ﬁve employment-generating industries, 
freight logistics alone is expected to provide jobs to 
nearly 95 lakh people, while warehousing capacity 
across Grade A, B and C facilities is set to rise from 1 
billion sq ft to 1.2 billion sq ft by 2027.
The CII Institute of Logistics (CII-IL), a CII Centre of 
Excellence established in 2004, has been driving 
competitiveness and transformation in the logistics 
and supply chain domain. In 2025, CII-IL’s focus 
sharpened on innovation, artiﬁcial intelligence (AI) and 
robotics, next generation warehousing, workforce 
upskilling, sustainability-driven green logistics, 
gen-AI-enabled e-commerce and logistics kaizen & 
total cost management (TCM) for positioning the 
sector for future-ready excellence.
ACTION 
ENGAGING WITH GOVERNMENT
CII-IL facilitated a session with the Department for 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) 
oﬃcials on ‘Assessment of Logistics Cost in India’, 
providing valuable insights to understand logistics 
cost dynamics and identify eﬃciency opportunities.
The Centre organised a stakeholder consultation on 
the Telangana Logistics Policy 2.0 & Integrated 
Logistics Master Plan in collaboration with the 
Logistics Department, Government of Telangana. The 
session was chaired by the Commissioner of Industries 
and Vice President (Logistics), Government of 
Telangana, focusing on gathering structured 
feedback, Industry perspectives, global best practices 
and actionable inputs from key stakeholders across 
the logistics ecosystem.
EDUCATION, TRAINING AND SKILLS
CII-IL strengthened logistics education through academic 
partnerships and capability centres, enabling students to 
pursue Master’s and Certiﬁcate programmes. This

TCM AND TOTAL COST MATURITY 
MODEL
CII-IL's focus included expanding TCM via the Total 
Cost Maturity Model, a structured framework that 
supported over 250 organisations in aligning business 
strategies and improving operational eﬃciency.
EVENTS
Knowledge-sharing platforms impacted over 1200 
professionals through multiple events. Six 
conferences and summits were organised across India.
SCALE AWARDS 
The 12th edition of the Supply Chain and Logistics 
Excellence (SCALE) Awards recorded participation 
from 285 companies with 115 awards conferred 
across multiple Logistics Service Providers and User 
Company categories. The edition placed special focus 
on women leadership in logistics.
NEW INITIATIVES
Collaborative Logistics Advancement 
Network (CLAN)
CII-CLAN is an integrated platform designed for 
professionals within the logistics community to connect 
and collaborate, aiming at establishing a dynamic 
network of organisations committed to logistics 
excellence, facilitating collaborative learning and 
knowledge-sharing, empowering participants to drive 
improvements within their organisations and promoting 
the adoption of standardised methodologies to 
enhance regional logistics performance.
Supplier Rating Model 
The CII Supplier Rating Model aims to build world-class 
suppliers for India’s global value chains, promoting 
value innovation, supplier diversity and a shift from 
inside-out to outside-in evaluation. It ensures 
suppliers meet global standards in product quality, 
timely delivery, sustainability and ethical practices.
SECTORAL FORUMS
• Warehouse National Network (WNN), is a national 
movement that connected stakeholders across 
India’s warehousing Industry, focused on 
evolution, eﬃciency and empowerment, driving 
growth momentum and delivering tangible results 
in building world class warehousing enterprises
• Membership of Value Engagement (MOVE) is a 
knowledge-sharing platform that brought together 
stakeholders across the logistics and supply chain 
ecosystem, with emphasis on policy advocacy. With 
71 Members, MOVE addressed Industry challenges 
and fostered professional growth
• Women Logistics Leadership (WLL) highlighted the 
growing role of women in logistics and supply 
chain sectors, amplifying the ‘voice and wings’ of 
women professionals. WLL encouraged girl 
students through awareness, mentoring and 
career guidance to build future participation
• Academic Advisory Group (AAG) worked to 
modernise curricula, suggest new Industry relevant 
programmes and integrate case studies that 
broaden student perspectives. It enhanced CII-IL’s 
knowledge base through resources and global 
collaborations, while creating certiﬁcation pathways 
for professionals. These built a strong foundation 
for future talent and workforce development.

BUSINESS EXCELLENCE
Business Excellence played a catalytic role in shaping 
modern Indian Industry. By transitioning organisations 
from compliance-focused quality systems to 
integrated, performance-centric management 
models, it elevated leadership maturity, strategic 
coherence, customer focus and operational rigour.
Beyond operational gains in productivity, cost 
eﬃciency and quality, Business Excellence drove a 
cultural shift-embedding continuous improvement, 
OPERATIONAL EXCELLENCE
The Operational Excellence (OPEX) Department 
supported organisations in achieving superior 
performance across productivity, quality, cost, 
delivery, safety and morale. Through structured 
deployment of TPM, Lean, Six Sigma and continuous 
improvement frameworks, CII–IQ worked closely with 
leadership and shopﬂoor teams to institutionalise 
robust operating systems and enhance asset reliability.
Key outcomes included measurable improvements in 
process capability, waste elimination, equipment 
eﬀectiveness and cross-functional collaboration.

the organisational DNA. It strengthened resilience, 
governance and long-term value creation, positioning 
Indian enterprises as globally competitive and socially 
responsible institutions.
Impact
• Over 100 assessors trained based on European 
Foundation for Quality Management (EFQM) Model
• More than 25 recognitions 
• 25% - 40% cost reduction
• 20% enhancement in people satisfaction.
The CII Institute of Quality (CII–IQ), CII’s ﬁrst Centre of 
Excellence, has been at the forefront of advancing 
India’s quality and competitiveness movement for 25 
years. Working across manufacturing, services and the 
public sector, CII–IQ enables organisations to achieve 
measurable business results through structured 
interventions in Business Excellence, Total Productive 
Maintenance (TPM), Lean, Six Sigma, Operational 
Excellence and Quality Management Systems.
Last year, CII–IQ deepened Industry engagement 
through focused training programmes, assessments, 
consulting assignments, cluster initiatives and thought 
leadership platforms-helping organisations translate 
best practices into tangible performance improvements.

The OPEX Chennai Chapter was launched in December, 
marking an important step in strengthening the regional 
excellence ecosystem by providing a collaborative

integrated, enterprise-wide OPEX. Building on Chennai’s 
strong manufacturing base, the Chapter focused on 
advancing productivity, quality, cost, delivery, safety, 
sustainability and digital maturity through structured 
methodologies. The initiative aims to enable peer 
learning, capability building and best practice-sharing, 
positioning Chennai as a key hub for OPEX initiatives 
aligned with CII-IQ’s national framework.

TESIP provides insights into India’s Quality Infrastructure 
(QI) Framework, including standardisation, metrology,

The portal enables businesses to access sector-speciﬁc

DRIVING NATIONAL 
ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY REFORM
CII-CESD played a pivotal role in strengthening India’s 
environmental regulatory ecosystem. Through 
sustained collaboration with the Ministry of 
Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), 
Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Bureau of 
Indian Standards (BIS), Department for Promotion of 
Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), NITI Aayog, 
regulators and subnational Governments, CII-CESD 
advanced several high-impact policy reforms that 
enhance both environmental integrity and ease of 
doing business. Key contributions included:
• Rationalisation of greenbelt norms, enabling more 
eﬃcient land use while maintaining environmental 
safeguards
• Expansion of White Category exemptions, 
reducing compliance burdens for low-polluting 
industries
• Clariﬁcation of Environmental Clearance 
processes, improving predictability and 
accelerating project implementation
• Launch and functionality strengthening of the 
Uniﬁed Consent and Monitoring System (UCAMS) 
– a major step toward transparent, digital and 
streamlined environmental approvals
• Enhancements to India’s Extended Producer 
Responsibility (EPR) framework, including 
co-design of the CPCB Uniﬁed EPR Portal and 
reﬁnements improving credit utilisation and ease 
of compliance.
CII-CESD also provided inputs on Solid Waste 
Management Rules, new EPR frameworks for 
non-plastic materials and sector-speciﬁc challenges 
across diverse waste streams including plastics, 
e-waste, batteries, tyres, used oil, construction & 
demolition waste, biomedical waste and hazardous 
waste. These reforms support India’s shift toward a 
credible, harmonised and future-ready environmental 
governance landscape.
Importantly, CII-CESD’s engagement with NITI Aayog 
and Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) contributed to 
the development of national recycling policy guidance 
For over two decades, the CII Centre of Excellence for 
Sustainable Development (CII-CESD) has been a national 
catalyst for embedding sustainability into India’s growth 
model. Established before sustainability gained 
mainstream momentum, CII-CESD built many of India’s 
foundational frameworks on environmental governance, 
responsible business conduct, sustainable supply chains, 
circular economy pathways, climate resilience and ESG 
reporting. Across these years, CII-CESD has shaped the 
policies, partnerships and initiatives underpinning India’s 
transition toward green growth, industrial 
competitiveness and environmental stewardship.
This long-standing commitment was symbolically 
renewed with the launch of /uni0927Raa – the CII 
Sustainability Mascot, unveiled during CII-CESD’s 20th 
anniversary celebrations by Shri Bhupender Yadav, 
Minister of Environment, Forest & Climate Change. 
/uni0927Raa represents the essence of the Centre’s work: 
inspiring responsible manufacturers, mindful 
consumers and sustainability-conscious citizens. It 
symbolises CII-CESD’s evolution from a pioneering 
knowledge centre to a national movement-builder, 
carrying forward the 20 years into the next era of 
India’s sustainable development journey.
CII CENTRE OF
EXCELLENCE FOR
SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT

Sustainability Summit in New Delhi

and sustainability standards aligned with international 
benchmarks such as ISO/TC 323, ensuring India 
remains globally competitive as circularity becomes 
critical to international trade and responsible 
manufacturing norms.
ACCELERATING INDIA’S TRANSITION 
TO A CIRCULAR ECONOMY
Circularity remained central to CII-CESD’s work, and 
this year saw major progress in advancing business-led 
circular solutions. At the 2nd CII Circular Economy 
Conference, the Centre showcased a new publication, 
‘Circular Economy Practice in India’, highlighting 
scalable Industry initiatives that are embedding 
circular design, reverse logistics, recyclability and 
material recovery into mainstream business strategy.
Internationally, CII-CESD elevated India’s position at 
the World Circular Economy Forum 2025 in Brazil, 
organising an Accelerator Session to identify 
pathways and barriers for circular economy adoption 
across the Global South. These discussions shaped 
global thinking on how emerging economies can 
embed circularity while pursuing economic growth.
The CII India Plastics Pact catalysed market 
transformation by promoting recyclable packaging 
design, reducing virgin plastic use and expanding 
recycled content uptake. The ﬁrst CII Sustainable 
Plastic Packaging Awards recognised ten companies’ 
pioneering solutions that make plastic packaging 
more recyclable and circular. These business-led shifts 
signal a maturing ecosystem where circularity drives 
innovation, investment and behaviour change.
STRENGTHENING ESG GOVERNANCE 
AND ENABLING SUSTAINABLE 
FINANCE
As global investors prioritised sustainability-aligned 
growth, CII-CESD advanced India’s Environmental, 
Social and Governance (ESG) architecture. The CII 
National Mission on Sustainability (NMS) identiﬁed four 
national priorities: ESG governance, decarbonisation, 
nature-based resilience and circular economy practices. 
CII-CESD led eﬀorts across all four themes.
A landmark publication, ‘Assessing the Impact of ESG 
Standards Alignment on Sustainable Finance in India’, 
analysed the alignment between domestic Business 
Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) 
requirements and International Financial Reporting 
Standards (IFRS) S1 & S2 across 15 sectors, oﬀering 
clear insights into how Indian companies can improve 
disclosure quality and access sustainable ﬁnance.
To support policy reﬁnement, the India Sustainability 
Task Force (ISTF) engaged senior policymakers 
including the Chairperson of Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (SEBI) and MoEFCC leadership, 
providing actionable recommendations to strengthen 
BRSR and BRSR Core frameworks. This aligns India’s 
sustainability disclosures more closely with global 
investor expectations and improves the credibility of 
sustainability data.
CII-CESD also expanded its work with MSMEs and 
supply-chain companies, recognising that India’s 
sustainability transition must be inclusive. 23 MSME 
partners were awarded the Eco Edge Certiﬁcate for

commitment to building capacity and strengthening ESG 
adoption across India’s industrial base.
The roundtable on ‘Delivering Sustainability at Scale: 
Pathways for Global Transformation’ coincided with 
the World Economic Forum Annual Meeting 2026 in 
Davos in January. The session highlighted India’s 
economic rise; its sustainability roadmap and shared 
how it oﬀers strong returns on investment, with low 
NPAs, low inﬂation, rising production and rapidly 
improving infrastructure.
BUILDING CLIMATE RESILIENCE AND 
A LOW-CARBON INDUSTRIAL 
ECONOMY
As climate impacts intensify, CII-CESD deepened its 
work on climate resilience, risk assessments and 
decarbonisation.
Climate Risk, Adaptation & Resilience
The Centre strengthened the Physical Climate Risk 
Assessment Framework (PCRAF) through new pilot 
studies across districts and industrial sites. The Disaster 
Resilience Framework for Eluru, Andhra Pradesh and 
West Godavari districts provided actionable 
recommendations for improving disaster risk reduction 
using CII-CESD’s structured assessment methodology. 
Decarbonisation and Climate Finance
To accelerate India’s low-carbon transition, CII-CESD 
submitted recommendations on the draft India 
Climate Finance Taxonomy, a critical step in mobilising 
green capital. In partnership with the Industrial 
Transition Accelerator (ITA) and Boston Consulting 
Group, CII-CESD supported the expansion of India’s 
pipeline of bankable green projects. Phase I identiﬁed:
• Sixty high-impact projects across hard-to-abate 
sectors
• Representing USD 150 billion in investment 
potential
• With capacity to create over 2,00,000 jobs
• Abating 140–170 million tonnes of CO₂e.
These insights will inform strategic investments driving 
India’s industrial decarbonisation. CII-CESD also 
contributed to global climate dialogues, including 
engagements with COP30 leadership, positioning 
Indian businesses as partners in advancing global 
climate solutions.
PROMOTING NATURE-POSITIVE 
BUSINESS ACTION
CII-CESD strengthened its work on biodiversity 
conservation and nature-related risk management.
The conference ‘Action for Biodiversity Conservation: 
Investing in People & Planet’, organised with the 
International Big Cat Alliance, ampliﬁed the role of 
Industry in conservation. The report ‘Aligning BRSR and 
TNFD’ provided a practical roadmap for companies to 
integrate nature-related disclosures into corporate 
reporting, enhancing transparency and long-term risk 
management.
IMPROVING AIR QUALITY, PUBLIC 
HEALTH AND RURAL LIVELIHOODS
Air pollution remains one of India’s most signiﬁcant 
public health and environmental challenges. Through 
the Cleaner Air Better Life (CABL) initiative, CII-CESD 
delivered major cross-sector solutions focused on 
Industry, logistics, urban centres and agriculture. Key 
actions included:
• Promoting data-driven solutions for cleaner air in 
cities and industries
• Advancing ﬁnancing models for zero-emission 
logistics
• Supporting clean construction practices
• Facilitating Industry-wide action through the India 
CEO Forum for Clean Air.
A highlight of this year was the expansion of the CABL 
Crop Residue Management Programme, which reached:
• Two lakh farmers
• Across 1004 villages in Punjab and Haryana
• Preventing stubble burning on over 90% of 11 lakh 
acres of paddy ﬁelds. 
These interventions resulted in:
• Twenty two million kg of PM10 avoided
• Two-and-a-half million kg of black carbon reduced
• Two hundred and ﬁfty million m 3 of irrigation 
water saved.
CII-CESD’s mission for the next decade is clear: to drive 
systemic, scalable, measurable impact that supports 
India’s ambition to become a global model for 
sustainable, resilient and inclusive growth.

CII CENTRE OF
EXCELLENCE FOR
COMPETITIVENESS
FOR SMEs
The CII Centre of Excellence for Competitiveness for 
SMEs (CII-CFC) has emerged as a premier institution 
committed to driving excellence and competitiveness 
across Indian Industry, especially MSMEs. The Centre 
serves as a catalyst to help organisations adopt 
world-class practices, enhance operational eﬃciency 
and achieve sustainable growth.
ADVOCACY
CII-CFC supports Industry through consulting, advisory 
and training & development interventions across the 
following verticals: 
• Manufacturing excellence consulting: Lean 
implementation, Zero Defect Manufacturing and 
related initiatives through structured handholding 
and onsite visits
• Energy audits: Optimisation of power 
consumption, conducted by Bureau of Energy 
Eﬃciency-certiﬁed energy auditors
• Corrosion assessments and audits: Identiﬁcation 
and mitigation of corrosion-related risks and losses
• Continuing Education Programme: To upskill 
working professionals, the Centre runs the 
following focused programmes:
 - Postgraduate Professional Development 
Programme in Corrosion Management & 
Technology in association with IIT Ropar
 - Postgraduate Professional Development 
Programme in Manufacturing Excellence & 
Management in association with Thapar University
 - Postgraduate Professional Development 
Programme in Energy Management & Climate 
Action with Thapar University.
By oﬀering impact services, the Centre enables 
MSMEs and suppliers to: 
• facilitate robust supply chain integration with 
Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs); 
• reduce costs and improve proﬁtability through 
operational excellence and energy savings; 
ACTION
CII-CFC’s initiatives aim to strengthen cross-sectoral 
collaborations, showcase Indian competitiveness and 
engage with the international business community to 
beneﬁt businesses, economies and societies globally.
18th CII NATIONAL COMPETITIVENESS 
& CLUSTER SUMMIT
The CII National Competitiveness & Cluster Summit 
fosters collaboration and facilitates partnerships to drive 
India's manufacturing sector towards greater 
competitiveness. It serves as a platform for knowledge 
exchange, networking and collaboration, ultimately 
contributing to the growth and success of Indian 
industries in an increasingly competitive global market.
The 18th edition of the summit witnessed
• over 1000 Kaizens participating in Kaizen 
competitions
• more than 270 best case studies being presented
• over 500 Industry oﬃcials joining.
The Conference on Manufacturing Transformation for 
Excellence, an integral part of the Summit chaired by
Dr Tapan Sahoo, Executive Oﬃcer, Digital Enterprises, 
Information & Cyber Security, Maruti Suzuki India Ltd 
featured sessions focusing on automation & robotics, 
artiﬁcial intelligence (AI), machine learning and 
digitisation and supply chain optimisation.

CORTEM
Under the aegis of its Corrosion Management Division, 
CII organised the 2nd edition of the International 
Conference on Corrosion Technology & Management – 
CORTEM 2025 in Chennai. CORTEM 2025 was a 3-day

Aligned with India’s ambition to become a globally 
competitive manufacturing powerhouse, the CII 
Centre of Manufacturing Excellence (CII-CME) enables 
capability building, operational excellence and 
industrial transformation. Through a structured 
portfolio of technical training programmes, learning 
missions, safety initiatives, awards and youth 
engagement platforms, CII-CME supports 
organisations across sectors in enhancing productivity, 
innovation, sustainability and global competitiveness 
toward Viksit Bharat@2047.
CII CENTRE OF
MANUFACTURING
EXCELLENCE
TECHNICAL TRAINING & CAPABILITY 
DEVELOPMENT
CII-CME conducted over 190 training programmes 
through both open and customised in-company 
formats. These programmes were delivered by a 
strong pool of experienced faculty and Industry 
practitioners and covered critical focus areas including 
manufacturing and operations, Industry 4.0, advanced 
manufacturing and analytics, occupational health and 
safety, project and supply chain management, 
international trade & ﬁnance and human resources 
(HR), sales and other soft skills.
The initiatives collectively reached to more than 1500 
organisations, 4000 professionals and 450 MSMEs, 
enabling participants to strengthen technical 
competencies, adopt digital and smart manufacturing 
practices, improve shop-ﬂoor productivity, enhance 
safety performance and build leadership and behavioural 
capabilities for sustainable business performance.
INTERNATIONAL & DOMESTIC 
LEARNING MISSIONS
CII-CME’s learning missions provided immersive 
exposure to global and domestic best practices. 
The Learning Mission to Japan on Smart 
Manufacturing and the World Expo oﬀered 
participants ﬁrsthand insights into advanced 
production systems, automation, robotics, digital 
manufacturing and sustainability-driven innovation 
through curated visits to leading manufacturing 
facilities, research institutions and innovation 
ecosystems. The mission enabled benchmarking with 
global leaders and provided strategic perspectives on 
Japan’s manufacturing excellence, quality culture and 
continuous improvement ethos.
The Domestic Learning Mission on Manufacturing 
Excellence and Smart Manufacturing in Pune, 
Maharashtra, focused on peer learning and practical 
exposure within the Indian context. Participants 
benchmarked progressive Indian organisations, gained 
insights into technology adoption, lean practices, 
quality systems and operational excellence 
frameworks and identiﬁed scalable best practices 
relevant to their own enterprises.
OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH & SAFETY 
(OHS)
Strengthening safety leadership and systems remains 
a core focus area for CII-CME. The Centre anchors the 
National Task Force on Industrial Safety which has 
participation across sectors from both top 
management to safety leaders.
The 10th National Conference on Occupational Health & 
Safety held in Mumbai, brought together more than 200 
safety professionals, senior leaders, policymakers and 
experts to deliberate on strengthening occupational 
safety and health systems, integrating technology and 
behavioural interventions and aligning safety 
performance with India’s long-term development vision.

The 7th edition of the Competition on Best Practices in 
Occupational Health & Safety, covered engineering, 
manufacturing, oil, gas, chemicals, construction, 
infrastructure and utilities sectors and received 
participation from 100 companies, reﬂecting strong 
Industry engagement. A robust three-level evaluation 
process-comprising detailed submission review, online 
presentations and physical site assessments-ensured 
objectivity and rigour. The competition recognised 
exemplary initiatives and reinforced the importance of 
proactive risk management, structured emergency 
planning and preparedness in building resilient 
organisations and safer workplaces.
AWARDS & RECOGNITION FOR 
MANUFACTURING EXCELLENCE
CII’s National Awards for Excellence in Manufacturing 
remain India’s most prestigious recognition, celebrating 
organisations that demonstrate outstanding 
performance and leadership across all dimensions of 
manufacturing excellence. The awards are based on a 
comprehensive evaluation framework covering seven 
key parameters: technology, collaboration, production, 
market dynamics, sustainability, policy and behavioural 
aspects—providing a 360° view of organisational 
capabilities and Industry best practices.
The 4th edition of the awards witnessed participation 
from 77 organisations spanning diverse sectors, 
reﬂecting commitment to innovation, operational 
eﬃciency, sustainability and global competitiveness. 
Organisations were assessed on their ability to 
integrate advanced technologies, optimise production 
processes, foster collaboration across the value chain, 
respond eﬀectively to market dynamics, implement 
sustainable practices, adhere to policies and promote a 
culture of continuous improvement and excellence 
among their workforces.
The awards served as a benchmark for manufacturing 
excellence, encouraging organisations to adopt best 
practices, drive innovation and elevate their global 
competitiveness.
YOUTH ENGAGEMENT & 
MANUFACTURING ADVOCACY
CII-CME hosted the 6th edition of ANVESH, India’s 
premier manufacturing quiz, nurturing awareness, 
interest and engagement among young professionals 
and students in the manufacturing sector. The initiative 
creates a platform where participants can explore 
manufacturing concepts, emerging technologies, 
Industry trends and operational excellence practices, 
fostering a‘manufacturing- friendly’ mindset among the 
next generation of Industry leaders.
The 2025 edition witnessed participation from over 200 
young professionals and students representing leading 
manufacturing companies, startups and academic 
institutions across India.
The quiz covered a wide spectrum of topics, including 
manufacturing processes, quality systems, continuous 
improvement methodologies, design philosophies, 
Industry best practices and regulatory frameworks, 
encouraging participants to deepen their understanding 
of real-world manufacturing challenges and 
innovations.
Structured in a multi-stage format, including preliminary 
rounds, semi-ﬁnal buzzer rounds and a high-intensity 
grand ﬁnale, the quiz tested both conceptual 
knowledge and problem-solving agility. ANVESH 2025 
not only celebrated excellence and innovation but also 
reinforced the importance of knowledge-driven 
competitiveness, critical thinking and collaborative 
learning in shaping India’s manufacturing ecosystem.
