pages.description: CII Annual Report 2025-26 — theme: Accelerating Competitiveness: Globalisation, Inclusivity, Sustainability, Trust.
pages.text:
Annual Report 2025-2680
ENERGY TRANSITION SERVICES
CII-GBC houses India’s largest energy eﬃciency team, 
facilitating industries to achieve world-class energy 
eﬃciency standards. The team collaborates with 
Industry, Government and national & global 
organisations to drive impactful actions toward Net 
Zero emissions.
Key accomplishments: 
• Conducted more than 2200 energy audits across 
25 countries
• Trained over 1,00,000 professionals in energy 
eﬃciency management
• Developed more than 100 energy eﬃciency 
manuals and publications
• Facilitated over 400 innovative technologies 
driving emissions reduction
• Facilitated renewable energy in excess of 1 GW 
across the country
• Certiﬁed 104 vendors through the CII Rooftop 
Solar Vendor Rating Programme (VRP)
• Recognised more than 180 plants through the CII 
Performance Excellence Awards for Solar, Wind 
and Hybrid Plants.
The Energy Eﬃciency Summit, India’s largest 
conference on energy eﬃciency, marked its 24th 
anniversary this year. Featuring sector-focused 
conferences on thermal power and pulp & paper, it 
hosted the National Award for Excellence in Energy 
Management and witnessed international 
participation, including 19 startups from Australia, 
highlighting global collaboration and innovation in 
energy eﬃciency solutions. 
IGBC GREEN AND NET ZERO 
BUILDING MOVEMENT 
In alignment with its vision to facilitate India’s 
leadership in Net Zero and sustainable development, 
the Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) has been 
driving climate-responsive, energy-and 
resource-eﬃcient practices through certiﬁcation, 
membership and capacity-building initiatives. As IGBC 
marked its Silver Jubilee this year, it strengthened its 
contributions to national goals of Net Zero emissions 
by 2070. 
IGBC’s milestones achieved:
• Approximately 15.75 billion sq ft green building 
footprint with more than 19,070 IGBC registered 
projects
• Thirty-two regional chapters, 260 founding 
Members and over 2600 organisational Members
• Impact from approximately 36 lakh residential 
dwelling units, over 4990 residential projects, 
10,915 commercial projects, 920 industrial buildings, 
1260 transit infrastructure projects, 188 built 
environment projects and 245 Net Zero projects.
Asia’s largest green building conference and expo, the 
Green Building Congress, witnessed the launch of 
IGBC Green Hotels Rating System along with product 
launches by 21 exhibitors. These initiatives highlighted 
market readiness for adoption of green building 
products, materials and technologies, reinforcing the 
integration of innovation and standards with India’s 
green building and Net Zero ecosystem.
GREENPRO ECOLABEL
The GreenPro Ecolabel empowers end users to choose 
environmentally friendly products and materials, 
minimising the ecological impact of construction 
activities and the built environment.
The CII Green Business Centre (CII-GBC) is CII’s 
developmental institute on green practices and 
businesses, aimed at oﬀering world-class advisory 
services on conservation of natural resources. CII-GBC 
provides services on energy management, green 
buildings, green companies, green product certiﬁcation, 
cleantech startup acceleration, green mobility and 
green cooling. Together, all the services facilitate a 
reduction of over 55 million tons of CO2 per year.
CII GREEN BUSINESS
CENTRE
Annual Report 2025-26 81
As of 2025, GreenPro has certiﬁed over 14,500 
products from more than 750 companies across 50 
categories for ecolabelling standards.
Key achievements: 
• Signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) 
with the Singapore Environment Council to enable 
mutual recognition and strengthen sustainable 
procurement in the APAC region
• Recognised John Deere for its leadership and 
innovation in advancing sustainability across its 
supply chain
• Ecolabelling India’s ﬁrst GreenPro-certiﬁed 
two-wheeler, manufactured by TVS Motor Company
• Signed MoUs with Green Mark – Republic of 
Uzbekistan and the Thailand Ecolabelling Institute. 
These partnerships aim to facilitate green trade, 
enable alignment of sustainability standards and 
promote mutual recognition of ecolabels, 
strengthening cross-border cooperation in 
sustainable consumption and production.
GREENCO COUNCIL
The GreenCo Council is an Industry-led body overseeing 
India's premier environmental performance rating 
system and certiﬁcations for the Industry. Through 
leadership engagement and capacity building, it drives 
advancements in climate action, energy eﬃciency, 
water stewardship, circular economy principles and 
green supply chains, positioning Indian Industry as a 
global sustainability leader.
GreenCo milestones:
• Rating over 1050 industrial units, delivering 
measurable reductions in emissions, resource use 
and operating costs
• The ﬁrst 600 GreenCo-rated industrial units 
mitigated 5.7 million tonnes of GHG emissions, 
conserved 194 million kL of water and saved INR 
5136 crore annually
• Marked signiﬁcant expansion, with GreenCo 
initiating internationalisation through a feasibility 
study in Southeast Asia
• Launched Zero Liquid Discharge Certiﬁcation 
Guidelines
• Certiﬁed 760 practitioners through 13 training 
programmes
• Convened 32 forum meetings and events 
showcasing advanced green technologies
L - R: Dr Suchitra K Ella, Vice President, CII and Co-Founder & Managing 
Director, Bharat Biotech International Limited; Duddilla Sridhar Babu, 
Minister for Information Technology, Electronics & Communications, 
Industries & Commerce and Legislative Aﬀairs, Government of 
Telangana and Jamshyd Godrej, Chairman & Managing Director, 
Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Company Ltd at the GreenCo Summit 
in Hyderabad
• Advanced institutional engagement via an MoU 
with the Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board, 
integrating GreenCo metrics into regulatory 
frameworks
• Expanded digital accessibility with ‘Greenie’, an 
AI-powered advisory chatbot
• Flagship platforms, including the GreenCo Summit, 
the Waste and Resource Management Summit and 
the Indian Green Champions League, mobilised 
thousands of stakeholders.
These initiatives accelerated pathways toward Net 
Zero, circular economy adoption and enhanced ESG 
performance nationwide.
GREEN ENTREPRENEURSHIP COUNCIL 
The Green Entrepreneurship Council (GEC) fosters an 
ecosystem of innovators, implementers and mentors to 
drive clean tech innovation and accelerate its market 
adoption. By 2025, GEC made a signiﬁcant impact in 
promoting collaboration and innovation within the 
cleantech and sustainability sectors. 
Key achievements: 
• Over 50 cleantech startup cohort Members 
• Introduced the startups to more than 15 sectors 
• Facilitated 570 B2B interactions
• Generated over 700 B2B interests from Industry 
stakeholders
• Countries engaged - Australia, Bangladesh, 
Sweden, Ethiopia and Japan.
Annual Report 2025-2682
NEW INITIATIVES
CII National Leadership Summit
The maiden edition of the CII National Leadership 
Summit emerged as the apex leadership platform of 
the Centre, bringing together senior leaders and 
policymakers to examine leadership in an era of 
disruption and change. The Summit focused on 
building leadership capabilities that balance purpose 
with performance, agility with resilience and 
innovation with responsibility. Through high-impact 
keynotes and curated dialogues, it explored 
leadership imperatives across strategy, technology, 
transformation and culture.
Animal Wellbeing Summit
The maiden National Animal Wellbeing Summit 
convened policymakers, regulators, Industry leaders, 
researchers and innovators to strengthen India’s 
animal health ecosystem. Discussions focused on 
modernising regulatory and policy frameworks, 
promoting indigenous research & development, 
accelerating digital adoption and enhancing global 
competitiveness in line with national priorities such as 
Atmanirbhar Bharat and rural economic development. 
Deliberations highlighted the critical role of animal 
wellbeing in food security, public health and rural 
livelihoods. Key themes included upgrading disease 
surveillance, improving access to quality veterinary 
products & services and tapping emerging 
opportunities in companion animal health, alternate 
medicine integration and export-driven 
manufacturing.
CAPACITY BUILDING 
INTERVENTIONS
Certiﬁed Leadership Development 
Programme for ‘First Time Managers’
Acknowledging the pivotal role that emerging talent 
plays in organisational success, the Centre delivered 
three editions of its ﬂagship, long-duration, 
evaluation-based certiﬁcation programme. The 
programme was designed to nurture future-ready 
leaders and adopted a multi-touchpoint learning 
design. The initiative integrated innovative 
methodologies including online simulations, 
e-learning modules and videocasts, enabling sustained 
engagement, applied learning and long-term impact.
12th & 13th Young Leadership 
Development Digital Programme 
In a period marked by business uncertainty, 
organisations continued to place strong emphasis on 
leveraging and developing internal talent. In response, 
the Centre delivered successive editions of its ﬂagship 
Young Leadership Development Digital Programme 
(YLDP). The programme’s sustained relevance and 
impact were reﬂected in continued organisational 
participation, underscoring its eﬀectiveness in 
preparing emerging leaders to take on higher 
responsibilities and future leadership roles.
NextGen Finance Leadership 
Development Programme
The NextGen Finance Leadership Development 
Programme was designed as a strategic 
capability-building initiative to enhance leadership 
eﬀectiveness of ﬁnance professionals in a complex and 
dynamic business environment. Through expert-led 
sessions, case discussions and experiential learning, 
participants strengthened their understanding of 
strategic ﬁnance, risk management and value creation, 
emerging better equipped to navigate volatility and 
contribute meaningfully to business strategy.
Amid global uncertainties and emerging 
opportunities, the CII Centre of Excellence (CoE) for 
Leadership focused on building leadership capacities 
through innovative 'people' and 'process' 
transformations. Interventions included training 
programmes, ﬂagship conferences, masterclasses and 
targeted interventions, fostering new skills and 
driving business excellence.
CII CENTRE OF
EXCELLENCE
FOR LEADERSHIP
Annual Report 2025-26 83
L-R: R Mukundan, President Designate, CII & Chairman, CII Leadership Summit and Managing Director & CEO, Tata Chemicals Ltd; Sudhanshu Vats, 
Managing Director, Pidilite Industries and Neelkanth Mishra, Chief Economist, Axis Bank at The National Leadership Summit 2025 in Mumbai
CII Certiﬁed Online Programme on 
Strategising in Fiercely Competitive 
Markets
Recognising the critical role played by mid-level 
managers in organisational performance, the 
programme was curated to strengthen the strategic 
management capabilities of middle and senior 
leaders. It equipped participants with practical tools 
and perspectives to navigate market complexity and 
make informed, forward-looking decisions that create 
sustainable competitive advantage.
Leadership in the Age of AI
Recognising the growing impact of artiﬁcial 
intelligence (AI) and Generative AI on leadership and 
organisational decision-making, the CoE conducted 
two batches of its ﬂagship ‘Leadership in the Age of 
AI’ programme. Designed for senior and mid-level 
leaders, the live virtual programme focused on 
building future-ready leadership capabilities by 
enabling participants to align AI with strategy, 
navigate change eﬀectively and lead responsibly in an 
AI-integrated business environment.
Certiﬁed Programme on Current & 
Emerging Technologies for Managers
To help managers navigate the fast-changing 
technological landscape, the Centre conducted batch 
II of the CII Certiﬁed Programme on Current & 
Emerging Technologies for Managers (CII-CETM).
The programme covered the ‘Essential Six’ 
technologies: AI and machine learning (ML), internet 
of things (IoT) and the Metaverse, cloud services, 
robotic process automation (RPA), augmented & 
virtual reality and blockchain. Designed to empower 
managers with actionable insights, it focused on 
leveraging these technologies to drive innovation, 
enhance eﬃciency and create competitive 
advantages. 
Leadership Programme on Generative AI
The Centre organised the 2nd Cohort – ‘Leadership 
Programme on Generative AI and Knowledge Graphs 
for Business Growth’ which explored how Generative 
AI, enhanced by retrieval-augmented generation 
(RAG) and knowledge graphs, can drive innovation, 
improve decision-making and boost operational 
eﬃciency. Participants included business leaders and 
professionals keen to leverage these transformative 
technologies.
OutThink Masterclass Series
The Centre organised an OutThink Session on ‘Driving 
Business Growth through Strategic Product 
Leadership’. The session brought together Industry 
leaders and experts to share practical perspectives on 
product strategy, innovation, data driven 
decision-making and building resilient product teams. 
With participation from senior practitioners across 
sectors, the programme enabled rich peer learning 
and strategic dialogue.
Annual Report 2025-2684
CII MISSION ON WATER
The CII Mission on Water, with the overarching goal of 
achieving water neutrality by 2030, catalysed 
Industry-led collective action to promote the adoption 
of water-neutral practices across sectors. Guided by 
the principles of sustainability and ecosystem 
preservation, the Mission focused on bridging water 
demand–supply gaps by enabling the creation of 
Water Neutral Companies under the Water Neutrality 
Framework of NITI Aayog. 
Over 90 plants and campuses were certiﬁed as 
'Aspiring Water Neutral' as per NITI Aayog's 
Guidelines, while two facilities were certiﬁed as 
'Water Positive' taking the cumulative total to 110 
plant locations. These companies serve as lighthouse 
examples, demonstrating scalable and replicable 
solutions for water security.
The Mission also advanced awareness and capacity 
building through a series of focused engagements, 
including webinars, training initiatives and thematic 
sessions at various capacity building programmes - 
both at regional and national levels. 
INTERNATIONAL ENGAGEMENTS 
CII Water Institute actively participated in strategic 
international engagements and global water 
stewardship dialogues. The Institute contributed to 
discussions on Corporate Water Stewardship at the 
Stockholm World Water Week 2025 and participated at 
the India–Belgium Collaboration on Water and Waste 
Management Solutions, which explored opportunities 
for partnership with Belgian companies in the sector.
The India–Australia Water Accelerator Programme, 
implemented in partnership with the Australian Trade 
and Investment Commission (Austrade), hosted an 
Australian water-sector delegation in Mumbai and 
Chennai, enabling dialogue, technology exchange and 
partnership development.
ADVISORY SERVICES 
CII’s water audits over the years have resulted in 
potential water savings of 400 billion litres, guiding 
Indian industries towards improved water use eﬃciency. 
In 2025, the Institute undertook 70 water audits across 
India, with signiﬁcant water-saving potential (30-40%) 
possible through low-to-medium cost strategies. 
The Centre also built competitiveness in the Industry 
through CII’s performance-cum-system-based 
certiﬁcation and ranking-CII Blue Rating System.
The CII Water Institute addresses emerging and 
complex water challenges through science-led, 
technology- driven solutions. Leveraging advanced 
digital analytics, tools and frameworks, the Centre 
supports informed decision-making and advances the 
national agenda for a water-secure future.
Recipients of the Water Neutrality Certiﬁcation at Water Innovation Summit 2025 in New Delhi
CII WATER INSTITUTE

Annual Report 2025-26 85
Following the assessment, plants were rated based on 
water management in operations, watershed level 
community engagement, supply chains and leadership 
strategies.
Hydrological, Hydrogeological and 
WATSCAN Studies for Indian Industries
CII's WATSCAN tool, a digital water resource 
assessment tool, has been pivotal in undertaking 
hydrological assessments, oﬀering insights on water 
resources. About 4.5 lakh sq km of India’s geographical 
area has been mapped by WATSCAN so far. WATSCAN 
was applied to projects run by a leading Industry 
Member in their Nimapada unit in Odisha and 
Bengaluru unit in Karnataka, where it facilitated 
watershed assessments, identiﬁcation of recharge 
opportunities, evaluation of lake rejuvenation 
potential, understanding of hydrological behaviour 
and water security challenges. These insights enabled 
eﬀective strategic planning, prioritisation of 
interventions, capacity enhancement and 
development of sustainable water conservation and 
groundwater recharge initiatives.
CII Water Institute also conducted two detailed 
hydrogeological studies supporting sustainable water 
management across the airports and distilleries sectors in 
India. Notable projects included aquifer analysis for various 
industries, groundwater monitoring for plants in Alwar 
and a Water Sustainability Study and Water Neutrality 
Assessment for leading public infrastructure entities.
KNOWLEDGE SHARING 
Water Innovation Summit 
The 11th Water Innovation Summit provided a 
platform to discuss opportunities, partnerships and 
collaborations for enhancing water security. 
Deliberations at this ﬂagship annual event 
underscored the urgency of adopting sustainable 
practices, strengthening resilience to emerging water 
risks and the power of collective action in driving 
long-term water security. 
Israel was the Focus Country at the Summit, where 
Indian companies engaged in B2B meetings with an 
Israeli delegation.
CII National Awards for Excellence in 
Water Management 
The 19th CII National Awards for Excellence in Water 
Management recognised 25 companies across sectors 
for their water management practices across three 
categories – ‘Within the Fence’ (within the company), 
‘Beyond the Fence’ (at the watershed level) and 
‘Innovative Water Saving Product’. 
WaterTech Summit 
Deliberations at the CII Water-Tech Summit focused 
on digital innovation, AI-enabled automation and 
cross-disciplinary approaches alongside cost-eﬀective 
and environmentally sustainable strategies for water 
reuse, resource recovery and advanced systems for 
measuring and monitoring water resources. 
Discussions also echoed strong emphasis on 
collaboration among Government, Industry and 
technology partners.
National Conference on Pulp and Paper
The 10th edition of the CII Pulp and Paper Summit 
emphasised the importance of sustainability, 
innovation and future readiness in the pulp and paper 
Industry. The Summit highlighted the need for 
long-term resilience through sustainable water 
management practices, eﬀective policy integration 
and climate-conscious operations. 
Recipients of the 19th CII National Awards for Excellence in Water Management
Annual Report 2025-2686
The CII Food and Agriculture Centre of Excellence 
(CII-FACE) strengthens India’s agri-food value chain 
from farm to fork through innovation, capacity 
building and productivity enhancement. Working with 
farmers, Industry and Government, CII-FACE helps to 
improve market access, food safety and farmers’ 
incomes while reducing post-harvest losses. Through 
data-driven assessments, sectoral research and 
high-impact public–private partnerships, the Centre of 
Excellence (CoE) delivers scalable solutions that 
advance food security, nutrition, sustainability and 
inclusive growth.
Through the Dairy Investment Accelerator project 
(DIA), CII-FACE is advancing inclusive and sustainable 
transformation in India’s dairy sector by combining 
farmer-centric innovation, capacity building and 
investment facilitation, with a strong focus on 
women-led smallholder farmers. DIA scales proven 
technology solutions such as solar-powered 
hydroponic fodder systems, silage baling and 
AI-enabled artiﬁcial insemination to address fodder 
insecurity, improve milk yields, reduce costs and lower 
environmental impacts. This initiative in Madhya 
Pradesh trained over 3000 women farmers and 
facilitated nearly INR 1000 crore in dairy investments 
in Uttar Pradesh, oﬀering a scalable model for sectoral 
transformation. It was instrumental in increasing milk 
yields by 1–2 litres per cow per day in Bihar. 
LARGE-SCALE FOOD FORTIFICATION
CII-FACE contributed to Large-Scale Food Fortiﬁcation 
(LSFF) by strengthening quality systems, mobilising 
private-sector participation and building technical 
capacity across the value chain. Through ecosystem 
assessments on double fortiﬁed salt, technical 
exposure visits, Industry engagement on premix 
supply and state-level capacity-building workshops, 
CII-FACE addressed key challenges related to quality 
TRAINING AND CAPACITY BUILDING
Food Safety and Quality Workshops
Assessor trainings for CII Food Safety Awards, FSSAI’s 
Food Safety Training and Certiﬁcation (FoSTaC) and 
interactive workshops on ‘Enhancing Analytical Skills of 
Food Lab Personnel’ were extensively conducted Pan 
India, to strengthen capacity of food business operators. 
More than 500 participants attended these workshops.
CII FOOD AND
AGRICULTURE CENTRE
OF EXCELLENCE
DAIRY INVESTMENT ACCELERATOR
PROJECT
compliance, testing credibility and scale-up, 
reinforcing the quality, credibility and scalability of 
food fortiﬁcation in India.
BUILDING RESILIENT VALUE CHAINS: 
APPLE AND CHILLI 
Under the Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) 
Business Support Unit, two value chain development 
initiatives were implemented with FPOs in selected 
districts in Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka, focusing on 
apples and red chilli, respectively. Launched in 2023–24, 
the programmes strengthens FPO institutions, improve 
post-harvest and on-farm practices, enabling digital and 
climate-smart interventions and enhancing market 
linkages. These programmes supported scalable, 
quality-focused value chains aimed at improving 
farmers’ incomes and long-term resilience.
Impact
• 12 FPOs engaged across three states and more 
than 40 villages
• More than 3000 farmers reached across 
horticulture and spice value chains
• Over 9000 acres covered through improved 
agronomy and digital tools
• Targeted capacity building on post-harvest 
management, value addition and Integrated Pest 
Management (IPM)
• Adoption of climate-smart practices, bio-input and 
real-time advisories
• Stronger institutional capacity and market 
readiness of FPOs.
ACTION
Annual Report 2025-26 87
Awardees receiving the 15th CII Food Safety Awards in New Delhi
Agri-Carbon Market Masterclass
CII-FACE launched an Agri-Carbon Market Masterclass 
series that strengthened stakeholder's understanding 
and capacity of agri-carbon markets. The ﬁrst 
masterclass, held in New Delhi in November, 
comprised six modules covering the fundamentals of 
agri-carbon markets, project-level greenhouse gas 
accounting, engagement with carbon registries, risk 
management in voluntary carbon markets, ensuring 
credit quality and integrity and ﬁnancing mechanisms 
for carbon project development and implementation.
BUILDING A CULTURE OF EXCELLENCE 
CII Food Safety Awards 
The 15th edition of the CII Food Safety Awards was 
organised in New Delhi, recognising excellence in 
food safety across small, medium and large food 
businesses. The Awards promote internationally 
benchmarked food safety practices, build capacity 
across the food value chain and provide a framework 
for continual improvement. The initiative 
strengthened food safety performance across 22 food 
sectors, with applications increasing 14-fold and the 
pool of trained assessors expanding more than 
25-fold over the last 15 years.
CII Food Safety and Quality Kaizen 
Competition
The 7th edition of the CII Food Safety and Quality 
Kaizen Competition, organised in partnership with 
Food Safety System Certiﬁcation (FSSC) and in 
collaboration with Japan Union of Scientists and 
Engineers (JUSE), was held in New Delhi. It showcased 
grassroots innovations from across the food sector 
and attracted nearly 100 participants. Over the years, 
the competition has generated 289 improvement 
ideas across 10 food sectors, setting benchmarks for 
MSMEs and large enterprises while fostering 
cross-learning. This edition reinforced the 
competition’s role as a catalyst for innovation, 
operational excellence and continuous improvement 
across India’s food sector.
CII FPO Excellence Awards
The 3rd edition of the CII FPO Excellence Awards was 
held alongside the CII FPO Summit in New Delhi. The 
Awards showcased achievements of outstanding FPOs 
across 4 distinct categories - market linkages, women 
leadership, technology deployment & value addition 
and branding. 
CII Cold Chain Awards
The 9th CII Cold Chain Awards, held in Mumbai, 
recognised organisations and initiatives demonstrating 
excellence in innovation, sustainability, operational 
eﬃciency and service quality across the cold-chain 
value chain. The Awards celebrated Industry leadership 
and best practices that are shaping a resilient, 
technology- driven and future-ready cold chain 
ecosystem. This year, alongside regular categories such 
as Integrated Supply Chain Solutions, IQF Technology 
and Frozen Food Cold Chain, new categories were 
introduced to acknowledge emerging innovations in 
last-mile delivery, controlled atmosphere technology, 
automated cold storage and collaborative partnerships.
Annual Report 2025-2688
CII Centre of Excellence for Innovation, 
Entrepreneurship and Startups (CII-CIES) is a national 
catalyst for innovation that shapes meaningful 
engagement in India’s startup ecosystem. Through 
structured programmes, partnerships and policy 
engagement, CII-CIES strengthens innovation 
pathways toward enterprise adoption and scale.
Since the Centre’s launch in 2020, it has enabled 
startups to scale while helping corporates co-create 
solutions that address sectoral challenges and unlock 
sustainable economic value nationwide.
CII CENTRE OF
EXCELLENCE FOR INNOVATION,
ENTREPRENEURSHIP
AND STARTUPS
ADVOCACY
CII-CIES continued its policy advocacy eﬀorts by 
submitting more than 100 recommendations to central 
ministries and State Governments to create a more 
enabling environment for innovation, growth and 
competitiveness.
CII-CIES submitted GST rationalisation 
recommendations including relief for Research & 
Development (R&D) and prototyping, incubation 
services, Government project procurement in 
strategic sectors like defence and environment.
The Centre proposed key reforms to further strengthen 
India’s startup ecosystem, with a focus on tax and 
compliance simpliﬁcation, patent incentives, streamlined 
exit processes and enhanced access to capital.
Targeted recommendations were submitted to the 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on 
enabling founders to receive Employee Stock 
Ownership Plans (ESOPs), providing ﬂexibility in 
promoter shareholding post the Initial Public Oﬀering 
(IPO), taxing ESOPs at liquidity instead of at exercise 
and creating a multi-tiered capital market to support 
startups while protecting investor interests.
The Centre also developed an Action Plan to support 
and scale startups in agritech, biotech and 
semiconductors that outlined a comprehensive 
strategy to build globally competitive startup 
ecosystems in these sectors under the NITI Aayog FTH 
Startup Workstream. The initiative focused on key 
enablers such as policy reforms, funding access, 
infrastructure development, talent creation, R&D and 
international collaborations. 
The CII Unicorn Forum strengthened its policy 
inﬂuence by enabling structured founder-led 
engagement ‘Founder’s Huddle‘ to surface priority 
issues across key sectors and translate them into 
focused, outcome-oriented policy dialogue aligned 
with Industry and national priorities.
Corporates across diverse sectors from automobile 
and healthcare to consumer products and jewellery 
were engaged through the Market Access initiative 
across 100 focus areas, supported by innovative 
startups. This resulted in 1500 applications from 
startups, of which 240 were shortlisted to pitch 
directly to corporates. Collectively, these 
engagements accelerated meaningful Industry-startup 
collaborations, enabling innovation adoption, pilot 
opportunities and long-term partnerships.
The CII-CIES Startup Aﬃliation Programme is designed 
to certify growth stage startups and provide them a 
platform to connect with corporates and key 
ecosystem enablers. The aﬃliation serves as a 
credible endorsement, reﬂecting rigorous vetting 
against Industry benchmarks, enhancing startup 
visibility. Many aﬃliated startups received the 
opportunity to pitch their products and services to 
corporates and investors through the monthly 
360-degree pitching series. For founders, this 
translated into stronger positioning and increased 
readiness for enterprise and investor engagement.
CII-CIES delivered high-impact capacity building 
masterclasses across key ecosystem segments, 
reaching more than 450 leaders while creating 
sustained stakeholder relationships. The Family Oﬃce 
Masterclass series themed ‘Why Investing in Startups 
Should Be Part of Your Portfolio’ was conducted
across Aurangabad, Madurai, Hyderabad and 
Kolkata, engaging over 100 family oﬃces. These 
sessions focused on alternative investments, startup 
due diligence beyond ﬁnancial metrics and portfolio 
construction for patient capital.
The ‘Art of Storytelling’ Masterclass trained startup 
founders in purpose-driven pitch development using 
the 4C Framework (Customer, Context, Challenge, 
Change). The Corporate Venture Capital (CVC) 
Masterclass engaged CVC heads with strategic 
frameworks for dual-objective mandates (ﬁnancial 
returns and strategic alignment). By deepening 
understanding of startup potential and alternative 
investment approaches, the sessions enhanced the 
ability of stakeholders to unlock innovation and 
channel capital into high-impact startups.
The ﬂagship ICONN Summit served as a 
multi-stakeholder platform bringing together 
corporates, startups, investors and ecosystem 
enablers to advance innovation-led collaboration. 
The summit featured three thematic tracks - 
Sustainability, Manufacturing and Financial Inclusion 
- along with an expo showcasing solutions from 
startups. Key knowledge outputs included three 
reports and compendiums on hardware and 
DeepTech innovation, ﬁnancial inclusion and 
women-led innovation. The programme also oﬀered 
high-impact masterclasses focused on future-ready 
product innovation and responsible use of emerging 
technologies, equipping participants with strategic 
insights, practical perspectives and collaboration 
opportunities.
Aligning with the ICONN Summit, CII-CIES successfully 
concluded the 6th edition of the CII Startupreneur 
Awards, recognising and celebrating groundbreaking 
innovations and entrepreneurial excellence shaping the 
future of Indian Industry. This year, from over 700 
applications received nationwide, 12 outstanding 
startups were recognised across the categories of Best 
Women-Led Innovation, Best Social Impact Startup, 
Excellence in Product/Technology Innovation by a 
Startup and Best Emerging Innovation.
ICONN NINJA India Programme is a strategic initiative 
jointly led by CII-CIES and the Japan International 
Cooperation Agency (JICA) under the Supporting Indian 
Startups for Global Business Expansion (SGBBE) 
project. The programme deepens Indo-Japan startup 
collaboration by facilitating structured engagements 
between high-potential Indian startups and leading 
Japanese corporates. This year, three cohorts brought 
together nine Japanese corporations and 30 startups 
selected from 1500 applications, creating tangible 
opportunities for cross-border partnerships. 
CII-CIES organised four international startup delegations 
to Japan, Sweden, UAE and Singapore. The delegations 
enabled B2B meetings and interactions with 
Government leaders, investors, corporates and 
ecosystem enablers across global platforms including 
SusHiTech, Osaka Expo, GITEX, Vitalis and SWITCH. 
These missions signiﬁcantly strengthened India’s global 
innovation footprint, facilitating market access, 
partnerships and investment linkages. The engagements 
also translated into concrete market expansion 
opportunities, helping startups establish a presence and 
strengthen operations in international markets.

Annual Report 2025-2690
The CII Centre of Excellence (CoE) on Skills bridges the 
skills gap and cultivates a future-ready workforce by 
aligning the skilling and placement initiatives to the 
dynamic Industry requirements, thereby delivering 
measurable social impact at scale. 
In line with this strategy, CII strengthened its policy 
engagement with the States and the Central 
Government, focusing on creating a vibrant skilling 
ecosystem in the country. Through the year, CII scaled 
up Industry-Academia collaboration through CII Multi 
Skill Training Institutes (MSTIs), CII Model Career 
Centres (MCCs), Education 2 Employment (E2E) 
Career Lounges, certiﬁcation programmes and 
international pathway programmes.
CII CENTRE OF
EXCELLENCE ON SKILLS
ADVOCACY
To strengthen policy coherence, deepen Industry 
alignment and enhance India’s skilling ecosystem, the 
CII National Committee on Skill Development and 
Livelihood engaged with key stakeholders to build a 
robust policy advocacy agenda.
Several position papers identifying priority reform 
areas were prepared and submitted to the 
Government.
Recommendations included development of a 
Universal Labour Information Management System 
(ULIMS); creation of an integrated dashboard, linking 
State Skill Development Missions with the Ministry of 
Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE); 
adoption of a cluster-based approach through 
Integrated Skill Development Centres (ISDCs); 
facilitating skilling and upskilling of the micro, small 
and medium enterprise (MSME) workforce; policy 
incentives to promote quality skilling and 
employment; development of a framework for 
international skill mapping and skill gap studies; and 
strengthening IndiaSkills and WorldSkills initiatives.
Dedicated sessions were held with Shri Jayant 
Chaudhary, Minister of State (I/C), MSDE and Smt 
Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE, focusing on 
strengthening Industry-aligned skilling pathways to 
L-R: Suresh Prabhu, Former Union Minister; Dr Arvind Virmani, Member, NITI Aayog; Aditya Ghosh, Chairman, CII National Committee on Skill Development 
& Livelihood and Co-Founder, Akasa Airlines & Founder- Homage and Chairman, Social Enterprise Centre of SEWA at the CII Conference on Jobs & Future 
of Work: Critical Growth Enablers in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26 91
meet domestic and global workforce requirements; 
institutionalising Industry participation in curriculum 
design; enhancing trainer exposure to Industry 
practices; expanding apprenticeships and placement 
linkages; modernising industrial training institute (ITI) 
infrastructure to deliver job-ready outcomes; and 
accelerating the rollout of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling 
and Employability Transformation (PM-SETU) through 
upgraded ITIs.
ACTION 
STRENGTHENING INDUSTRY- 
ALIGNED SKILLING AND 
EMPLOYMENT ECOSYSTEM
CII MCCs, operating as Industry-led employment 
exchanges, provide aptitude-based career counselling, 
soft skills training and placement support to youth. 
Currently, 59 MCCs operate in 23 states, having 
counselled over 19.14 lakh candidates and placed 
more than 12.86 lakh candidates across key sectors.
Under the guidance of Shri N Chandrababu Naidu, 
Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, four MCCs were 
launched in Vijayawada, Tirupati, Visakhapatnam and 
Sri City. An MCC was also established by the CoE in 
Churachandpur district, Manipur.
CII initiated the E2E Career Lounges to enable a 
seamless transition from education to employment 
for university students. Currently, 31 E2E Career 
Lounges are operational across universities in India, 
with plans to scale up to 100. 
CII MSTIs strengthened their presence, starting 
operations at two new centres - Ghitorni in Delhi and 
Sambalpur in Odisha. These MSTIs are 
multi-corporate, multi-skilling models, designed to 
deliver vocational training across specialised trades in 
high-growth sectors. The CII Skill Centre App was 
launched to expand access to skilling opportunities. 
Eight MSTIs operate in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, 
Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan and West Bengal, with 
20 new MSTIs planned.
INTERNATIONAL PATHWAYS
The CoE facilitated international workforce mobility, 
placing candidates in Japan, Finland and Australia in 
electronics, automotive, healthcare, hospitality, 
shipbuilding, construction and electricals. In Japan, over 
600 Indian candidates have been deployed till date.
To expand global opportunities, CII signed an MoU 
with City & Guilds, the United Kingdom (UK), to 
address skill shortage in the UK. This was followed by 
a Letter of Intent with Deakin University, Australia, to 
launch the Global Job Readiness Programme - 
bringing world-class employability training to Indian 
learners. The International Mobility Initiative is now 
expanded to Germany, South Korea, France, the 
Middle East and other Scandinavian nations.
INDUSTRY-ACADEMIA 
COLLABORATION
India’s ﬁrst international diploma programme - the 
Vocational Education and Training (VET) by École 
hôtelière de Lausanne (EHL), the Swiss Professional 
Diploma in Hospitality, was delivered in partnership 
with EHL Hospitality Business School, Switzerland.
The programme was accredited by National Council 
for Vocational Education and Training, establishing a 
benchmark for global–local integration in skill 
certiﬁcation.
The launch of CII–IGNOU Career Edge Academy will 
deliver Industry–Academia integrated, degree-aligned, 
credit-linked skilling programmes in high-growth 
sectors like hospitality, healthcare, information 
technology, ﬁnance and cybersecurity in online and 
blended formats.
The CoE partnered with the International Centre for 
Industrial Transformation, to accelerate India’s digital 
manufacturing transformation through the globally 
recognised Smart Industry Readiness Index, equipping 
Industry with globally benchmarked frameworks, 
training, assessments, certiﬁcation and sustainable 
Industry 4.0 roadmaps.
The CoE also enabled Industry alignment for the All 
India Council for Technical Education (AICTE)–Industry 
Fellowship Programme, facilitating Academia 
engagement with Industry to gain practical exposure 
and transfer learning to Academia through curriculum 
alignment, enhanced teaching outcomes and 
strengthened Industry–Academia linkages. 
CII, in collaboration with NITI Aayog, also organised 
the Conference on Jobs and Future of Work that 
underscored the need for India’s employment and 
skilling strategy.
Annual Report 2025-2692
CII CENTRE OF
EXCELLENCE ON
EMPLOYMENT AND LIVELIHOOD
The CII Centre of Excellence on Employment & 
Livelihood (CII-CEL) empowers micro and small 
entrepreneurs across India to grow, thrive and scale 
their businesses. CII-CEL aims to transform India’s micro 
entrepreneurial landscape, with a vision to support and 
uplift one lakh micro entrepreneurs across the country. 
The Centre enables growth by providing continuous 
handholding, capacity building engagements, business 
interventions and mentorship for business owners.
It also facilitates market linkages to help entrepreneurs 
expand their reach and scale sustainably.
MICRO BUSINESS EXCELLENCE 
INITIATIVE
To provide guidance and business engagements to 
entrepreneurs and business owners of the micro and small 
enterprises, CII-CEL constituted state and district level 
Entrepreneurs Development Forums (EDFs) nationwide.
Entrepreneurs from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra 
Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Kerala, Odisha, 
Nagaland, Mizoram, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim 
and Ladakh are currently being supported through the 
Centre’s growth engagements and EDFs.
During the year, CII-CEL impacted over 2600 micro 
and small entrepreneurs in 38 districts across 12 
states and one UT. These enterprises employ over 
43,000 people and generate a combined turnover of 
more than INR 13,000 crore.
MICRO AND SMALL BUSINESS 
EXCELLENCE PROJECT
CII-CEL launched its landmark initiative, the Micro and 
Small Business Excellence Project and the Mizoram 
EDF, inaugurated by Shri Pu Lalduhoma, Chief Minister 
of Mizoram. 
The Centre also launched the Project in Odisha and
the Sambalpur EDF in Sambalpur, Odisha.
The initiative was formally inaugurated by Shri 
Dharmendra Pradhan, Minister of Education.
The Centre’s project in Arunachal Pradesh was 
inaugurated by Lt Gen Kaiwalya Trivikram Parnaik 
(Retd), Governor of Arunachal Pradesh.
OUTREACH
Through a Parliamentarians’ session hosted in Delhi in 
August, 28 Members of Parliament from 11 states 
participated. R Dinesh, Immediate Past President, CII

commitments to nurture and scale micro and small 
businesses across India, showcasing a model of 
livelihood improvement.
INCLUSIVE ENTREPRENEURSHIP
CII-CEL, in partnership with the CII Foundation and the 
India Business & Disability Network, organised a 
special growth programme for entrepreneurs with 
disabilities in Tamil Nadu (Coimbatore and Chennai). 
Over 130 entrepreneurs are being supported with 
business strategy, ﬁnancial management, artiﬁcial 
intelligence (AI)-driven marketing and digital tools, 
fostering inclusion and growth.
CII-CEL STATE & DISTRICT 
PARTNERSHIPS
CII-CEL signed a cooperative MoU with the Andhra 
Pradesh MSME Corporation, with the signing taking 
place in the presence of the Chief Minister of Andhra 
Pradesh. Another MoU was signed with the District 
Administration of Chamarajanagar to implement the

Under these MoUs, the State and District Departments 
will jointly work with the CII-CEL initiative in supporting 
over 1200 micro and small business owners.
ENTREPRENEURS DEVELOPMENT 
FORUM ENGAGEMENTS 
The CII–CEL Chennai EDF Meet provided forum 
Members with ﬁrst-hand exposure to world-class 
manufacturing practices. The initiative facilitated peer 
learning and benchmarking of best practices, while 
reinforcing CII–CEL’s objective of enhancing 
competitiveness, operational eﬃciency and growth 
readiness among micro and small entrepreneurs.
Entrepreneurs supported by CII-CEL were mentored by 
CII Business leaders from region, state and zones. Over 
the year, CII-CEL partnered with leading corporates to 
foster inclusive economic growth, empower 
entrepreneurs at the grassroots and build a resilient, 
future-ready India.
Annual Report 2025-2694
VLFM Batch-18 Inauguration in Mumbai
CII’s Competitiveness Development Services (CDS) 
division anchors national-level initiatives that 
strengthen the global readiness of Indian Industry by 
advancing innovation, capability enhancement and the 
adoption of world-class practices. Within this wider 
mandate, CDS steers coordinated transformation 
programmes that blend leadership development with 
manufacturing excellence. The CDS division also aims 
to foster continuous learning, advance small and 
medium enterprises (SMEs) and nurture projects 
ensuring inclusive growth through manufacturing.
COMPETITIVENESS
DEVELOPMENT SERVICES
VISIONARY LEADERS FOR 
MANUFACTURING (VLFM) 
PROGRAMME
CII's Visionary Leaders for Manufacturing (VLFM) 
programme is a nation-building initiative to create 
future-ready leaders who leverage their VLFM learnings 
in their company's ecosystem as 'Champions for Societal 
Manufacturing', through breakthrough thinking, 
envisioning considerable growth and global exposure 
with an experiential continuous learning mindset. 
The VLFM programme, established under a joint 
technical cooperation agreement between the 
Government of India and Japan in December 2006, in 
its 18th batch last year, has trained over 1500 senior 
managers in manufacturing, driving breakthroughs 
across more than 300 organisations. The impact 
includes over 450 documented success stories.
Launch of VLFM Batch 18
Batch 18 of the VLFM programme was inaugurated by 
dignitaries from Industry, representatives from Japan 
International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and senior 
faculty, marking the beginning of another impactful 
journey of leadership and transformation.
This batch represents one of the most diverse and 
vibrant groups of Industry learners and senior experts in 
the programme, bringing together participation from a 
wide range of sectors such as auto original equipment 
manufacturers (OEMs), auto components, air 
conditioning, heavy engineering, automation, chemicals, 
construction, oil and gas, jewellery, fast-moving 
consumer goods (FMCG), appliances, aerospace, 
logistics, textiles and several emerging sectors. 
With 106 participants, Batch 18 stands as the largest 
batch in the history of the VLFM programme, 
reﬂecting its expanding relevance across India’s 
manufacturing landscape. Participants come from key 
functional roles including operations and 
manufacturing, research & development, design, 
supply chain and procurement, quality assurance,

and maintenance, human resources, environment, 
health and safety, marketing & data and artiﬁcial 
intelligence (AI). This multidimensional proﬁle brings 
together deep technical expertise and cross 
functional perspectives, strengthening collaborative 
learning throughout the programme.
Having successfully completed Module 5, Batch 18 is 
now preparing for the Japan Learning Visit in 2026, 
where participants will experience world class 
manufacturing systems, cultural discipline and 
breakthrough thinking.
VLFM Global Learning Visit to Japan 
Each VLFM batch undertakes a Japan Learning Visit, 
one of the most powerful experiential components of 
the programme. The purpose is to learn from Japan’s 
globally admired manufacturing systems, social 
discipline, design philosophy and leadership culture. 
Participants observe Japan through an Outside-In 
perspective, enabling them to return with fresh ideas, 
deeper reﬂection and clarity on what India can 
become. As part of this journey, every participant 
works on a Self Initiated Research (SIR) project that 
generates structured insights aimed at societal and 
industrial beneﬁt.
VLFM participants of Batch 17, during the Japan 
Learning Visit, explored how discipline, culture and 
technology came together to create sustainable 
excellence. They observed unmanned factories where 
robots assemble other robots, inclusive manufacturing 
systems designed for specially abled individuals, and 
futuristic exhibitions showcasing humanoids, 
embodied AI and next generation automation.
They also engaged with Japan’s cultural heritage to 
understand how social values inﬂuence national 
behaviour, productivity and quality consciousness.
This immersive learning experience encouraged 
participants to reﬂect deeply on leadership, systems 
thinking and their own behavioural patterns. The 
Japan module also strengthened cultural and 
economic ties between India and Japan while 
enhancing global leadership skills through direct 
observation, structured reﬂection and exposure to 
advanced manufacturing and societal systems.
16th VLFM Learning Convention and 
Graduation Ceremony
The Graduation Ceremony for Batch 16 was held in 
Mumbai. The ceremony felicitated 76 participants for 
successfully completing their one year programme. 
The ceremony honoured 26 faculty members, who are 
esteemed Industry experts.
The CII Centre of Manufacturing Excellence hosted 
CXOs, presidents, directors, chief human resources 
oﬃcers (CHROs), plant heads, senior managers and 
heads of department (HODs) from nominating 
companies, giving them a ﬁrst hand experience of the 
VLFM ecosystem during the VLFM Learning 
Convention and Graduation Ceremony.
The ceremony was enriched by an interactive question 
and answer session between the audience and the 
panellists, adding depth and value to the learning 
experience.
Visionary Small and Medium Enterprise 
Programme
Under the VLFM umbrella, CII also runs the Visionary 
Small and Medium Enterprise (VSME) programme. 
Launched in 2010, the VSME programme is a strategic 
initiative under VLFM programme. It focuses on 
transforming Indian SMEs, particularly those that 
serve as vendors of OEMs and Tier 1 companies, into 
globally competitive manufacturing units. 
The VSME programme has delivered outstanding 
improvements across the supply chain, supporting 
over 30 OEMs and about 300 Tier 2 and Tier 3 
suppliers so far. 
The successful execution of VSME initiatives across 
diverse manufacturing operations demonstrates how 
focused process improvement and strategic 
alignment can generate substantial business beneﬁts. 
These outcomes not only showcase higher 
productivity and stronger ﬁnancial performance but 
also establish a strong benchmark for operational 
excellence within the SME ecosystem.
Annual Report 2025-2696
FAMILY BUSINESS
NETWORK
The CII Family Business Network (FBN) India Chapter 
continues to advance its mission of strengthening the 
family business ecosystem in India. With a focus on 
continuity, responsible ownership and long-term value 
creation, the Chapter actively curates initiatives that 
support family enterprises across generations.
ACTION
In collaboration with The Family Business Consulting 
Group, a Learning Journey to Saudi Arabia was 
organised for 15 family business leaders from India. 
Held across Riyadh and Jeddah, the programme 
provided ﬁrsthand exposure to the Kingdom’s rapidly 
transforming economic landscape, enabling 
meaningful interactions with leading family 
enterprises and insights into governance, diversity and 
cross-border growth opportunities.
CII–FBN India hosted the FBN Now Gen International 
Forum and Learning Journeys, bringing together 
current-generation leaders from family enterprises 
across the world. The programme featured the main 
forum in Delhi, followed by curated learning journeys 
to Bengaluru, Kochi and Jaipur, oﬀering ﬁrsthand 
exposure to leadership practices and diverse regional 
business ecosystems.
The 6th NxG Annual Summit brought together over 85 
next-generation leaders and family business experts for 
two vibrant days in Bengaluru. The event explored how 
family businesses can evolve while preserving their core 
values. Discussions covered leadership, technology, 
governance and culture, oﬀering fresh perspectives on 
navigating change across generations. 
The 24th CII-FBN India Annual Convention brought 
together family business leaders from across the 
country for two days of reﬂection, dialogue and deep 
engagement on a theme that sits at the heart of every 
enduring enterprise-stewardship. Held in Kochi, the 
convention explored balancing legacy and innovation in 
an increasingly volatile, fast-changing world. 
The closed-door session at Davos convened global 
family business leaders for a candid dialogue on circular 
leadership, innovation and growth.

The CII National Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
(MSME) Council undertook sustained, evidence-based 
advocacy with Ministry of MSME, Finance, Cabinet 
Secretariat, Department for Promotion of Industry 
and Internal Trade, Reserve Bank of India (RBI), NITI 
Aayog and Parliamentary Committees.
MICRO, SMALL & MEDIUM
ENTERPRISES
ADVOCACY
Key CII recommendations accepted:
• Periodic revision of the MSME deﬁnition at ﬁxed 
intervals (every 3–5 years)
• Enhancement of corpus of the Credit Guarantee 
Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises 
(CGTMSE)
• Priority support for micro enterprises through 
aﬀordable credit, capacity building, mentorship, 
market access and infrastructure
• Leveraging Digital Public Infrastructure to enable 
cash-ﬂow–based lending.
The Council presented a comprehensive MSME reform 
agenda to the Cabinet Secretariat and NITI Aayog’s 
High-Level Committee and Working Group on 
Deregulation, covering regulatory simpliﬁcation, 
public procurement, access to ﬁnance and technology 
adoption. Key recommendations included 
decriminalising minor compliance lapses, enabling 
self-certiﬁcation and digital dispute resolution, 
amending the MSMED Act 2006, rationalising Quality 
Control Orders and labour compliances.
CII also advocated for strengthening the Government 
e-Marketplace (GeM)’s deviation and appeal 
mechanisms. In consultation with RBI and ﬁnancial 
regulators, CII recommended measures to sustain 
MSME credit, including regulatory forbearance, 
concessional working capital, enhanced utilisation of 
CGTMSE, extended non-performing assets (NPA) 
recognition timelines and targeted liquidity support 
for export-oriented sectors.
To address trade disruptions from US tariﬀ measures, 
CII advocated targeted support, including an 
Emergency Export Shock Window for MSMEs, 
multi-year interest subvention, assured Remission of 
Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP) 
continuity and stronger export credit and risk-cover 
mechanisms. Following Mexico’s tariﬀ escalation from 
January 2026, CII proposed diplomatic engagement 
for transitional relief on existing contracts and 
sector-speciﬁc exemptions.

Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs), contributing nearly 
13–14% to India’s GDP, remain pivotal to the country’s 
next phase of economic transformation. As India 
advances rapidly towards a USD 10 trillion economy, 
growth will be driven by digitalisation, capital 
expenditure, innovation and supportive policy 
frameworks. In this journey, PSEs are expected to act 
with urgency and collective purpose to expand their 
economic footprint and align with national priorities.
Over the past year, the CII-PSE Council—the apex 
forum of CEOs and CMDs of Central Public Sector 
Enterprises—worked consistently to reinforce the 
critical role of PSEs and to articulate a robust growth 
framework that enables them to be future-ready and 
globally competitive while advancing India’s 
development objectives.
PUBLIC SECTOR
ENTERPRISES
ACTION
A key policy engagement during the year was the 
interaction facilitated by CII between the Secretary, 
Department of Public Enterprises and Chief 
Executives of Central PSEs. This dialogue enabled 
discussion on strengthening the PSE growth 
framework, improving operational eﬃciency and 
aligning enterprise strategies with national 
development priorities. 
Recognising the increasing importance of eﬃcient 
dispute resolution in improving ease of doing business 
(EoDB) for PSEs, CII organised an interactive session on 
‘Adopting a Transformative Vision for Mediation’. The 
session focused on the implications of the new 
Mediation Law and explored mediation and negotiation 
as eﬀective alternative dispute resolution (ADR) 
mechanisms. Policy discussions emphasised reducing 
litigation burdens, improving contract enforcement 
and building institutional capacity through structured 
training of legal professionals to create a pipeline of 
future mediators within the PSE ecosystem.
The Council also advanced policy discourse on 
responsible business conduct and sustainability 
through a dedicated workshop organised in 
Arun Kumar Singh, Chairman, CII PSE Council and Chairman & CEO, 
ONGC and K Moses Chalai, Secretary, Department of Public 
Enterprises at an Interactive Session with Chief Executives of CPSEs
in New Delhi
collaboration with the CII Centre of Excellence on 
Sustainable Development (CII-CESD) and RITES, a 
Navratna PSE. The workshop deliberated on 
Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) integration 
within business operations and value chains, 
biodiversity, climate change, circularity and compliance 
with Business Responsibility and Sustainability 
Reporting (BRSR). 
CII organised a seminar on ‘Legal & Regulatory 
Framework for India’s Energy Sector’ that focused on 
leveraging legal expertise, risk mitigation strategies 
and regulatory clarity to enhance EoDB, ensure 
compliance and support sustainable investment in 
India’s energy economy.
Publications
The Council undertook a research report with support 
from National Foundation for Corporate Governance 
(NFCG) to examine the role of PSEs in facilitating 
EoDB for MSMEs, with a focus on procurement 
practices, institutional engagement, state-level policy 
variations, cluster-based integration and 
sector-speciﬁc experiences. 
‘PSE Insights’, a quarterly magazine oﬀering key 
perspectives and actionable insights into the 
development agenda of PSEs, was published 
periodically during the year. This publication 
highlights the signiﬁcant role of PSEs in driving India’s 
economic growth and reiterates CII’s commitment to 
supporting their advancement.

During the year, organisations moved beyond 
experimenting with Generative AI to embedding it 
into Human Resources (HR) and workforce strategies 
at scale. CII supported members in leveraging artiﬁcial 
intelligence (AI) for practical business impact, guiding 
the integration of technology into decision-making, 
talent development and innovation, while helping 
prepare leaders and workforces for a rapidly evolving 
digital economy.
The CII Committee on Leadership and HR led 
initiatives to help organisations adapt to technological 
shifts. By focusing on innovation, continuous learning 
and skill enhancement, the committee supported 
businesses in transforming HR functions and 
preparing a future-ready workforce.
HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT
ACTION 
15th CII HR Conclave
The 15th CII HR Conclave brought together HR 
leaders, business heads and thought leaders to 
explore the forces reshaping organisations amid 
technological disruption and evolving workforce 
expectations. Discussions reinforced HR’s role as a 
strategic enabler of India’s growth, with leadership 
shifting toward adaptive, purpose-driven models 
deﬁned by mindset and impact rather than hierarchy. 
The conclave highlighted bold workforce strategies, 
including rural and grassroots talent development and 
emphasised AI and human–machine collaboration as 
catalysts for change. Equally central was human 
experience, with wellbeing, resilience, trust and 
belonging recognised as key drivers of sustainable 
performance. Overall, the conclave positioned HR as a 
shaper of the future of work and leadership.
Key Outcomes
• HR established as a strategic driver linking 
business, technology and culture
• Shift to capability-led, purpose-driven leadership
• Emphasis on AI-enabled work redesign and 
human–machine collaboration.
THE CII HR EXCELLENCE MODEL 
The CII HR Excellence Model provides a proven 
framework to measure and advance organisational HR 
maturity across six key areas: leadership; learning and 
development; HR strategy; people engagement; 
inclusion and wellbeing; and HR processes and results. 
The 16th CII National HR Excellence Award recognised 
organisations demonstrating outstanding HR 
performance, with the model helping them 
benchmark their HR processes and practices and 
identify areas for improvement.
Puneet Chhatwal, Managing Director & CEO, The Indian Hotels 
Company Ltd at the HR Conclave in Mumbai
Suresh Narayanan, Former Chairman & Managing Director, 
Nestle India Ltd
CII worked with the Ministry of Labour and 
Employment (MoLE) and key stakeholders to support 
transition to the new framework through Industry 
engagement that addressed implementation 
challenges and helped strengthen compliance 
preparedness, particularly among micros, small and 
medium enterprises (MSMEs), to facilitate smoother 
implementation of labour codes.
CII also collaborated with national and international 
organisations like International Labour Organisation 
(ILO), International Organisation of Employers (IOE) and 
Responsible Business Alliance (RBA) on Responsible 
Business Conduct (RBC), supporting the Industry in 
aligning workplace practices with global frameworks.
Collectively, these initiatives supported the eﬀective 
rollout of the Labour Codes, contributing to improved 
ease of doing business (EoDB) and strengthened 
workers’ welfare.
INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS
AND LABOUR
Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of Labour & Employment and Youth 
Aﬀairs and Sports at India Edge in New Delhi
ADVOCACY
CII played a proactive role in supporting labour 
reforms by:
• Submitting detailed recommendations to the 
MoLE on Labour Codes to enhance clarity and 
operational feasibility across sectors, particularly 
for MSMEs
• Advocating procedural clarity to promote 
employment generation under the Pradhan Mantri 
Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana
• Engaging with Employees' Provident Fund 
Organisation for the launch and implementation 
of Employment Linked Incentive Scheme
• Advancing policy dialogue on Responsible 
Business Conduct (RBC) with the ILO on 
responsible workplace practices and labour 
standards
• Recommending working women's hostels and 
creche facilities to improve safety and mobility for 
women workers.
ACTION
CII, in partnership with the MoLE, convened a regional 
dialogue on social justice under the Global Coalition for 
Social Justice, in the presence of Gilbert F Houngbo, 
Director-General, ILO, advancing discussions on equitable 
growth, social protection and labour market inclusion.
To strengthen Responsible Business Conduct (RBC), CII, 
along with Employers Federation of India and ILO 
conducted capacity-building workshops in Chennai, Delhi 
and Pune for the manufacturing sector.
Labour and employment priorities were further 
advanced through high-impact platforms, including the 
Conference on the Future of Jobs and the ‘Learning to 
Earning: Bridging the Employability Gap’ session at the 
CII Annual Business Summit 2025 with Dr Mansukh 
Mandaviya, Minister of Labour & Employment and Youth 
Aﬀairs and Sports.
The CII National Awards for Excellence in Employee 
Relations and in Diversity, Equity and Inclusion recognised 
organisations demonstrating leadership in progressive 
workplace practices. At IndiaEdge 2025, inaugurated by 
Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, Industry leaders emphasised 
labour reforms, modernisation and skilling to advance a 
Viksit Bharat through productivity-led growth.
Internationally, CII participated at the 113th Session of 
the International Labour Conference in Geneva and led 
an Industry–trade union delegation to Japan, 
strengthening bilateral cooperation. CII also conducted 
an interaction with Dr Mansukh Mandaviya on National 
Career Service with employers in Doha, Qatar. 
Annual Report 2025-26 101
Annual Report 2025-26102
L-R: Nidhi Yadav, Brand and Marketing Head, Senior Director, India Boston Consulting Group; Bhadresh Pathak, Executive Vice President and Business 
Head L&T-SuFiN; Dipankar Mukherjee, Chief Marketing and Sales Oﬃcer, mjunction and Ankur Periwal, Managing Director, KPT Piping System at
The Business Marketing Summit 2025, in New Delhi
CII’s National Committee on Marketing Leadership, 
along with the newly constituted India Business 
Marketing Forum, comprised Chief Marketing 
Oﬃcers (CMOs) and senior marketing leaders 
representing leading national brands. Together, they 
drove a range of initiatives aimed at advancing 
marketing excellence and strengthening leadership 
capability across the CII Membership.
MARKETING LEADERSHIP
ADVOCACY
The activities of both these bodies focused on 
strengthening marketers’ capabilities through 
targeted interventions, while laying the groundwork 
for enabling marketing leaders to conﬁdently 
navigate evolving challenges and emerging market 
complexities.
ACTION
CII organised the 9th edition of the Marketing Leadership 
Summit, which brought together India’s leading 
marketing practitioners and thought leaders to 
deliberate on the evolving mandate of CMOs and the 
strategic imperatives of resilience, relevance and 
reinvention in a rapidly changing business 
environment.
In a signiﬁcant step towards strengthening the B2B 
marketing ecosystem, CII constituted the Indian 
Business Marketing Forum (IBMF) - a one-of-a-kind 
platform dedicated to business marketing in India. 
Chaired by Madhav Singhania, Joint Managing 
Director & CEO, JK Cement Limited, the Forum 
brought together 25 eminent business marketing 
professionals. 
CII also organised the maiden Business Marketing 
Summit, which provided a strategic platform for 
Industry leaders to exchange insights, share real-world 
best practices and explore how business marketing 
can act as a catalyst for growth, innovation and 
competitiveness in an evolving Indian marketplace.
To build future-ready marketing leadership, CII 
organised the Certiﬁed Next-Gen Marketing 
Leadership Programme to enable marketers to master 
strategic and digital-ﬁrst marketing approaches, build 
agile and growth-oriented marketing organisations 
and develop leadership capabilities aligned with 
emerging challenges. Supported by rigorous 
assessments and continuous progress monitoring, the 
programme witnessed strong participation from CII’s 
Membership.
SECTORSCAPE
Agriculture, Food Processing, Fisheries,
Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Manufacturing
Infrastructure
Defence and Aerospace
Energy
Fast Moving Consumer Goods
Services
Indian Digital Gaming Society
Design
Health and Lifesciences
Education
AGRICULTURE, FOOD
PROCESSING, FISHERIES,
ANIMAL HUSBANDRY & DAIRYING
The CII National Council on Agriculture advocated 
strengthening Farmer Producer Organisations 
(FPOs), improving agri-food procurement, export 
eﬃciency and promoting sustainable value chains.
ADVOCACY
CII Food and Agriculture Centre of Excellence’s 
(CII-FACE) pre-budget deliberations proposed reforms 
across the agri value chain, including stronger FPOs 
through priority-sector credit, Kisan Credit Card 
interest subvention, a dedicated support fund and 
easier mandi licensing. To reduce market distortions, 
recommendations covered rationalisation of 
Minimum Support Price, stable export policies, 
phasing out stock limits and better inter-ministerial 
coordination. The agenda also backed private-led agri 
R&D, seed exports, fertiliser reforms and Product 
Linked Incentive support for agrochemicals.
L - R: Rajesh Srivastav, Chairman, Prowess Advisors; Dr Sudhanshu, Secretary, APEDA; Salil Singhal, Chairman Emeritus, PI Industries; Devesh Chaturvedi, 
Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; Sanjay Sacheti, Co-Chairman, CII National Council on Agriculture and Country Head, Olam Agro, 
and K R Ramalingam, General Manager, NABARD at the FPO Summit in New Delhi
ACTION 
The CII FPO Summit highlighted the role of FPOs in 
strengthening India’s agricultural ﬁrst mile. With 
over 150 stakeholders, discussions focused on 
capacity building, governance, market readiness, 
digital and precision technologies, partnerships and 
sustained policy support to improve farmer incomes 
and enhance FPO competitiveness.
The Agri-Carbon Dialogue brought together 
policymakers, Industry, researchers, startups and 
international organisations to discuss opportunities 
carbon markets present in advancing climate action 
in agriculture. Key themes included value chain 
integration, Monitoring, Reporting, and Veriﬁcation 
(MRV) systems, sustainable ﬁnance, digital 
technologies and trends in voluntary
carbon markets.
Annual Report 2025-26 105
FOOD PROCESSING
The CII National Committee on Food Processing 
Industries works towards advancing regulatory 
reforms, export competitiveness and sustainability, 
aligning with CII’s broader initiatives across agriculture, 
nutrition, environment, FMCGs and MSMEs.
ADVOCACY
GST POLICY ADVOCACY
CII-FACE undertook targeted policy advocacy for GST 
rationalisation in the food processing sector by 
submitting chapter-wise, evidence-based 
recommendations to the GST Council and the Ministry 
of Food Processing Industries. This supported the 
development of a simpler, more predictable and 
sector-aligned tax framework, helping reduce 
compliance complexity, ease working-capital 
constraints and improve investor conﬁdence.
POLICY RECOMMENDATIONS:
CII INDIA EDGE 2025
At CII India Edge 2025, policy recommendations were 
presented to the Secretary, Ministry of Food 
Processing Industries (MoFPI), that included a Model 
Food Processing Policy to create a uniform national 
framework, the establishment of a Citrus Development 
ACTION 
Following GST Council reforms announced in 
September, CII-FACE, in partnership with MoFPI, 
organised a CEO Roundtable on GST 2.0 in New Delhi, 
Board to strengthen processing and export of citrus 
products, the creation of a dedicated agro-processing 
ﬁnancial institution to support MSMEs and the 
expansion of food processing clusters through a 
national zero-waste value-addition programme.
STREAMLINING FOOD REGULATIONS:
KEY FSSAI INITIATIVES
Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) 
approved regulatory reforms to improve ease of 
doing business while safeguarding food safety. These 
include revised registration and licensing thresholds, 
exemption of eligible street vendors, automatic 
registration, introduction of a perpetual licensing 
regime and adoption of a risk-based inspection 
system. Compliance was further simpliﬁed through 
rationalised record-keeping norms, retention of 
First-in-First-out (FIFO) as a recommended best 
practice, integration with the Department for 
Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade’s National 
Single Window System and extension of the labelling 
compliance timeline from 180 to 365 days.
L-R: Jayen Mehta, MD, Gujarat Co-operative Milk Marketing Federation Ltd; Chirag Paswan, Minister of Food Processing Industries; Piruz Khambatta, 
Chairman, CII National Committee on Taxation and Chairman & MD, Rasna International and AP Das Joshi, Secretary, Ministry of Food Processing 
Industries at the Interactive Session on Next Gen GST Reforms in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26106
FISHERIES, ANIMAL 
HUSBANDRY AND DAIRYING
The animal husbandry, dairying and ﬁsheries sectors 
are critical to India’s rural livelihoods, food security, 
and employment, particularly for marginal farmers 
and women. The CII National Committee on Animal 
Husbandry & Dairying advanced strategic initiatives 
and policy advocacy to enhance productivity, 
sustainability and smallholder support.
ADVOCACY
Recommendations to Department of Animal 
Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD) called for modernising 
veterinary education by aligning Bachelor of 
Veterinary Science and Animal Husbandry (BVSc & AH) 
curricula with the World Organisation for Animal 
Health (WOAH) core framework, integrating One 
Health, epidemiology, food safety and public health. 
Proposals included species-speciﬁc specialisation, 
stronger clinical and Industry exposure, faculty 
upskilling through a National Veterinary Teaching & 
Learning Academy, upgraded labs and digital 
platforms and targeted research support on 
anti-microbial resistance (AMR), vaccines, climate 
resilience and digital extension.
ACTION 
CII-FACE, in partnership with Indian Federation of 
Animal Health Companies (INFAH), launched the AMR 
Stewardship Drive as a four-session national outreach 
programme.
The initiative focused on responsible antimicrobial 
use, biosecurity, improving point of care diagnostics 
and AMR surveillance. The Drive strengthened 
multi-stakeholder partnerships, youth engagement 
and reinforced a coordinated One Health approach to 
address antimicrobial resistance in dairy, poultry and 
ﬁsheries sector. 
CII-FACE led a business delegation to Maldives to 
strengthen cooperation in agriculture and food 
processing. Engagements with senior ministers, 
oﬃcials and a India-Maldives Business Meet explored 
partnerships across agribusiness, animal husbandry, 
poultry, ﬁsheries, ﬂoriculture and coconut value 
chains. Field visits to key agriculture centres 
highlighted opportunities for Industry collaboration, 
technology exchange and capacity building, 
reinforcing India–Maldives cooperation.
chaired by Shri Chirag Paswan, Minister, MoFPI.
The session brought together around 40 CEOs from 
leading food processing companies to discuss tax 
rationalisation, sector-speciﬁc implications and 
implementation challenges.
An interactive session on ‘Enabling Investments, 
Employment & Growth’ was held in Patna in October, 
with over 100 participants from food processing, 
agri-enterprises, MSMEs and investors chaired by Shri 
Chirag Paswan, Minister, MoFPI. Deliberations covered 
GST rationalisation, investment and jobs and Bihar’s 
growing role in food processing, including initiatives like 
the proposed Makhana Board and National Institute of 
Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management 
(NIFTEM), strengthening Industry–Government 
collaboration for inclusive growth.
STATE CONNECT is a joint initiative with FSSAI and 
State Food and Drug Administration (FDAs) to 
strengthen food safety systems and improve State 
Food Safety Index performance. It brings together 
Central and State regulators, Food Business Operators 
(FBOs), SMEs, Hotel, Restaurant and Catering sectors 
(HoReCa) and other stakeholders to address sectoral 
challenges, align with global trade practices and 
promote collaboration. During the year, three State 
Connect sessions were held in Uttar Pradesh, 
Maharashtra and Delhi.
