pages.text:
Annual Report 2025-26108
MANUFACTURING
Manufacturing is at the core of India’s long-term growth 
and strategic autonomy and is a central pillar of the 
Government’s Viksit Bharat@2047 vision, driving 
productivity-led competitiveness, resilient global value 
chain integration, creation of global ‘Made in India’ 
champions, large-scale skilled employment and inclusive 
development across states, with the potential to raise 
manufacturing’s contribution to over 25% of GDP and 
position India among the world’s leading hubs for 
advanced manufacturing.
The CII Council on Manufacturing Excellence advanced a 
focused agenda on competitiveness, innovation, 
sustainability and global integration to support India’s 
emergence as a global manufacturing hub. Special focus 
was placed on emerging, high-potential sectors such as 
leather, footwear, furniture and tyres to support the wider 
manufacturing ecosystem.
ADVOCACY
• Working with NITI Aayog’s High-Level Committee on 
Non-Financial Regulatory Reforms (HLC-NFRR), CII 
ﬂagged Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) compliance 
burdens on footwear MSMEs and proposed 
production-linked fees, ‘One Unit–One BIS’, annual 
audits, graded penalties and simpliﬁed procedures, 
potentially reducing costs by 15–20%
• CII recommended Production Linked Incentive (PLI) 
schemes with lower investment thresholds for 
employment-intensive sectors such as leather, 
footwear and furniture.
ACTION
In partnership with NITI Aayog, CII anchored the 
advanced manufacturing agenda through the joint 
release of ‘Reimagining Manufacturing: India’s 
Roadmap to Global Leadership in Advanced 
Manufacturing’, outlining a sector-focused strategy to 
deploy frontier technologies for sustained 
manufacturing growth. This was complemented by a 
research study on the impact assessment of 14 PLI 
sectors, alongside recommendations for 11 sectors 
for the next phase of PLI, supporting a more targeted 
and eﬀective industrial policy framework.
CII also advanced policy learning through international 
outreach, facilitating a smart manufacturing 
delegation to the USA and a business delegation on 
Manufacturing Excellence to Germany, focused on 
advanced technologies, sustainability and supply-chain 
resilience. 
CII launched the inaugural edition of the National Best 
Practices Award on Future Ready Manufacturing. 
These awards recognised the eﬀorts by Industry and 
measured the outcomes achieved in adopting 
future-ready technologies and technology solutions in 
their manufacturing processes, thus encouraging 
organisations to accelerate continuous improvement 
in manufacturing.
L - R: Narayan Sethuramon, Co-Chairman, International Council and Trade Policy Council, CII and Managing Director, Sanmar Matrix Metals Ltd; Salil 
Singhal, Chairman, CII Indian Chemicals and Petrochemicals Conference and Member, SCALE and Chairman Emeritus, PI Industries; Piyush Goyal, Minister 
of Commerce and Industry; R Mukundan, President Designate, CII and Chairman, CII National Committee on Chemicals and Petrochemicals and Managing 
Director & CEO, TATA Chemicals Ltd and Chandrajit Banerjee, Director General, CII at ICPC in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26 109
CHEMICALS AND 
PETROCHEMICALS 
The CII National Committee on Chemicals and 
Petrochemicals worked on competitiveness, 
sustainability and long-term growth, with policy 
advocacy aimed at strengthening domestic 
manufacturing, expanding exports and addressing 
regulatory and trade barriers.
ADVOCACY
• CII highlighted high compliance costs and weak 
testing capacity, recommending a Remission of Duties 
and Taxes on Exported Products (RoDTEP ) increase 
for chemicals to 2–3%, full digitalisation of approvals, 
trackable grievance redressal, third-party inspections 
and self-declaration-based licence renewals
• In consultations chaired by the Joint Secretary 
(Chemicals), CII advocated phased, globally aligned 
rollout of upcoming Quality Control Orders 
(QCOs) with clear timelines and prior assessment 
of testing capacity to avoid supply disruptions, 
especially for MSMEs.
ACTION
CII organised the 7th Indian Chemicals and 
Petrochemicals Conference (ICPC), focused on 
positioning India as a globally competitive chemicals 
hub and released the report ‘People Powering 
Progress: Building India’s Chemical Workforce for a 
USD 1 Trillion Industry by 2040’. The report outlines a 
comprehensive roadmap, identifying skills as a critical 
enabler of innovation, safety and sustainable growth.
CONSUMER ELECTRONICS 
AND DURABLES
The CII National Committee on Consumer Electronics 
and Durables worked on strengthening domestic 
demand, deepening the component and raw material 
base, rationalising and streamlining Quality Control 
Orders, improving export competitiveness, 
accelerating digital adoption and promoting 
sustainability. 
ADVOCACY
• CII highlighted near-term shortages in domestic 
inner grooved copper tubes (IGT) availability and 
sought a one-year, time-bound extension of the 
existing import clariﬁcation to bridge the gap 
despite planned capacity additions
• CII ﬂagged that nearly 50 million room Air 
Conditioners (ACs) were over 10 years old and 
recommended a structured framework to replace 
ineﬃcient units with higher-rated Bureau of 
Energy Eﬃciency (BEE) models.
ACTION
CII organised closed-door consultations with the 
Government to address critical issues such as reducing 
import dependency, shaping the next phase of 
incentives under PLI 2.0 and advancing proposals for 
dedicated electronics export parks. In addition, CII 
closely engaged with BEE to advance energy 
eﬃciency initiatives across the sector.
Chandrajit Banerjee, Director General, CII; Debjani Ghosh, Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog; B V R Subrahmanyam, Former CEO, NITI Aayog; Devendra 
Fadnavis, Chief Minister of Maharashtra; Late Ajit Pawar, then Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra, amongst dignitaries unveiling NITI Aayog Frontier 
Tech Hub’s roadmap ‘Reimagining Manufacturing: India’s Roadmap to Global Leadership in Advanced Manufacturing’ in Pune
A leading manufacturing company being felicitated by Suman Bery, Vice 
Chairman, NITI Aayog. Also present is Rajiv Memani, President CII and 
Regional Managing Partner of EY Africa India region, Chair – EY Growth 
Markets Council at the Annual Business Session in New Delhi
MINING
The CII National Committee on Mining worked 
towards positioning the sector as a global leader by 
promoting private participation in critical and rare 
minerals, supporting import substitution for clean 
energy transition and advocating for policy reforms 
aligned with the National Critical Mineral Mission.
ADVOCACY
• CII suggested linking iron ore average sale price 
(ASP) under Mineral Concession Rules (MCR) with 
international prices/indices to align with global 
practices
• CII recommended intermediary timelines in the 
Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2015 to speed up 
operationalisation of auctioned blocks
• CII proposed amendments to enable viable 
recovery of associated critical minerals and 
inclusion of contiguous areas in leases for 
scientiﬁc mining of deep-seated minerals.
ELECTRONICS 
The CII National Committee on Electronics 
Manufacturing focused on strengthening domestic 
value chains, promoting product and intellectual 
property (IP) ownership and enabling startups and 
MSMEs to position India as a trusted global 
manufacturing and innovation hub.
ADVOCACY
• CII advocated moving beyond assembly-led 
manufacturing to indigenous product design and 
ownership, stronger component manufacturing and 
capital equipment ecosystems
• CII focused on improving market access and 
procurement, while addressing standards, testing, 
logistics, free trade sgreements (FTAs) and timely 
incentives to boost export competitiveness
• CII provided inputs to ensure clear, non-overlapping 
regulations, protect consumer data and safety and to 
adopt evidence-based compliance.
ACTION
CII advanced stakeholder-led policy consensus 
building by leveraging the 8th CII Electronics Summit 
as a strategic platform to drive advocacy on advanced 
manufacturing, design-led product development, 
startup-driven innovation and export-led growth. 
Deliberations across thematic sessions consolidated 
Industry perspectives on value-chain deepening, 
design ownership and export readiness, which were 
subsequently reﬂected in CII’s policy representations 
to the Government.
GEMS AND JEWELLERY
The CII Task Force on Gems and Jewellery is 
committed to strengthening India’s leadership by 
driving innovation, promoting sustainability and 
embedding consumer conﬁdence at the heart of its 
growth journey.
ADVOCACY
• CII advocated for the introduction of bullion 
hallmarking to ensure purity and quality of raw 
materials for manufacturers and retailers across the 
gems and jewellery value chain; stronger consumer 
protection and quality assurance measures in the 
rapidly growing silver jewellery segment
• Diamond nomenclature standards for clarity and 
consistency, standardised lab-grown diamonds and 
studded jewellery certiﬁcations were advocated to 
ensure authenticity, clarity and consumer awareness.
ACTION
CII organised the Conference on Gems and Jewellery, 
which served as a platform for Industry–Government 
dialogue on hallmarking reforms, transparency, 
consumer protection, sustainability and the adoption 
of emerging technologies.
Annual Report 2025-26110
SEMICONDUCTORS
The CII Task Force on Semiconductors focused on 
strengthening domestic demand, enabling end-to-end 
value chains, addressing raw material and 
infrastructure bottlenecks and improving cost and 
ease of doing business.
ADVOCACY
• CII advocated leveraging anchor sectors - electric 
vehicles, 5G, data centres, defence, space and 
Internet of Things (IoT) to convert India’s 
electronics market into sustained semiconductor 
demand, while strengthening design, system 
integration, product ownership and cost 
competitiveness across fabs and ATMP/OSAT 
(Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging/ 
Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test)
• CII focused on building end-to-end semiconductor 
supply chains through customs and Harmonised 
System of Nomenclature (HSN) reforms, 
Manufacturing and Other Operations in 
Warehouse Regulations (MOOWR) extension, 
domestic capabilities in materials, gases, 
chemicals, equipment, stronger infrastructure, 
testing, certiﬁcation and skilling around 
semiconductor hubs.
ACTION 
CII advanced semiconductor policy advocacy through 
stakeholder-led Industry-Government dialogues to 
build consensus on demand-side interventions, raw 
material strategies and ecosystem gaps. Based on 
consultations with Industry, startups and academia,
CII submitted recommendations covering 
demand-creation levers, design-PLI support, R&D 
incentives, semiconductor Special Economic Zones 
(SEZs), customs and GST reforms and targeted 
support for ATMP/OSAT and MSMEs.
SMART MANUFACTURING
CII National Committee on Smart Manufacturing 
actively collaborated with key stakeholders to 
encourage widespread adoption of smart 
manufacturing practices, with particular emphasis on 
empowering MSMEs.
ADVOCACY
• CII advocated making advanced manufacturing a 
core focus under the National Manufacturing 
Mission to accelerate adoption of cutting-edge 
practices and improve productivity, quality and 
energy eﬃciency
• CII recommended developing mega clusters with 
plug-and-play infrastructure, testing and validation 
labs, R&D facilities and common utilities to lower 
entry barriers and enable rapid capacity creation.
ACTION 
CII organised the Smart Manufacturing Summit, 
focusing on key themes such as MSME digital 
enablement, Industry-led skilling and scaling 
technology adoption. Complementing policy dialogue, 
CII strengthened on-ground capabilities through 
capacity-building programmes, covering over 200 
professionals.
STEEL
The CII National Committee on Steel focused on 
enhancing sector competitiveness by addressing raw 
material availability, increasing steel intensity across 
key user sectors and advancing sustainable steel 
production to build a self-reliant steel Industry.
ADVOCACY
• Before NITI Aayog’s HLC-NFRR , CII ﬂagged delays 
in forest clearance (FC) transfers due to 
post-compliance approvals and pending 
compensatory aﬀorestation notiﬁcations, 
advocating faster FC transfers and timely state 
action to avoid project and capacity delays
• CII recommended expediting iron ore auctions in 
Jharkhand and Odisha, rationalising royalty payments 
and allowing third-party conversion to improve 
availability and reduce costs for the steel sector.
ACTION 
CII organised the India Mining Summit as an 
Industry-led dialogue highlighting the strategic role of 
critical minerals in India’s clean energy and 
manufacturing sectors and calling for policy incentives, 
streamlined regulations, advanced mining and 
processing technologies, public–private partnerships 
and R&D in exploration, recycling and recovery.
Annual Report 2025-26 111
L-R: Jayant Acharya, Co-Chairman, CII National Committee on Steel and 
Joint Managing Director & CEO, JSW Steel Ltd; Sandeep Poundrik, 
Secretary, Ministry of Steel; Koushik Chatterjee, Co-Chairman, CII 
National Committee on Steel and ED & CFO, Tata Steel Ltd at the CII 
Steel Summit in New Delhi
ACTION 
CII submitted a granular report to the Government 
recommending measures to make beneﬁciation 
economically viable, ensure raw material security for 
non-captive and secondary producers and provide 
carbon price assurance to enable large-scale green 
investments. CII also organised the Steel Summit as a 
platform to advance consensus on specialty steel 
development, quality standards, skilling, smart 
manufacturing and supportive frameworks for green 
procurement, carbon markets and transition ﬁnance 
to build a sustainable and globally competitive steel 
ecosystem aligned with Viksit Bharat.
L-R: Giriraj Singh, Minister of Textiles; Kulin Lalbhai, Chairman, CII National Committee on Textiles & Apparels and Vice Chairman, Arvind Ltd; Neelam 
Shami Rao, Secretary, Ministry of Textiles; Rohit Kansal, then Additional Secretary, Ministry of Textiles at a high-level Industry interaction with the 
Ministry of Textiles in New Delhi
TEXTILES & APPAREL
The CII National Committee on Textiles and Apparel 
focused on market access, raw material competitiveness, 
sustainable infrastructure and ease of doing business 
reforms to drive Industry growth.
ADVOCACY
• CII recommended removing the 11% cotton duty 
and eliminating QCOs on key polyester and viscose 
inputs to align domestic prices with global levels 
and address raw material gaps
• CII sought a uniform 5% GST on apparel across price 
points and ﬁbres; this was partially accepted with 
garments up to INR 2500, brought under 5% GST
• CII advocated a 55–60 hour work week, nationwide 
ﬁxed-term contracts and rationalised overtime 
wages at 1.5 times to unlock scale, productivity 
and global competitiveness in garmenting.
ACTION 
CII organised TEXCON’25 which served as a platform 
for value-chain collaboration and dialogue on global 
supply chain integration, man-made ﬁbre (MMF) 
ecosystem development and competitiveness through 
innovation, AI, speed and sustainability.
Annual Report 2025-26112

L-R: Dr Alok Kumar Srivastava, Director General, National Test House, 
Department of Consumer Aﬀairs, Ministry of Consumer Aﬀairs, Food & 
Public Distribution; R Mukundan, President Designate, CII and Managing 
Director & CEO of Tata Chemicals Ltd; Rajesh Agrawal, Special Secretary, 
Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry at the First 
Meeting of CII Associations Council in New Delhi
The CII Associations’ Council (ASCON) brings together 106 national sectoral associations representing 
over 75,000 companies, serving as a unifying platform to strengthen collaboration among Industry 
bodies and amplify the collective voice of Indian Industry. ASCON enables coordinated policy advocacy, 
cross-sector dialogue and inclusive growth, contributing to a more competitive and resilient economy.
ADVOCACY
CII-ASCON played a central role in strengthening coordinated Industry advocacy by aggregating sectoral 
inputs from national and sectoral associations and translating them into structured, evidence-based 
policy representations. ASCON facilitated focused deliberations with senior Industry leaders and 
policymakers on key issues impacting competitiveness and long-term growth.
A key outcome was the consolidation of ASCON’s annual agenda through four dedicated Working Groups 
on competitiveness, technology, ﬁnance & taxation and sustainability, which functioned as 
action-oriented think tanks. These Working Groups aggregated Industry feedback on GST, direct tax and 
compliance-related challenges; advanced recommendations to improve access to ﬁnance-particularly for 
MSMEs; examined mechanisms to enhance utilisation of R&D funding and ﬁnancial incentives; and 
advocated the adoption of energy eﬃciency measures, ESG frameworks and sustainable manufacturing 
practices. The consolidated inputs were submitted as coordinated policy representations to relevant 
Ministries and regulatory authorities, enhancing the credibility, coherence and impact of Industry 
advocacy within the CII framework.
ASSOCIATIONS’ COUNCIL (ASCON)
R Mukundan and Rajat Kumar Saini, CEO & MD, NICDC at the 
Second Meeting of CII Associations Council in Gurugram

Annual Report 2025-26114
L-R: Dr Suchitra K Ella, Vice President, CII and Co-Founder & Managing 
Director, Bharat Biotech International Ltd; Kinjarapu Rammohan 
Naidu, Minister of Civil Aviation; Samir Kumar Sinha, Secretary, 
Ministry of Civil Aviation at the 2nd CII International Conference and 
Exhibition on Aerospace Manufacturing in Visakhapatnam
INFRASTRUCTURE
The CII Infrastructure Council and its specialised 
committees and Task Forces played a pivotal role in 
advancing India’s infrastructure transformation in 
alignment with the national vision of Viksit 
Bharat@2047. The Council drove critical structural 
reforms across the infrastructure value chain, 
including GST rationalisation for business 
infrastructure, revitalisation of the Public–Private 
Partnership (PPP) framework and 
institutionalisation of digital and single-window 
approval mechanisms to reduce friction, cost and 
time across the project lifecycle.
These reforms were facilitated through sustained 
engagements with senior policymakers and 
regulators, including Shri Nitin Gadkari, Minister of 
Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH); Shri 
Ashwini Vaishnaw, Minister of Railways, 
Communications & Electronics & Information 
Technology; Shri Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu, 
Minister of Civil Aviation; Shri V Somanna, Minister 
of State for Ministry of Railways and Shri Shantanu 
Thakur, Minister of State for Ministry of Ports, 
Shipping and Waterways ensuring alignment 
between Industry priorities and national policy 
objectives.
Through ﬁve sectoral knowledge publications and 
several high-level dialogues, CII engaged over 1200 
leaders and featured insights from over 300 
policymakers and domain experts, laying a resilient 
foundation for long-term economic transformation 
in India’s infrastructure ecosystem. A new Task 
Force on Elevators and Escalators & Building 
Technology was also constituted to promote the 
development of a safe, accessible and future-ready 
ecosystem with a focus on technology adoption, 
regulatory strengthening of sustainable and 
inclusive urban infrastructure.
AVIATION, AEROSPACE AND 
ADVANCED AIR MOBILITY 
India’s aviation and aerospace ecosystem is undergoing 
a structural transformation as new technologies, 
innovative platforms and global integration reshape the 
future of air travel, mobility and aerospace 
manufacturing.
ADVOCACY
• CII engaged with the Ministry of Civil Aviation 
(MoCA) to build a competitive aerospace and 
Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) 
ecosystem through speciﬁc policy 
recommendations including development of 
aerospace clusters, ﬁscal and tax incentives, 
promotion of Original Equipment Manufacturer 
(OEM) partnerships, skill development, certiﬁcation 
reforms to enhance indigenisation, MSME 
participation and global competitiveness
• CII advocated for advanced air mobility to MoCA, 
focusing on electric vertical take-oﬀ and landing 
(eVTOL) certiﬁcation, advanced air mobility pilots, 
drone integration, infrastructure and air traﬃc 
frameworks, manufacturing, skilling, ﬁnancing 
and global regulatory alignment for scalable adoption.
Ashwini Vaishnaw, Minister of Railways, Information & Broadcasting 
and Electronics & Information Technology at the CII International Rail 
Conference in New Delhi
URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND
SMART CITIES 
India’s urban development and smart cities ecosystem 
is at a pivotal juncture, where emerging technologies, 
integrated planning and sustainable infrastructure are 
reshaping the future of urban mobility, governance and 
livable city spaces. 
ADVOCACY
Aligned with Viksit Bharat@2047, CII championed the 
strengthening of urban governance, investment 
frameworks and sustainable city development through 
innovative urban ﬁnancing and the Urban Challenge 
Fund in consultation with the Government.
ACTION 
CII advanced sectoral outcomes through two ﬂagship 
initiatives organised with MoCA:
• The 2nd International Conference and Exhibition 
on Aerospace Manufacturing, held in collaboration 
with the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers, 
enabled focused dialogue on strengthening 
aerospace manufacturing and MRO, highlighting 
Andhra Pradesh’s aerospace ecosystem and policy 
priorities across skilling, research & development 
(R&D), certiﬁcation infrastructure, advanced 
manufacturing and global supply chain 
integration. Addressing the conference, 
Shri Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu underscored 
India’s transition from an aircraft buyer to a global 
aerospace and MRO hub
• The International Conference and Exhibition on Air 
Mobility, organised as part of Bharat Mobility 
Global Expo, advanced India’s future air mobility 
agenda through discussions on regulatory 
readiness, infrastructure planning, ﬁnancing, 
skilling and manufacturing for drones and eVTOLs, 
reinforcing pathways for safe, sustainable and 
globally competitive air mobility solutions.
RAILWAYS 
India’s railway sector is undergoing a profound 
transformation, emerging as a cornerstone of 
sustainable economic growth, technological innovation 
and inclusive connectivity.
ADVOCACY 
CII advanced India’s railway transformation through 
sustained advocacy and strategic engagement with 
the Ministry of Railways, channelled via the Railway 
Council (formerly CII Rail Transportation and 
Equipment Division) and its six dedicated working 
groups. Key policy interventions focused on the 
development of high-speed rail corridors, achieving 
Net Zero emissions by 2030, digitalisation, safety 
enhancements such as Kavach, multimodal integration, 
ﬁnancing reforms and strengthening Industry– 
Academia partnerships for skill development and R&D.
ACTION 
• CII organised the 3rd edition of the Rail Connect 
Conference, which addressed multimodal integration, 
investment opportunities and policy reforms. CII 
also convened a high-level roundtable on
 high-speed rail corridors, advancing evidence-based 
recommendations on corridor prioritisation, 
indigenisation, ﬁnancing models and multimodal 
integration
• CII strengthened global cooperation through the CII 
International Rail Conference (IRC), organised alongside 
the 16th edition of the International Railway Equipment 
Exhibition. The conference witnessed the launch of the 
CII–ATO report ‘On the Right Track? A State of Play for 
Railways in Asia and the Paciﬁc, with a Spotlight on 
India’ by Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw and the CII 
Compendium on ‘Technological Success Stories in 
Indian Railways’ by Shri Satish Kumar, Chairman of 
Railway Board respectively, alongside the signing of an 
MoU with Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya. Bilateral 
cooperation was reinforced through the Indo-German 
Industry Roundtable on Urban Rail with Gesellschaft für 
Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ). CII also facilitated 
the Indian Railways delegation to EXCON 2025.
Annual Report 2025-26 115
ACTION
The report ‘Urban India and the Road to Viksit Bharat’, 
launched during the Conference on Exploring Urban 
Dynamics: Outlook 2030, outlined a forward-looking 
framework for sustainable, inclusive and future-ready 
urban development.
At the conference, Smt D Thara, Additional Secretary, 
Ministry of Housing and Urban Aﬀairs (MoHUA) 
highlighted the need for deeper alignment on priority 
urban reform themes.
REAL ESTATE AND HOUSING 
The real estate and housing landscape in India is 
evolving rapidly, shaped by policy reforms, technological 
adoption and inclusive development approaches that 
are redeﬁning urban living and housing solutions. 
ADVOCACY
CII submitted recommendations to the Government 
on Real Estate Investment Trusts/ Infrastructure 
Investment Trusts (REITs/InvITs), land pooling and a 
broader real estate policy, with a focus on sustainable 
and Net Zero buildings, emerging technologies, 
investment-friendly reforms, workplace 
transformation and future-ready urban infrastructure.
ACTION
• A report on ‘Indian Real Estate 2030: Technology, 
Sustainability, and Growth’ was launched during 
the 5th edition of the Real Estate & Building 
Technology (REBT) Conference, which informed 
forward-looking policy discussions on sustainable 
construction, emerging technologies, green 
buildings and inclusive urban development
• An interactive session with Shri Srinivas Katikithala, 
Secretary, MoHUA, brought together senior 
Industry leaders to deliberate on policy 
interventions, regulatory frameworks and 
strategies for advancing India’s urban 
development and real estate sector
• A report titled ‘Commercial Real Estate: Potential 
is Built, Opportunity is Now’ was launched during 
the Conference on Evolving Landscape of Indian 
Real Estate, shaping policy discussions on 
investment opportunities, regulatory reforms, 
technology adoption, evolving workplace models 
and sustainable, future-ready growth of India’s 
commercial real estate sector.
ROADS AND HIGHWAYS
The CII National Committee on Roads and Highways 
continued to focus on the 3S framework - Safety, 
Sustainability and Smart Roads. Members deliberated 
on concrete steps to improve road safety, ensure 
fairer contracts with shared risk, reduce disputes and 
leverage technology with the overarching objective of 
improving the quality of roads and highways and 
making them safer, smarter and more sustainable.
ADVOCACY
CII recommended safety enhancement, deﬁning Smart 
Roads, improving Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) and 
revitalising PPPs and GST application in the roads 
sector. To build consensus on a nationally relevant 
evolving deﬁnition of Smart Roads, top policymakers 
and Industry leaders from various sectors including 
Shri Nitin Gadkari and Shri V Umashankar, Secretary, 
MoRTH inaugurated the CII initiative on Smart Roads 
at the Conference on Future of Smart Roads.
ACTION
• The Conference on the Future of Smart Roads was 
organised where Shri Nitin Gadkari shared his 
thoughts on maintaining accountability and 
transparency during construction of world-class 
highways
• CII initiated state-level road safety deliberations, 
with special emphasis on two-wheeler safety, 
including a discussion in Gujarat on ‘Raising the Bar 
of Safety for Two-Wheeler and Bike Taxis in 
Gujarat’ as a part of its dialogue on ‘How to 
Building Last Mile Connectivity’.
L - R: Jagdish Kadam, Vice Chair, CII National Committee on Roads & 
Highways and CMD, Rajpath Infrastructure; Nitin Gadkari, Minister of 
Road Transport & Highways; Vinayak Pai, Chairman, CII National 
Committee on Roads & Highways and CEO & MD, Tata Projects and 
Chandrajit Banerjee, Director General, CII at the Future of Smart Roads 
in India in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26116
DEFENCE AND
AEROSPACE
DEFENCE AND AEROSPACE
India’s defence and aerospace sector has transitioned 
from import dependence to an innovation-led 
manufacturing ecosystem under Atmanirbhar Bharat. 
In FY25, defence production reached a record INR 1.54 
lakh crore, supported by over 16,000 MSMEs and 788 
industrial licences issued to 462 companies. Indigenous 
defence production stood at INR 1,27,434 crore in 
FY24, marking a 174% increase from FY15. Defence 
exports hit a record INR 23,622 crore in FY25, reaching 
over 100 countries.
Aligned with this national momentum, CII, through its 
dedicated defence arm, Society of Indian Defence 
Manufacturers (SIDM), played a catalytic role by 
leading over 100 high-impact initiatives. These 
engagements connected the Armed Forces, Industry, 
MSMEs, startups, Academia and global partners to 
advance self-reliance, operational readiness and 
India’s emergence as a credible defence 
manufacturing and export hub.
ADVOCACY
CII focused on improving ease of doing business, 
accelerating procurement and enhancing export- 
readiness. Key contributions included structured 
inputs to the review of Defence Acquisition Procedure 
(DAP) 2020, addressing simpliﬁed procurement 
categories, faster timelines, incentives for indigenous 
design and development, balanced Intellectual 
Property (IP) frameworks and support for critical 
technologies and exports.
CII also advocated for the transition of trial 
procedures from No Cost No Commitment (NCNC) to 
Full Cost No Commitment (FCNC), rationalisation of 
Quality Assurance (QA) processes, ease of payment 
and surety norms and streamlining of export licensing. 
Additional inputs covered recognition of 
India-designed semiconductors manufactured abroad, 
improved ﬁnancing and testing access for MSMEs and 
recommendations on the proposed Military 
Airworthiness Bill.
L-R: Rajinder Singh Bhatia, Immediate Past President, SIDM and Chairman, Defence Business, Kalyani Group; Rajnath Singh, Raksha Mantri; Rajesh Kumar 
Singh, Secretary, Ministry of Defence and SP Shukla, Past President, SIDM at the SIDM Annual Session & Champion Awards in New Delhi

Delegation Visit to Brussels, Belgium
ACTION
CII’s policy and ecosystem interventions translated 
into clear outcomes. A key milestone was the East 
Tech Symposium in Ranchi, jointly organised with HQ 
Eastern Command that featured over 175 exhibitors, 
400 delegates and participation from Armed Forces 
procurement directorates. Strengthening MSME 
integration and advanced dual-use innovation, the 
event facilitated more than 300 B2G meetings, 
aligning Industry capabilities with operational needs.
During ‘Operation Sindoor’, CII enabled rapid Industry 
mobilisation through capability demonstrations, 
urgent vendor interactions and direct engagement 
with Service Headquarters, resulting in expedited 
induction of indigenous Unmanned Aerial Systems 
(UAS), ammunition and critical spares. This was 
reinforced by the establishment of an SIDM Extension 
Oﬃce at the Indian Army HQ in New Delhi and 
in-principle acceptance of the proposal for a National 
Mission on Military Unmanned Systems.
Internationally, CII led over 40 outreach initiatives to 
enhance market access and defence supply-chain 
integration. A major milestone was leading an Indian 
Defence Industry delegation to Brussels in December, 
supported by the Ministry of External Aﬀairs (MEA) 
and the Embassy of India. The visit positioned India as 
a trusted long-term defence industrial partner for 
Europe and advanced collaboration in 
co-development, co-production and joint IP creation 
within emerging European defence value chains.
Annual Report 2025-26118
ENERGY
BIOENERGY
Aligned with its Net Zero 2070 commitment, India’s 
bioenergy sector is poised for a four- to six-fold 
growth by 2030, driven by its ethanol blending 
success (20% target achieved ahead of schedule) and 
ambitious goals for advanced biofuels that include 5% 
Compressed Biogas (CBG) blending by 2028-29, 2% 
bio-jet fuel for international ﬂights by 2028, 5% 
biodiesel by 2030 and 7% biomass co-ﬁring by 2026. 
ADVOCACY
The CII National Bioenergy Committee focused on 
developing a supporting ecosystem for emerging 
feedstocks such as algae, energy crops and waste-based 
sources, currently in early R&D or pilot stages. It also 
called for strengthening physical and digital 
infrastructure to support the collection, preprocessing 
and transportation of diverse feedstocks. Alongside, it 
advocated promoting market awareness and user 
incentives to increase uptake of biofuels.
ACTION 
Complementing its policy advocacy eﬀorts, CII hosted 
the 13th edition of the Bioenergy Summit, celebrating 
India's ethanol blending milestone. The summit aligned 
Government, Industry and global partners on feedstock 
diversiﬁcation, advanced biofuels adoption and 
waste-to-energy models. It reinforced India’s leadership 
in ethanol blending, CBG expansion and sustainable 
aviation fuel, while strengthening policy frameworks, 
regional initiatives and international cooperation.
ENERGY TRANSITION AND 
GREEN HYDROGEN
The CII National Council on Energy Transition and 
Hydrogen brought together key stakeholders across 
sectors to strategise and understand speciﬁc needs 
for decarbonisation. The Council also focused on 
creating a robust green hydrogen ecosystem by 
aligning the energy transition needs, particularly in 
carbon-intensive and hard-to-abate sectors.
ADVOCACY
CII made key recommendations on green hydrogen, 
including advocating for its inclusion in the 
Harmonised List of Infrastructure to enable easier 
access to long-term ﬁnance.
Following Solar Energy Corporation of India’s 
memorandum of understanding (MoU) with H2Global 
to establish a joint India–European Union (EU) tender 
framework for green hydrogen, CII submitted detailed 
inputs on the draft MoU, emphasising the need for 
commercial clarity, appropriate risk-sharing and 
bankable contract structures.
Further, a CII technical paper highlighted that existing 
carbon intensity thresholds for green ammonia and 
green methanol are extremely stringent and need to 
be aligned with technology-readiness and global 
benchmarks.
ACTION
The International Business Conclave on Green 
Hydrogen focused on providing demand side 
enablers. As a multi-stakeholder platform bringing 
together Government representatives, Industry 
leaders and other stakeholders, it enumerated 
actionable pathways for India’s green hydrogen 
transition.
Alongside, CII convened the India–Netherlands 
Business Roundtable on the sidelines of India Energy 
Week. The roundtable focused on strengthening 
cooperation in energy transition including energy 
infrastructure, energy eﬃciency, green hydrogen, 
renewable energy and alternative fuels. It facilitated 
dialogue on co-developing policy frameworks, 
technologies and ﬁnancing pathways, while exploring 
bilateral trade and investment opportunities.
Continuing with international focus, CII organised a 
business delegation to the World Hydrogen Summit in 
Rotterdam. The delegation facilitated India’s strategic 
Annual Report 2025-26 119
positioning in the global hydrogen ecosystem with 
high-level interactions with ministries, Government 
agencies, multilateral institutions and Industry 
leaders. Engagements included the Kingdom of the 
Netherlands, Belgium, Germany and representatives 
of the EU.
HYDROCARBONS
The Government of India has set an ambitious target 
to increase the share of natural gas in the energy mix 
from 6.7% to 15% by 2030. This transition is anchored 
in expanding City Gas Distribution (CGD) networks, 
streamlining licensing policies and promoting 
domestic exploration and production of 
hydrocarbons.
ADVOCACY
The CII National Hydrocarbon Committee advocated 
for the inclusion of natural gas and all petroleum 
products under the GST framework and a uniﬁed CGD 
code across states to streamline regulations.
In line with CII recommendations on ease of doing 
business, the Government enacted the Oilﬁelds 
(Regulation and Development) Amendment Act, 2025 
to modernise India’s oil and gas regulatory framework, 
attract investments in the sector and promote the 
eﬃcient and sustainable development of oilﬁelds. The 
Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) 
also simpliﬁed its tariﬀ structure from three to two 
uniﬁed tariﬀ zones.
ACTION
CII organised a new initiative, the Seminar on Building 
Infrastructure for Gas-based Economy, that discussed 
investment mobilisation, Liqueﬁed Natural Gas (LNG) 
terminal utilisation and strategies for expanding 
pipeline infrastructure, reinforcing the role of natural 
gas in creating clean and inclusive energy access.
MOBILITY
CII launched a National Coalition on Future Mobility in 
June to adopt an integrated and holistic approach to 
addressing the future of mobility in India. The 
Coalition, which comprises senior Members from CII, 
Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM), 
Automotive Component Manufacturers Association of 
India (ACMA) and National Association of Software 
and Service Companies (NASSCOM), aims to 
streamline infrastructure development, promote 
innovation and bring sustainable, convenient, 
aﬀordable and timely mobility solutions for all.
ADVOCACY
CII advocated for alternative powertrains while also 
promoting higher ethanol blending and expanding use 
of blended gas. It also worked towards broadening 
application of biofuels—methanol, ethanol and 
biodiesel. Among other focus areas was the promotion 
of battery Electric Vehicles (EVs), hybrid EVs, plug-in 
hybrids and deployment of fuel-cell EVs. 
ACTION
Under the umbrella of Bharat Mobility, CII anchored a 
one-day conference featuring discussions on sustainable 
infrastructure development and evolution of 
future-ready mobility products. These discussions 
highlighted India’s growing potential as a global mobility 
hub, with emphasis on innovation, manufacturing 
localisation, exports and the contribution of MSMEs in 
strengthening the mobility value chain.
NUCLEAR POWER
Nuclear power is a critical pillar of India’s clean energy 
transition and long-term energy security. Aligned with 
the Government of India’s renewed thrust to scale 
nuclear capacity to 100 GW by 2047, CII sharpened its 
strategic focus on the sector. Globally, nuclear energy 
serves as a reliable baseload source, with leading 
economies deriving a signiﬁcant share of electricity

Energy Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh; Shripad Yesso 
Naik, Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy and 
Santosh Kumar Sarangi, Secretary, Ministry of New & Renewable 
Energy at the Business Conclave on Green Hydrogen in New Delhi

from nuclear power. In contrast, India’s nuclear 
contribution remains modest at around 3% of total 
electricity generation, highlighting the imperative to 
accelerate deployment in support of the country’s Net 
Zero commitment by 2070 and a diversiﬁed, resilient 
energy mix.
ADVOCACY
With installed capacity of just over 8 GW and a 
sizeable pipeline under construction and approval, the 
CII National Committee on Nuclear Power focused on 
enabling rapid scale-up through policy and regulatory 
reforms, ﬁnancing and investment frameworks, 
private sector participation, localisation of supply 
chains, workforce skilling and the integration of large 
reactors alongside emerging technologies such as 
Small Modular Reactors and Bharat Small Reactors. 
ACTION
CII deepened international engagement through 
participation in World Atomic Week, Moscow and by 
leading a delegation to the World Nuclear Exhibition, 
Paris, strengthening global partnerships and Industry 
capability.
RENEWABLE ENERGY & 
POWER
India’s renewable energy sector is evolving into an 
integrated and resilient ecosystem, supported by 
energy storage, grid stability and emerging low-carbon 
technologies. Accelerated reforms emphasising 
reliability, aﬀordability and sustainability were initiated 
in the power sector. Government initiatives focused on 
strengthening Distribution Companies (DISCOMs), 
reducing losses, upgrading infrastructure and enabling 
greater integration of renewable energy, digital 
systems and smart grid technologies.
ADVOCACY
The CII National Committee on Renewable Energy and 
the CII Renewable Energy Manufacturing Council 
made representations to the Government including 
temporary suspension of anti-dumping duties on solar 
glass to reduce input costs and support solar module 
manufacturing and automatic extension of General 
Network Access operationalisation to avoid penal 
transmission charges when Power Purchase 
Agreement signing is delayed. 
Simultaneously, the CII National Committee on Power 
made key representations on addressing procedural 
challenges in the veriﬁcation of captive generating 
plants operating across multiple states and issues 
related to ﬂexible operation norms for coal-based 
thermal power plants. The representations focused on 
easing regulatory compliance, ensuring technical 
feasibility, improving data authentication and digital 
processes and strengthening the smart metering 
ecosystem through skill development, infrastructure 
readiness, ﬁnancing support and cybersecurity 
safeguards.
ACTION
Strengthening policies is central to scaling clean 
energy technologies and enabling public–private 
partnerships for resilient supply chains and innovative 
green ﬁnance. During the 6th edition of the 
International Energy Conference & Exhibition (IECE), 
CII highlighted key issues through the launch of three 
reports: CII–EY’s ‘Eigenvectors of Net Zero Transition 
Pathways to Viksit Bharat 2047’, an Industry paper on 
India’s transmission sector and ‘Manufacturing for 
India and the World’.
An exclusive CEO roundtable with Shri Manohar Lal, 
Minister of Power and Housing & Urban Aﬀairs, 
enabled dialogue with Industry leaders on the evolving 
energy landscape, policy frameworks and avenues for 
collaboration in advancing sustainable growth.
Manohar Lal, Minister of Power and Housing & Urban Aﬀairs at the 
CEOs roundtable at the 6th International Energy Conference & 
Exhibition in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26 121
CEOs also interacted with sixteen Members of 
Parliament from seven parties and representing nine 
states to discuss equitable power access, consumer 
tariﬀ protection, balanced energy transition and local 
job creation. Industry leaders highlighted the need for 
DISCOM reforms, clarity on carbon markets and green 
hydrogen incentives, long-term renewable energy 
contracts and expanded transmission infrastructure. 
The 3rd CII Conference on Smart Metering addressed 
sectoral challenges, shared best practices and 
developed actionable recommendations to enable a 
more sustainable and eﬃcient power distribution and 
transmission system in the country. A theme paper 
‘Protecting the Future of Energy: Cybersecurity and 
Privacy in Smart Metering Infrastructure’ focused on 
data monetisation and protection from challenges in 
the digital space.
ENERGY SECURITY 
CII Energy Security Department works towards 
institutionalising a mechanism for a regular interface 
between the Government, Industry, Academia, civil 
society and media on issues related to India’s energy 
security. Issues related to oil and gas, critical 
minerals, cross-border integration of renewable 
energy and cross-border power trading were 
addressed during the year.
ADVOCACY
CII, along with the Economic Research Institute of 
ASEAN and East Asia, Jakarta undertook a study on 
Cross Border Energy Trade and Integration of 
Renewable Energy which explored diﬀerent models 
of global energy trade between regions and their 
beneﬁts and challenges with a special focus on India’s 
North East region. The study provided analytical 
perspectives on drivers, constraints, opportunities and 
barriers, as well as measures to address institutional, 
ﬁnancial, policy and governance issues to minimise the 
total costs of energy security and maximise the 
social-economic beneﬁts for people in these regions. 
ACTION
CII in collaboration with the Ministry of External Aﬀairs 
and Ministry of Mines organised its 15th Energy 
Security Conference that facilitated discussion on 
speciﬁc strategies for ensuring India’s energy security 
and to secure a sustainable and low-carbon future.
The 10th edition of South Asia (BIN) Power Summit 
organised with the Ministry of Power and Ministry of 
External Aﬀairs, discussed and deliberated enhancing 
energy cooperation through cross border power 
trade, creating sustainability though grid integration, 
promoting power exchanges, promoting hydropower 
and pump storage and accelerating investment in the 
power sector.

Sudhir Sitapati, Chairman - CII National Committee on FMCG and 
Managing Director and CEO, Godrej Consumer Products at the CII 
National FMCG Summit held in Mumbai
FAST MOVING
CONSUMER GOODS
The fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sector 
navigated a year marked by evolving consumer 
expectations, regulatory shifts and supply chain 
transformation. The CII National Committee on FMCG 
steered Industry priorities, strengthened dialogue 
between policymakers and Industry leaders and shaped 
forward-looking reforms. Through structured 
consultations and targeted submissions, the Committee 
worked to ensure that regulatory environments support 
sustained sectoral growth, enhance aﬀordability for 
consumers and drive competitiveness.
ADVOCACY
CII intensiﬁed policy engagement to ensure FMCG 
sector’s priorities were systematically reﬂected in the 
Government’s reform agenda. Extensive consultations 
with Member companies culminated in 
recommendations to support rapid, high impact 
regulatory interventions. A major thrust area was GST 
rationalisation, where CII submitted a detailed proposal 
advocating lower GST rates for mass consumption 
categories, correction of inverted duty structures and 
greater rate parity to enhance aﬀordability and 
formalisation. The representation also highlighted the 
need for stable, long-term GST frameworks, eﬃcient 
refund mechanisms and streamlined compliance to 
reduce working capital pressures.
Recommendations also included sustainable 
packaging timelines, risk based regulatory treatment 
for low hazard categories and simpliﬁcation of 
processes spanning multiple regulatory agencies. 
These submissions aimed to strengthen consumer 
access, spur manufacturing competitiveness and 
enable a smoother transition as India undertakes wide 
ranging tax and regulatory reforms.
ACTION
The Committee deepened Member engagement 
through high impact knowledge platforms to navigate 
emerging market shifts and evolving economic 
conditions. A Strategy Session on Raw Material 
Inﬂation brought together leaders to decode global 
and domestic trends shaping cost structures across 
the FMCG value chain. Speakers oﬀered evidence- 
based outlook on edible oil and crude price 
movements, highlighting implications for pricing, 
continuity planning and input cost risk management. 
They further provided an in-depth analysis of India’s 
agri economy, examining volatility in key commodities 
and their downstream eﬀects on FMCG 
manufacturing and supply chains. 
The Committee’s ﬂagship annual conference - CII 
National FMCG Summit, held in Mumbai, convened 
business leaders, analysts and strategists to explore the 
sector’s evolving growth trajectory. Speakers 
underscored how GST 2.0 and recent ﬁscal reforms are 
reshaping consumption patterns and formalisation, 
while calling for stronger research & development 
(R&D), sharper value propositions and innovation 
attuned to India’s diverse consumer segments. Panel 
discussions examined the fragmentation of the ‘new 
Indian consumer’, balancing aﬀordability and aspiration 
and the growing interplay between traditional, 
digital-ﬁrst and regional brands. The Summit explored 
shifts in rural demand, the role of technology in 
deepening market penetration and enduring principles 
of building brands and talent in a transforming 
ecosystem. These engagements equipped Members 
with strategic insights and actionable perspectives to 
navigate India’s next phase of FMCG growth.
Annual Report 2025-26 123
Annual Report 2025-26124
SERVICES
India’s ﬁnancial sector demonstrated remarkable 
resilience to global shocks with stronger balance 
sheets, declining non-performing assets (NPAs), 
improved capital adequacy and rapid digital adoption 
reﬂecting sustained reforms, regulatory 
strengthening and targeted Government 
interventions. CII continued to work closely with 
Industry, regulators and Government to foster 
innovation, inclusion and long-term growth across the 
ﬁnancial ecosystem.
NBFCs AND HFCs
CII worked to strengthen non-banking ﬁnancial 
companies (NBFCs) and housing ﬁnance companies 
(HFCs), recognising their role in expanding credit 
access to underserved segments and support ﬁnancial 
stability and growth.
ADVOCACY
Advocacy focused on positioning NBFCs as systemically 
important institutions through calibrated regulatory 
parity with banks; creating liquidity and reﬁnancing 
backstops for well governed entities; harmonising tax 
and capital norms; expanding access to Debts Recovery 
Tribunals (DRTs) and securitisation and reconstruction 
of ﬁnancial assets and enforcement of security interest 
(SARFAESI) for faster recoveries; strengthening fraud 
prevention via shared registries; enabling funding 
diversiﬁcation through deeper corporate bond markets; 
eased expected credit loss (ECB) norms; and greater 
participation by pension funds.
ACTION
A roundtable with Shri M Nagaraju, Secretary, 
Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of 
Finance facilitated dialogue on policy initiatives and 
sectoral growth with acknowledgment of the 
importance of deepening corporate bond markets for 
NBFC resilience.
INSURANCE AND PENSIONS
CII advocated measures to strengthen the insurance 
sector to enhance investment, expand access, improve 
regulatory eﬃciency and promote sustainable growth.
ADVOCACY
Advocacy included fast tracking 100% foreign direct 
investment (FDI) in insurance through amendments to 
the Insurance Act, addressing distribution challenges, 
improving inter-regulatory coordination, strengthening 
sectoral talent pipelines, resolving adverse taxation 
issues and introducing an Insurance Risk Score for 
standardised premium pricing. The Insurance Act 
enabling 100% FDI was passed in November.
ACTION
Committee deliberations emphasised strengthening 
digital distribution, improving claims transparency, 
enhancing regulatory coordination across Insurance 
Regulatory and Development Authority of India 
(IRDAI), Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and DFS and 
building talent capacity.
FINTECH AND FINANCIAL INCLUSION
FinTech has transformed ﬁnancial services by 
expanding access, reducing costs and enabling real- 
time delivery. CII worked towards advancing 
technology and inclusion for underserved and 
unbanked populations.
FINANCIAL SERVICES
Nirmala Sitharaman, Minister of Finance and Corporate Aﬀairs at the 
CII Inaugural Summit on GCCs in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26 125
PRIVATE EQUITY AND VENTURE 
CAPITAL
CII worked to enhance inter-regulatory coordination in 
private equity (PE) and venture capital (VC), boost 
domestic institutional investment and address 
regulatory and tax challenges, supported by working 
groups ﬁnalising key recommendations.
ACTION
High-level engagements with Shri Tuhin Kanta 
Pandey, Chairman, Securities and Exchange Board of 
India (SEBI) and Shri M Nagaraju provided platforms 
for discussing regulatory priorities. Continued 
international outreach included planned interactions 
with global PE and VC stakeholders.
BANKING
CII focused on strengthening India’s ﬁnancial 
ecosystem to support inclusive growth, improve credit 
access and enable the transition towards more 
sustainable and resilient ﬁnancial systems.
ADVOCACY
Advocacy priorities included integrating climate ﬁnance 
and environmental, social and governance (ESG) criteria 
into banking practices; expanding MSME ﬁnancing 
through digital and UPI-linked solutions; scaling up 
credit guarantee coverage; addressing delayed MSME 
payments via Trade Receivables Discounting System 
(TReDS) and other mechanisms; and promoting 
innovative ﬁnancing such as sustainability-linked loans.
ACTION
Committee meetings and the Financing Summit 
enabled extensive dialogue with senior policymakers 
and regulators on banking reforms and future priorities.
ADVOCACY
Recommendations included consolidating fragmented 
regulatory guidelines into uniﬁed master directions; 
adopting technology driven oversight such as video audits; 
upgrading rural ﬁnancial institutions for Uniﬁed Payments 
Interface (UPI) integration; implementing scale-based 
regulation for FinTechs; shifting to demand-driven 
regulatory sandboxes; and adopting uniform, risk-based 
Know Your Customer (KYC) frameworks.
ACTION
The Financial Inclusion and FinTech Summit released a 
report on sectoral reforms, with regulators indicating 
ongoing deliberations on KYC norms and sandboxes.
FINANCIAL MARKETS
CII worked towards strengthening the policy and 
regulatory environment for India’s ﬁnancial markets to 
enhance capital allocation, liquidity and risk management.
ADVOCACY
Policy recommendations included permitting parking 
of unutilised initial public oﬀering (IPO) proceeds in 
low risk mutual funds; allowing Infrastructure 
Investment Trusts (InvITs) and Real Estate Investment 
Trusts (REITs) to invest surplus funds in liquid mutual 
funds; providing ﬂexibility in post-allotment security 
creation for non-convertible debentures (NCDs); 
strengthening listing and delisting frameworks; 
reducing minimum public oﬀer size for very large 
issuers; and modernising Employee Stock Ownership 
GLOBAL CAPABILITY CENTRES
The agenda of the newly-constituted Task Force 
included advancing dialogue on Global Capability 
Centres (GCCs), given their importance as innovation 
and service hubs for global ﬁnancial institutions.
ADVOCACY
Advocacy emphasised a national framework for GCCs, 
including digital economic zones, a national GCC council, 
single window clearances, stronger Industry– 
Academia linkages, advanced talent development and 
broader regional inclusion beyond Tier 1 cities, 
complemented by State-level frameworks enabling 
ﬂexibility for localised policy design.
Plan (ESOP) rules to allow grants to founder 
promoters with appropriate governance safeguards. 
Several recommendations, including reduced public 
oﬀer size norms and ESOP reforms, were 
implemented by SEBI. 
ACTION
Several domestic and international investor 
interactions were conducted to facilitate these 
recommendations during the year.
MEDIA AND ENTERTAINMENT
The CII National Council for Media and Entertainment 
works to position India as a globally competitive 
creative hub by aligning policy reforms, technology 
adoption, infrastructure, skilling and global outreach. 
The focus is on strengthening the creative economy 
across ﬁlm, television, Over-the-Top (OTT) service, 
Animation-Visual Eﬀects-Gaming-Comics (AVGC), 
music, radio and digital media, while enabling 
investment, innovation and international 
collaboration.
ADVOCACY 
Policy advocacy centred on building a future-ready 
media and entertainment ecosystem, with emphasis 
on regulatory reforms, ease of doing business, 
investment facilitation, skilling, infrastructure 
development and global market access. CII strongly 
advocated the adoption of a National Media and 
Entertainment Policy, noting that convergence, 
artiﬁcial intelligence-led transformation and 
platform evolution demand a uniﬁed national 
roadmap aligned to future business models and 
emerging technologies. Key advocacy included:
L-R: Rajan Navani, Co-Chair, CII National Council on Media & Entertainment and Chairman & Managing Director, Jetline Group of Companies; Sanjay Jaju, 
then Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting; Gaurav Banerjee, Chair, CII National Council on Media & Entertainment and MD & CEO, Sony 
Pictures Networks India; Gunjan Soni, Co-Chair, CII National Council on Media & Entertainment and Country Managing Director, YouTube India and Ravi 
Rajamani Managing Director, Global Head of AI Blackbelts, Google, California, United States at the CII Big Picture Summit in Mumbai
ACTION
Task Force meetings and GCC summits presented the 
national framework and strengthened Centre–State 
collaboration to position India as a global ﬁnancial 
services and innovation hub.
• Preserving self-regulation for OTT platforms and 
enabling market-led broadcasting reforms
• Establishing a National e-Sports and Gaming 
Development Authority
• Strengthening anti-piracy enforcement and 
Intellectual Property protection
• Building next-generation production infrastructure 
and expanding screen density
• Launching a dedicated media, gaming and 
AVGC-Extended Reality (XR) export and 
international distribution framework
• Implementing globally aligned skilling and 
education-to-employment pathways
• Introducing a Production Linked Incentive (PLI) 
scheme for gaming, media and AVGC-XR.
ACTION 
The 12th CII Big Picture Summit served as the principal 
advocacy and Industry convergence platform, 
facilitating high-level policy dialogue, structured B2B 
engagements and consensus-building on the future of 
the creative economy.
Dedicated investor-investee meetings and the WAVES 
Bazaar strengthened business matchmaking, enabled 
market access for creative startups and reinforced 
pathways for innovation-led entrepreneurship.
India’s international presence was strengthened through 
the CII Bharat Pavilion at the Cannes Film Festival, 
facilitating co-production discussions, global partnerships 
and promotion of select Indian states ﬁlm locations.
Annual Report 2025-26126
LUXURY RETAIL
The newly formed CII National Committee on Luxury 
Retail brings together leading players across fashion, 
retail, furniture, food and allied segments to 
strengthen India’s global luxury positioning. The 
committee focuses on showcasing India’s heritage, 
craftsmanship and design excellence, while promoting 
international collaboration, progressive policies, skilling 
and creative entrepreneurship across the value chain.
ACTION
CII led a luxury retail delegation to Dubai alongside 
Dubai Design Week to benchmark global best 
practices. The delegation engaged with key policy and 
trade bodies, including the Dubai Chamber of 
Commerce, Ministry of Foreign Trade and Dubai 
Economic Development Corporation to understand 
frameworks supporting luxury and creative industries.
Industry interactions with leading businesses provided 
insights on experiential retail, brand storytelling, 
digital integration, sustainable design, trade 
facilitation, ease of doing business and collaborative 
opportunities.
TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY
Tourism and hospitality continue to be key drivers of 
economic growth, employment and development. The 
CII National Committee on Tourism and Hospitality 
focuses on reviving inbound tourism, strengthening 
domestic travel and enabling structured 
Government–Industry engagement to address policy, 
regulatory and structural bottlenecks.
ADVOCACY
Through stakeholder consultations between 
Government and Industry, the committee pursued a 
comprehensive reform agenda to position tourism as 
a high-impact growth engine through coordinated 
policy reforms, destination-led development and 
sustained global branding. Key advocacy included:
• Grant and operationalisation of Industry status 
across states and nationwide infrastructure status 
for tourism and hospitality to unlock aﬀordable, 
long-term ﬁnancing
• Sustained investment in global tourism marketing, 
including revival and modernisation of the 
Incredible India campaign
• GST rationalisation to enhance price 
competitiveness and formalisation of the sector
• Ease of doing business through streamlining 
licences and approvals
• Emphasised accelerated development of 50 
ﬂagship destinations through mission-mode 
planning and professional destination 
management
• Expansion of aviation and transport connectivity 
to emerging tourism clusters
• Revival of inbound tourism through globally 
competitive visa and e-visa regimes
• Institutionalised skilling and structured career 
pathways across tourism and hospitality.
Aashti Bhartia, Chairperson, CII National Committee on Luxury Retail 
and Managing Director, Ogaan with Salem Al Shamsi, Executive Vice 
President – International Relation Sector, Dubai Chamber of 
Commerce during the CII Luxury Delegation to Dubai

INDIAN DIGITAL
GAMING SOCIETY
The Indian Digital Gaming Society (IDGS) strengthened 
India’s digital gaming and e-Sports ecosystem while 
supporting the country’s ambition to emerge as a 
global hub for innovation, talent and digital 
entertainment. Through policy engagement, Industry 
collaborations and knowledge-driven initiatives, IDGS 
worked with Governments, Academia and global 
partners to foster a responsible and future-ready 
gaming ecosystem.
ADVOCACY
IDGS engaged with State Governments and 
policymakers to develop a progressive policy and 
regulatory framework for the gaming and animation, 
visual eﬀects, gaming, comics and extended reality 
(AVGC-XR) sectors. The Society participated in 
consultations with the Government of Haryana to 
contribute recommendations for the State’s AVGC-XR 
and gaming policy, focusing on enabling Industry 
growth, strengthening talent development and 
encouraging investment in emerging digital sectors.
IDGS also engaged with Shri Priyank Kharge, Minister for 
Information Technology & Biotechnology, Government 
of Karnataka, highlighting the need for policy support, 
Industry collaboration and initiatives focused on skilling 
and infrastructure development in the State’s gaming 
and immersive technology ecosystem.
ACTION
IDGS participated in key Industry platforms and 
promoted collaboration, innovation and skill 
development. At WAVES 2025, the Society 
contributed to innovation showcases, panel 
discussions and exhibitions that brought together 
educators, developers and technology leaders.
A key initiative was the expansion of GameForge, an 
IDGS-led Academia–Industry platform designed to 
bridge the gap between education and Industry 
requirements in gaming and esports. The initiative 
focused on identifying emerging skill sets and career 
pathways while introducing students to opportunities 
in game development, esports management, 
broadcasting, analytics and digital content creation, 
impacting over 10,000 students.
To support Industry awareness and compliance, IDGS 
organised a legal webinar on the Digital Personal Data 
Protection (DPDP) Act and discussed the future of 
gaming at the IGS 2025. The Society also supported a 
post-budget discussion analysing key announcements 
from the Union Budget and their implications for the 
gaming and AVGC-XR ecosystem.
Global engagement was strengthened through a 
cross-border webinar connecting Indian participants 
with Korean Industry Members to explore 
collaboration opportunities in gaming, esports and 
creative technologies.
The Society engaged with the gaming community by 
participating in Gamicon, the WCG India LAN Event 
and the Big Picture Summit – Global Investor Meet, 
facilitating dialogue with developers, investors, 
esports players and technology leaders.
To promote grassroots innovation, IDGS supported 
the Game Jam in Jaipur, where students and 
developers collaborated to design and prototype 
games, encouraging creativity and hands-on learning. 
IDGS participated in international engagements 
during the visit of the President of Finland and 
contributed to discussions at the AI Summit on the 
impact of artiﬁcial intelligence (AI) on video games, 
e-Sports, cloud gaming and data centres.
Rajan Navani, President IDGS and Chairman & Managing Director, Jetline 
Group of Companies and Sean (Hyunil) Sohn, Vice President IDGS & CEO 
Krafton India at India Gaming Show in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26 129
CII strengthened India’s design ecosystem through 
strategic initiatives, policy frameworks and 
recognition programmes that foster innovation and 
celebrate design excellence. Eﬀorts focused on 
nurturing a sustainable, inclusive and globally 
competitive design Industry, recognising its vital role 
in driving economic growth and social development.
ADVOCACY
One such eﬀort was the National Design Policy 
Communiqué, developed through extensive 
consultations involving Industry leaders, Academics, 
policymakers through regional roundtables. Inputs 
were consolidated and the Communiqué was 
launched at the CII Design Summit for submission to 
relevant Government bodies to guide and strengthen 
India’s national design policy framework.
CII drove design-focused policy advocacy through 
three strategic whitepapers - ‘AI in Design’, ‘Design for 
a Sustainable Future’ and ‘Bengaluru Vision 2030’. 
These provided actionable insights to build a 
future-ready creative economy, promote sustainable 
design practices, foster innovation and position 
Bengaluru and India as global leaders in design, 
innovation and Industry-Academia collaboration.
DESIGN
ACTION
The CII India Design initiatives reinforced India’s 
position as a global design hub, combining 
international engagement, domestic learning and 
policy advocacy. The India Design Mission to South 
Korea strengthened cross-border collaboration, 
enabling MoUs with leading Korean design 
institutions, securing participation in the CII India 
Design Summit and generating insights on design 
innovation, sustainability and user experience.
The 25th CII Global Design Summit and Exposition 
positioned design as a strategic driver of innovation, 
competitiveness and sustainable growth. The Summit 
featured global dialogues, curated Industry visits, 
international MoUs, design exhibitions and awards, 
highlighting the integration of design with 
technology, business strategy and India’s global 
industrial transformation.
Recognition of excellence was central to the Summit. 
The CII Design Excellence Awards honoured over 100 
organisations and individuals for embedding design 
into business strategies, while the i-Design 
Programme 4.0 felicitated over 30 professionals for 
building structured capabilities, leadership and 
organisational maturity. Complementing these, the CII 
India Design Tag benchmarked products against 
rigorous standards, promoting superior design quality, 
market credibility and enhancing India’s global 
reputation as a design-led economy.
Three regional roundtables in Bengaluru, Pune and 
Delhi engaged over 150 leaders from Industry and 
Academia to shape a robust National Design Policy. 
Discussions focused on micro, small and medium 
enterprises (MSMEs), inclusive design education, 
Industry–Academia integration, artisan empowerment 
and entrepreneurship. Domestic Industry visits to 
manufacturing facilities provided more than 135 
delegates with ﬁrsthand learning on design 
integration, innovation processes and manufacturing 
excellence, ensuring practical insights and 
cross-Industry knowledge sharing.
Dr Udayant Malhoutra, Chairman, CII National Committee on Design 
and CEO & Managing Director, Dynamatic Technologies Ltd at the 
25th Global Design Summit & Exposition in Bengaluru
Annual Report 2025-26130
India’s healthcare ecosystem is undergoing a pivotal 
transition as the country advances towards Viksit 
Bharat@2047. In 2025, CII’s healthcare engagement 
focused on strengthening healthcare delivery while 
enabling care models that enhance longevity and 
quality of life. Key priorities included responsible 
digital health adoption, better alignment between 
providers and payers and deeper international 
collaboration to build a resilient, future-ready 
healthcare ecosystem.
HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS
CII’s engagement with healthcare providers addressed 
skill gaps, strengthening patient experience and 
supported sustainable hospital operating models 
aligned with national health priorities.
ACTION
The 22nd CII Annual Health Summit served as a 
ﬂagship platform to advance dialogue on the future 
of healthcare delivery, innovation and collaboration. 
DIGITAL HEALTH
The key focus was on positioning technology as a 
system enabler to strengthen prevention, early 
detection, continuity of care and workforce capacity, 
with emphasis on responsible adoption of digital 
health and AI.
ACTION
CII, in partnership with NITI Aayog, convened the CII 
Huddle on Frontier Technologies in Health to examine 
how emerging technologies can enable healthcare 
transformation aligned with Viksit Bharat@2047. 
Deliberations highlighted AI-augmented telemedicine, 
consent-based digital health records, voice-enabled 
and vernacular AI tools, along with gamiﬁcation and 
incentive frameworks as key enablers of improved 
health literacy, early detection and continuity of care. 
Further, the 4th CII Digital Health Summit reinforced 
the shift towards scaled, outcome-oriented adoption 
of digital health solutions.
HEALTH AND
LIFE SCIENCES
HEALTHCARE
Discussions focused on innovative ﬁnancing 
approaches and the role of multi-sectoral partnerships 
in building resilience.
A strong international dimension marked the Summit, 
with emphasis on cross-border collaboration with 
Japan to enable technology transfer, skill exchange 
and capacity building. A memorandum of 
understanding (MoU) between CII, the Economic 
Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia (ERIA) and 
Medical Excellence Japan (MEJ) reinforced 
institutional commitment to deepening international 
healthcare cooperation. The Summit also addressed 
priorities around Medical Value Travel, data 
protection under the Digital Personal Data Protection 
Act and the need for a human-centred approach to 
artiﬁcial intelligence (AI).
Dr Naresh Trehan, Chairman, CII Steering Group on Health and 
Healthcare Council and CMD, Medanta – The Medicity and Piyush 
Goyal, Minister for Commerce and Industry at the 22nd Health Summit 
in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26 131
HEALTH INSURANCE
The focus was on strengthening transparency and 
eﬃciency while positioning the health insurance 
ecosystem as an enabler of access and continuity of 
care and addressing systemic challenges for patients, 
providers and insurers.
ACTION
CII undertook a series of focused engagements with 
the Chairman, Insurance Regulatory and Development 
Authority of India (IRDAI). Key structural challenges 
were addressed with emphasis on co-designed codes 
of conduct, adoption of the National Health Claims 
Exchange, standardisation of claims and 
empanelment processes and the need for a credible 
framework to assess medical inﬂation, reinforcing a 
consensus-driven reform pathway.
AYURVEDA
CII focused on strengthening the ayurveda sector as a 
credible, evidence-led and innovation-driven system 
of care with both domestic relevance and global 
potential.
ACTION
A closed-door Industry policy and strategy dialogue 
was organised to shape a shared vision for ayurveda 
from 2025 to 2035. As a key outcome, CII, in 
partnership with the Indian Council for Research on 
International Economic Relations (ICRIER), is 
developing the Ayurveda Industry Vision 2035 report, 
drawing inputs from Industry, practitioners and 
Government to provide a clear roadmap for growth, 
governance and global positioning.
PUBLIC HEALTH
CII’s public health initiatives focused on prevention-led 
approaches, low-cost innovations, women and 
children’s health, tuberculosis (TB) screening for 
Industry members and a deeper private sector 
engagement beyond Corporate Social Responsibility. 
The CII Centre for Health, launched during the Annual 
General Meeting 2025, was positioned to drive 
coordinated stakeholder action and long-term public 
health priorities.
MEDICAL TECHNOLOGY
CII’s MedTech engagement worked towards 
strengthening India’s medical device ecosystem 
through regulatory clarity, innovation enablement and 
global competitiveness, while ensuring patient safety 
and quality standards.
ACTION
CII, in collaboration with the Central Drugs Standard 
Control Organisation (CDSCO), organised a 
ﬁrst-of-its-kind series of regulatory workshops across 
Delhi, Ahmedabad and Bengaluru, bringing together 
regulators and over 150 MedTech companies to 
address key regulatory challenges. 
ADVOCACY
CII, in partnership with the Women’s Collective Forum 
and leading academic institutions including Indian 
School of Business (ISB), Faculty of Management 
Studies (FMS), the Institute for Social and Economic 
Change (ISEC) and Population Council Institute, 
co-developed four national white papers on women’s 
and child health which assessed progress over the past 
decade and outlined policy recommendations on 
maternal health, child and adolescent health, family 
planning and innovations in women’s health.
ACTION 
• The 6th CII Public Health Summit reinforced the 
shift towards a prevention-ﬁrst public health 
agenda. Nine low-cost public health innovations 
were showcased, receiving feedback on 
integration into existing health systems. 
• An interaction with Members of Parliament 
focused on implementing policy recommendations 
on women and children’s health through 
constituency-level partnerships
• The ﬁrst meeting of the CII Centre for Health 
Steering Group identiﬁed priority areas for 
scalable public health action
• Under the CII TB-Free Workplaces Initiative, four 
screening camps covered 344 employees, enabling 
early detection and treatment linkage.
SENIOR CARE
CII’s senior care engagement addressed emerging 
challenges linked to India’s ageing population, with 
emphasis on dignity, independence, mental wellbeing 
and quality of life in later years.
ACTION
The ﬁrst CII Senior Care Conclave led structured 
dialogues on policy gaps in regulation, care delivery 
and digital inclusion. CII submitted detailed inputs to 
NITI Aayog outlining action areas across health and 
wellness, housing, technology use, ﬁnancial 
awareness and private sector participation, supported 
by background papers on digital inclusion and private 
sector engagement in senior care.
PHARMA & LIFE SCIENCES
CII’s engagement in Pharma and Life Sciences focused 
on positioning India as a global Contract Research, 
Development and Manufacturing Organisation 
(CRDMO) hub, advancing sustainable and 
innovation-led growth and strengthening global 
partnerships.
ACTION
CII convened Industry roundtables on the CRDMO 
ecosystem and international partnerships, including 
an India-Africa collaboration to exchange best 
practices and investment strategies. The 7th CII 
Pharma & Life Sciences Summit advanced dialogue on 
sustainability, innovation, talent and regulatory 
frameworks, alongside the release of CII knowledge 
reports on CRDMO leadership and sustainability in 
Pharma and Life Sciences.
L - R: Dr Naresh Trehan; Dr Jitendra Singh, Minister of State (I/C) of Science and Technology and Earth Sciences and Minister of State, Prime Minister’s 
Oﬃce; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Space and Atomic Energy; Dr Vinod K Paul, Member, NITI Aayog and Ms Neena Gupta, Ambassador,
CII Committee on Senior Care and Actor at the CII Senior Care Conclave in New Delhi
The 17th CII Global MedTech Summit advanced 
discussions on regulatory harmonisation, workforce 
readiness, innovation acceleration, global 
collaboration and strategies to boost medical device 
exports. The Summit also marked the release of the 
CII–BCG report on 'Positioning India for Global 
MedTech Leadership'.
Annual Report 2025-26132

Marshall; Prof Anil Sahasrabudhe, Chairman, National Educational Technology Forum; Dr V Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser to Government 
of India and Dr Nandini Rangaswamy, Co-Chairperson, CII National Higher Education Council and Chairperson, GRG Institutions launching the report 
‘Exploratory Study on CSR in Education: Assessing Impact and Trends in the Indian Context’ at the 15th Global Higher Education Summit in New Delhi
EDUCATION
CII advanced a cohesive education agenda spanning 
school and higher education, aligned with the future 
of workforce development and Education 5.0. The 
focus was on improving quality of education and 
research, strengthening faculty capacity, promoting 
responsible integration of artiﬁcial intelligence (AI) 
and technology, deepening Industry engagement and 
supporting National Education Policy (NEP) 
2020–aligned reforms to build a globally competitive, 
Industry-ready talent pipeline.
With quality education emerging as a top priority for 
the Government, CII addressed future-ready 
education reforms, focusing on:
• Improving quality of research and teaching 
through faculty development, Industry 
engagement and creation of conducive research 
and innovation ecosystems
• Advancing Industry-aligned pedagogy to bridge 
the Industry-readiness gap and strengthen 
employability outcomes
• Promoting AI and technology integration, 
particularly in higher education, with emphasis on 
ethical adoption, academic integrity and enhanced 
learning outcomes
• Strengthening STEM education, experiential 
learning and vocational exposure to foster scientiﬁc 
temper, critical thinking and job-oriented skills
• Supporting eﬀective implementation of NEP 2020 
and contributing to the vision of Viksit 
Bharat@2047, including interdisciplinary learning, 
holistic assessment and ﬂexible learning pathways.
ACTION
CII advanced its advocacy agenda through the 
following ﬂagship initiatives:
• The 15th Global Higher Education Summit and the 
9th National School Education Summit addressed 
faculty development, research quality, Industry- 
aligned pedagogy, AI in education, future STEM 
pathways, educator capacity building and 
workforce readiness, generating actionable policy 
insights
Annual Report 2025-26 133
• Strengthening international benchmarking, the CII 
School Leaders Global Learning & Partnership 
Mission to Switzerland enabled 17 school leaders 
to visit ﬁve international schools and colleges to 
participate in the Global Learning Conference, 
generating insights aligned with NEP-driven school 
transformation. The CII Higher Education Global 
Partnership Mission to the United Kingdom, led by 
Dr Naushad Forbes, Chairman, CII National Higher 
Education Council and Co-Chairman, Forbes 
Marshall, comprised 23 delegates and included 
visits to six institutions, strengthening India-UK 
collaboration in higher education and innovation
• The CII–Anusandhan National Research 
Foundation Prime Minister’s Fellowship for 
Doctoral Research strengthened Industry-funded 
doctoral research, supporting 90 fellows during 
the year, with 53 new fellows selected, reinforcing 
the research–innovation–Industry linkage.
SUPPORTING INITIATIVES AND 
ENGAGEMENTS
Additional initiatives included national-level case study 
competitions for school principals and higher 
education students, engaging over 50 educators, 170 
students and 80 academic institutions; the launch of 
the CII Schools’ Forum; PARAKH-NCERT Holistic 
Progress Card workshop series (three workshops 
engaging 150 educators); and the publication of 
‘Exploratory Study on CSR in Education: Assessing 
Impact and Trends in the Indian Context’ that 
examines education-focused CSR in India and oﬀers 
evidence-based recommendations to strengthen 
scale, sustainability, collaboration and long-term 
systemic impact.
