India@100 is a people-centric, long-term vision 
guiding India’s journey towards an inclusively 
developed and globally competitive nation by 2047. 
The vision serves as a compass for aligning the 
long-term mission of CII, anchoring its work ﬁrmly in 
the larger purpose of nation-building. Leveraging the 
collaborative legacy of India@75, India@100 reﬂects a 
shift from milestone-based development to sustained 
nation-building driven by convergence of Industry, 
Government, civil society, Academia and citizens, 
guided by the principle of Nation First.
The India@100 Foundation serves as a platform for 
translating this vision into immediate, short-term and 
long-term action. It facilitates convergence for 
fostering partnerships, leadership, volunteering and 
scalable high impact initiatives. 
INDIA@100
ADVOCACY
The ‘National Vision Document on India@100:
The People’s Agenda’ was developed as a strategic 
framework to carry forward the momentum of long-term 
nation-building in a focused manner under sectoral 
thematic areas for achieving vision objectives by 2047. 
The document articulates a shared roadmap advocating 
collective action to achieve national aspirations as the 
country approaches 100 years of Independence.
India@100 vision comprises ﬁve pillars of AMRIT that 
outline India’s pathway to ‘Ascend’ in the evolving 
world order by ‘Maximising’ economic growth, 
‘Revitalising’ its cultural and soft power, ‘Innovating’ 
to remain globally competitive and ‘Transforming’ its 
development model to unlock human potential.
The AMRIT framework enables a holistic approach to 
growth-one that aligns ambition with inclusion, 
innovation with equity and progress with long-term 
sustainability.
ACTION
Translating vision into action, the India@100 
Foundation, in collaboration with CII and leveraging its 
institutional outreach, has adopted a multi-pronged 
approach that ensures all initiatives remain aligned 
with national aspirations. Platforms such as the 
summit themed ‘India Ahead: Towards a Viksit Bharat’ 
brought together leaders from Industry, Government, 
Academia and civil society to align priorities central to 
India’s development journey ranging from inclusive 
growth and future-ready skills to innovation 
ecosystems, micro, small and medium enterprise 
(MSME) competitiveness and cross-sector 
collaboration. These dialogues helped translate 
long-term ambition into clear pathways, partnerships 
and actionable outcomes.
Annual Report 2025-26 139
Sustained thought leadership has been a key driver of 
this transition from intent to impact. The Fireside Chat 
Series ‘I Have a Dream’ convened inﬂuential voices of 
domain experts from diverse sectors to reﬂect on 
India’s development trajectory and outline a roadmap 
toward a developed and inclusive nation. 
Deliberations spanned manufacturing, ﬁnance, 
sustainability, education, healthcare, agriculture and 
India’s soft power. 
The ‘ChangeSpeake’ Series spotlighted changemakers 
translating their ideas into action. By showcasing 
scalable models, community-led innovation and 
leadership-driven solutions, the platform reinforced a 
result-oriented approach and highlighted the 
importance of measurement matrix for impact and 
outcomes across initiatives.
Campaigns such as Har Ghar Tiranga strengthened 
civic pride and national unity, while Swachhata Hi 
Seva, under Swachh Bharat, advanced cleanliness and 
collective responsibility through partnerships among 
NGOs, corporates, Government bodies and 
community networks, mobilising youth, women 
leaders, sanitation workers and local administrations. 
India@100 Foundation has consistently strengthened 
the culture of volunteerism, recognising it as an 
enabler and driver of inclusive development and 
participatory governance. A cornerstone of this action 
has been National Volunteering Week (NVW), which 
advocates volunteerism as a strategic pillar of 
nation-building. The 13th edition of NVW mobilised 
over 2,56,447 volunteers, contributing more than 3.6 
million+ hours of service and positively impacting over 
44 million beneﬁciaries (directly and indirectly) across 
areas such as education, health, environment, 
livelihoods, skills, social inclusion and women 
empowerment. Thematic dialogues and knowledge 
sessions further reinforced the volunteerism 
ecosystem by sharing best practices.
Functional Literacy Programme (FLiP) is a ﬂagship 
initiative that focuses on the Economically Weaker 
Section (EWS) for improving their livelihood and 
enhancing disposable incomes impacting more than 
4000 beneﬁciaries this year in Raigad, Maharashtra. 
FLiP-on-Wheels initiative is expanding outreach to 
remote and rural geographies by taking digital 
learning directly to communities and equipping them 
for a digitally connected, future-ready India.
Together, these eﬀorts underscore India@100 
Foundation’s commitment to aligning each of the 
initiatives with national priorities, adopting a 
forward-looking approach and embedding impact 
measurement at the core of each action, ensuring that 
stakeholders contribute in sync with India’s journey 
towards a Viksit Bharat by 2047.
India@100 Foundation, in collaboration with NGO partners, organised education drives and creative activities in Mumbai during National 
Volunteering Week

CII’s Aﬃrmative Action work focuses on strengthening 
Industry-led interventions to promote inclusion, 
diversity and equal opportunities for Scheduled Caste 
(SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) under four heads: 
employability, entrepreneurship, education and 
employment. CII also collaborates extensively with 
other institutions towards entrepreneurship 
development, market access and ﬁnancial inclusion for 
underrepresented communities aiming to transform 
social equity into business advantage for the country 
through proactive outreach and mentorship.
AFFIRMATIVE ACTION
ADVOCACY
CII’s advocacy eﬀorts focused on strengthening 
policies and institutional mechanisms to support the 
competitiveness of SC/ST and women entrepreneurs. 
CII worked closely with the Ministry of Tribal Aﬀairs, 
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
(MSME), National SC/ST Hub and other stakeholders 
towards capacity building and encouraging the 
marginalised enterprises to propel growth.
CII also advocated wider adoption of inclusive 
sourcing practices and improved vendor onboarding 
in accordance with the procurement mandate of 
public sector enterprises (PSEs) through Government 
e-marketplace (GeM) and special vendor development 
programmes. CII recommendations also focused on 
the need for aﬀordable ﬁnance and its improved 
access for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs, greater 
awareness of concessional funding schemes, venture 
capital support and blended ﬁnance models. 
Engagements with academic institutions like IIT Delhi 
reinforced structured business acceleration and 
mentorship programmes as tools for building 
entrepreneurial capability and enterprise sustainability.
ACTION
With a focus on strengthening a structured 
engagement between PSEs and SC-ST-owned micro 
and small enterprises (MSEs) and Women MSEs, CII in Mercy Epao, Joint Secretary, Ministry of MSME at ‘BizBridge-Special 
Development Meet’ in New Delhi
partnership with the Ministry of MSME, National SC/ST 
Hub, GeM and leading Central PSEs organised the 
‘BizBridge – Vendor Development Meet for SC/ST and 
Women MSEs’. The programme helped build inclusive, 
resilient and diversiﬁed supply chains by providing a 
platform for disseminating information about 
procurement priorities, vendor onboarding processes 
and future sourcing requirements of top PSEs.
To facilitate market access, entrepreneurial capability 
and ﬁnancial inclusion, CII advanced its diversity 
initiatives through the Business Accelerator 
Programme for SC/ST entrepreneurs, implemented in 
collaboration with premier institutions: IIM Nagpur, 
IIM Sambalpur, IIM Kashipur, IIM Sirmaur, IIM Ranchi, 
IIM Raipur, IIM Mumbai and the Institute of Rural 
Management Anand (IRMA). 
An awareness workshop ‘Access to Aﬀordable Capital’ 
was also organised at IIT Delhi in collaboration with 
IFCI Venture Capital Fund Ltd which focused on 
contours of the Ambedkar Social Innovation and 
Incubation Mission (ASIIM) and other dedicated 
funding schemes for SC/ST entrepreneurs providing 
clarity on eligibility, processes and funding structures. 
These eﬀorts were further strengthened through 
GeM seller onboarding workshops, reinforcing CII’s 
integrated approach to inclusive procurement and 
entrepreneurship development.

Rural development has emerged as a critical enabler for 
industrial growth, reﬂecting deeper shifts in the 
economy. Home to two-thirds of the population and 
accounting for about 46% of the national GDP, 
according to NITI Aayog, rural India is transitioning from 
predominantly agrarian systems to more diversiﬁed 
ones with rising non-farm and industrial activity. 
Rural development and migrant workforce development 
are closely interconnected as limited economic 
opportunities in rural areas drive migration to urban and 
industrial centres. Conversely, migrant workforce 
development feeds back into rural development 
through remittances, skill transfer and social change, as 
migrant incomes support household consumption, 
education, housing and small enterprises. 
Thus, an integrated approach that strengthens rural 
development while protecting and upgrading the 
migrant workforce is essential for balanced and 
inclusive economic growth.
The CII National Task Force on Rural Development and 
Migrant Workforce outlines strategic objectives to drive 
inclusive rural transformation in India. These priorities 
include raising rural incomes and employment 
RURAL DEVELOPMENT AND
MIGRANT WORKFORCE
opportunities, strengthening rural infrastructure, 
expanding access to quality education and healthcare 
and supporting the growth of rural enterprises.
ACTION
Recognising the central role of the migrant workforce 
in India’s economic landscape, CII organised the 
National Roundtable on Migrant Workforce in 
Coimbatore. The roundtable fostered dialogue, 
collaboration and practical solutions to improve 
working conditions, welfare and inclusion of the 
migrant workforce. Discussions centred around 
skills–migration linkages and Industry migration 
mapping, social security portability and digital labour 
governance, worker housing, health and living-dignity 
infrastructure. The deliberations are expected to help 
shape future policy discussions, institutional 
strategies and collaborative initiatives.
A Compendium on ‘Industry Best Practices in Rural 
Development’ capturing case studies from companies 
and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) was 
launched at the programme. The compendium serves 
as a knowledge resource for policymakers, Industry 
leaders and practitioners working to build a more 
inclusive, fair and resilient ecosystem.
L - R: C Devarajan, Vice Chair, CII Tamil Nadu and Managing Director, URC Constructions Ltd; Anuja Bapat, Deputy Director General, Ministry of MSME; 
Kumar Jayant, Chairman and Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Industrial Investment Corporation Ltd; Shankar Vanavarayar, Chairman, CII National Task 
Force on Rural Development & Migrant Workforce and President, Kumaraguru Institutions & Executive Director, ABT Industries; C K Saji Narayanan, 
Former National President, Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh and Sanjay Awasthi, Head of Oﬃce, International Organisation for Migration releasing the 
Compendium on Rural Development at the CII National Roundtable on Migrant Workforce in Coimbatore

The CII Foundation (CIIF) was set up by CII in 2011 and 
works across India through a collaborative approach, 
partnering with Government, corporates, civil society, 
NGOs, academic institutions and other key 
stakeholders to drive social change. The Foundation’s 
interventions are anchored in three core 
pillars-creating awareness, building capacity and 
infrastructure support-customised to drive meaningful 
on-ground change. During 2025–26, CIIF strengthened 
its initiatives for India’s inclusive development.
CII FOUNDATION
CROP RESIDUE MANAGEMENT 
INITIATIVE
The Crop Residue Management initiative addresses air 
pollution caused by stubble burning in North India. 
During the year, the programme’s geographic footprint 
increased from 793 villages to over 1000 villages across 
Punjab and Haryana, spanning 11,33,676 acres of 
farmland. Over two lakh farmers were enabled to 
adopt sustainable agricultural practices through 
machinery support, technical capacity-building and 
farm straw management to turn waste into wealth. The 
programme increased ex-situ management of stubble 
(oﬀ ﬁeld straw management) by installing over 10 
biogas plants during the year. Partnerships with State 
Governments were strengthened through high-level 
meetings in Punjab and Haryana to scale interventions. 
The project interventions resulted in about 85% of 
farmland being saved from burning, preventing nearly 
2.6 million tonnes of biomass from being burnt and 
avoiding 2.35 million tCO₂e emissions, along with 
saving 100 billion litres of water.
Live demonstration and training of the new machinery delivered under 
Crop Residue Management initiatives in Haryana
Jagdish Prasad Maithani, NSG Group Commander and other delegates 
planting trees in Judola, Haryana
CLIMATE CHANGE RESILIENCE 
TREE PLANTATION INITIATIVE
Community-managed agroforestry plantations were 
developed in Farukh Nagar block, Gurugram, Haryana 
and the Sundarbans, West Bengal to support 
biodiversity.
• Twenty thousand saplings were planted across 25 
acres in three villages in Farukh Nagar
• Thirty thousand saplings were planted in the 
Sundarbans.
Challenges including monsoon waterlogging, pest 
attacks and heat stress were addressed through local 
drainage solutions, neem-based pesticides and drip 
irrigation.
WATERBODY RESTORATION
Waterbody restoration was undertaken in Tamil Nadu, 
Haryana and Maharashtra, targeting water-stressed 
and ﬂood-aﬀected regions. 
• In Tamil Nadu, under the Water Alliance Initiative, 
the rejuvenation of the 86-acre Thalapalli 
waterbody in Pedathalapalli village, Krishnagiri 
district was initiated
• In Haryana, ﬁve waterbodies were restored in 
Farukh Nagar, resulting in a 20% increase in water 
capacity and a 50% reduction in waste dumping, 
strengthening local water security and use of 
shared resources
Inauguration of Anganwadi Centre in Wayanad
DISASTER RELIEF AND
REHABILITATION
• In Maharashtra, a water management and recharge 
planning initiative was launched across ten villages 
in Khultabad block, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar 
district. Baseline assessments were undertaken to 
develop a Detailed Project Report (DPR) to guide 
long-term groundwater recharge and sustainable 
water use intervention, following which, 
interventions were rolled out on sustainable 
farming practices and rainwater harvesting 
structures. The programme aims to ensure 
long-term water security in these areas. 
WASTE MANAGEMENT
To mitigate environmental and health impacts of 
ineﬃcient waste management, CIIF strengthened its 
waste management initiatives across project sites in 
Kerala and Ladakh, complementing local Government 
eﬀorts under the Swachh Bharat Mission.
In Leh, Ladakh, two Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) 
established in 2024-25 for supporting scientiﬁc 
segregation, sorting and recycling, processed 74,838 
kg (74.8 tonnes) waste. Additionally, 65% households 
practice segregation at source.
'Chelode Chellanam’, a CIIF initiative in Chellanam, 
Kerala, promoted self-sustaining waste management 
with the panchayat and Haritha Karma Sena operating 
MRF facility handling 1.25 tonnes of waste per day.
As part of the Swachhata Hi Seva campaign under the 
theme Swachhotsav, CIIF implemented the 
nationwide Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath initiative across 
India, engaging children, farmers, waste workers and 
local communities in cleanliness drives and awareness 
activities. The campaign reinforced source-level waste 
management, hygiene practices and collective action 
for cleaner and healthier public spaces.
CIIF supported disaster-aﬀected communities through 
infrastructure-led rehabilitation. In Wayanad, Kerala, 
eﬀorts focused on reconstructing community 
facilities, including a tribal kitchen and renovating 
Anganwadi centres impacted by landslides, 
re-establishing safe spaces for nutrition, early 
childcare and community activities.
Following ﬂoods and landslides in Himachal Pradesh, 
CIIF constructed temporary housing shelters in Mandi 
district for aﬀected families.
EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATION
CIIF strengthened Early Childhood Education (ECE) 
through Anganwadi centres in Andhra Pradesh, 
Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, working closely with 
State Governments and local partners under the 
Integrated Child development Services (ICDS) 
implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child 
Development. The focus remained on improving 
learning environments, strengthening capacities of 
Anganwadi workers and increasing community 
engagement to support holistic child development.
To strengthen science education, CIIF initiated a STEM 
Science Lab initiative in Gummudipoondi, Tamil Nadu, 
wherein six schools were identiﬁed and customised 
Information, Education and Communication (IEC) 
materials were developed and lab equipment set up to 
support hands-on learning and classroom engagement.
In Thirumudivakkam, Tamil Nadu, an education 
infrastructure improvement project was initiated at a 
Government Higher Secondary School.
The project includes renovation of ﬁve classrooms and 
essential facility upgrades to create safer, 
better-equipped learning spaces.
STRENGTHENING
HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS
The health systems strengthening programme in 
Chandauli District, Uttar Pradesh, focuses on eight villages 
in Dhanapur block. The programme aims to strengthen 
community access to public healthcare and nutrition, 
improve infrastructure, raise health awareness among 
children and adolescents and build frontline capacity. 
School-based health awareness programmes in Uttar 
Pradesh and Haryana promoted positive behavioural 
change among students, encouraging informed health 
choices and peer-to-peer learning on topics such as 
menstrual health and nutrition.
Annual Report 2025-26144
Annpurna Devi, Minister of Women and Child Development; Sanjiv Puri, Immediate Past President, CII and Chairman & Managing Director, ITC Ltd and 
Chandrajit Banerjee, Director General, CII with the winners of the CII Woman Exemplar Awards at the CII Annual Business Summit 2025 in New Delhi
SKILLING AND LIVELIHOODS
Rural livelihood programmes across Uttar Pradesh, 
Jharkhand, West Bengal, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu 
promoted locally viable enterprises such as 
beekeeping, poultry farming, food processing and 
digital literacy. CII Foundation is implementing a 
digital literacy programme for youth aged 16-25 years 
across Lakhimpur Kheri and Barabanki districts and 
Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh. Over the course of three 
months, over 600 youth have been trained in 
foundational digital skills. In Ballari district, Karnataka, 
CIIF implemented a Famer Producer Organisation 
(FPO)-led initiative to strengthen red chilli value chain 
across Kurgodu, Siruguppa and Sandur taluks, 
focusing on improved farm practices, cost eﬃciency 
and farmer resilience. During the year, 1300 farmers 
across six FPOs were engaged through ﬁeld 
monitoring and village-level training, promoting 
sustainable cultivation and peer learning.
CII Foundation supported initiatives on skill building 
facilitated by the CII Skills Department to expand 
employability through youth skilling, digital and soft 
skills training and placement-linked programmes 
across multiple states, aligning workforce capabilities 
with Industry demand.
CIIF also rolled out a disability and livelihood project 
‘Livelihood on Wheels’, addressing the dual challenges 
of mobility and unemployment, enabling persons with 
locomotor disabilities to achieve ﬁnancial self-reliance 
through assistive technology support. Across Nagpur, 
Indore and Jammu, 57 persons with locomotor 
disabilities were equipped with customised 
NeoMotion electric wheelchairs (NeoFly/NeoBolt) 
who were onboarded as food delivery platform 
delivery executives.
WOMAN EXEMPLAR PROGRAM
The Woman Exemplar Program identiﬁes, recognises 
and empowers grassroots women through capacity 
building and training women leaders working in 
health, education, micro-enterprise and community 
strengthening. 
The ‘Woman Exemplar Award 2025’ was presented to 
20 Exemplars by Smt Annpurna Devi, Minister of 
Women and Child Development at the CII Annual 
Business Summit 2025. Awardees were selected after 
a rigorous process from over 400 nominations. One 
winner across each category also received a cash prize 
of INR 3 lakh. 2025 marked the 20th year of the 
program, which has created a network of over 150 
Women Exemplars, collectively impacting more than
two million lives across 25 states.
CIIF expanded this national-level programme to the 
state level with the ‘Empowering Champions of Change 
Programme’, ﬁrst initiated in Assam last year. Launched 
in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan in November, it 
covers 30 women leaders reaching out to vulnerable 
populations in 20 districts across the two states.
The growing national network of Woman Exemplars 
has emerged as a platform for cross-sector 
engagement and collective advocacy.
Empowering Widows
CIIF initiated a national programme to empower 
widows through skills development and economic 
inclusion. During the year, training was initiated for 
1000 widows in Vrindavan, Uttar Pradesh marking the 
ﬁrst phase of a larger eﬀort aimed at reaching one 
lakh widows across India.

Annual Report 2025-26146
Over the last decade, Corporate Social Responsibility 
(CSR) legislation under the Companies Act, 2013 has 
provided a robust framework for companies to design 
and deliver meaningful interventions. Between 2014-15 
and 2023-24, companies in India spent over INR 2.2 lakh 
crore on CSR initiatives. Annual spending has consistently 
grown, tripling from INR 10,000 crore in 2014-15 to 
nearly INR 35,000 crore in 2023-24. As CSR evolved from 
a compliance-driven approach to an impact-oriented one, 
CII remained at the forefront advocating strategic shifts 
such as directing CSR investments towards priority states 
and aspirational districts. These eﬀorts have shaped a 
more focused, collaborative and outcome-driven 
approach to development initiatives.
ACTION
CII convened the ﬁrst edition of Kashi Samvaad 2025 
at Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi, in 
partnership with the Department of Social Welfare, 
Government of Uttar Pradesh and the CII Foundation. 
The summit was inaugurated by Smt Anupriya Patel, 
Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, who 
underscored that national aspirations cannot be 
fulﬁlled without active public participation. 
Discussions spanned critical themes including 
healthcare, education and skilling, rural prosperity, 
clean & green India and artiﬁcial intelligence for social 
transformation, with participation from senior 
DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVES
Government leaders, Industry, Academia and social 
sector experts. A deﬁning outcome was the release of 
the ‘Kashi Declaration’, outlining key recommendations 
for inclusive development, alongside the signing of a 
memorandum of understanding between CII and BHU 
to strengthen collaboration in research, innovation and 
rural development.
CII supported organisations in enhancing the depth and 
sustainability of their CSR interventions by introducing a 
three-day design-led programme – Design for Ecosystem 
Transformation. Tailored for senior CSR and civil society 
organisation leaders, the programme equipped 
participants with advanced design frameworks to 
navigate complexity, address ambiguity, prototype 
innovative solutions and maximise impact. Through a 
blend of mini-lectures, hands-on activities, peer learning 
and expert engagement, participants explored 
opportunities across strategy, operations, value creation, 
users, resources and capabilities, enabling a holistic and 
integrated approach to scaling social initiatives.
CII–INDIA BUSINESS AND 
DISABILITY NETWORK
A signiﬁcant focus area was advancing disability 
inclusion across Indian workplaces through the 
CII–India Business and Disability Network (IBDN).

with Physical Disabilities at the CII Awards for Excellence in Disability Inclusion 2025 in Lucknow
inclusive hiring and advancement, allyship and 
community engagement. A report ‘Inclusion Insights: 
Best Practices of Award-Aspiring Companies’ was 
developed, capturing best inclusion practices oﬀering 
both a reﬂection of progress achieved and a blueprint 
to inspire broader Industry transformation.
The year also saw renewed momentum towards 
building an accessible ecosystem beyond workplaces. 
CII launched a consultative Roundtable Series on 
Inclusive Tourism, Hospitality and Sports, with the ﬁrst 
in Goa, as a precursor to the International Purple Fest. 
Policymakers, Industry leaders and advocacy groups 
co-created an actionable framework for barrier-free 
travel and leisure experiences. Discussions highlighted 
Goa’s initiatives to make adventure sports such as 
scuba diving and paragliding accessible to PwDs, 
reinforcing that accessibility is not only a social 
imperative but also a powerful economic driver with 
the potential to generate employment, unlock new 
markets and contribute to GDP growth.
CII-IBDN partnered in the ﬁrst National Accessibility 
Summit on Sports, Tourism, Transport and ICT in New 
Delhi. The summit convened Government 
representatives, global organisations, architects, 
transport authorities, cultural institutions, digital 
leaders and accessibility practitioners. 
Strengthening leadership capability remained central to 
sustaining inclusion eﬀorts. CII continued its ﬂagship 
CII–IBDN Certiﬁcate Training Programme on ‘Creating 
Disability-Inclusive Leaders at the Workplace,’ now in its 
sixth year. Delivered by 13 expert faculty members across 
seven modules over two weeks, the programme built 
organisational capability, fostered inclusive mindsets and 
equipped leaders with practical tools to embed disability 
inclusion into everyday business practices.
Working closely with Industry, Government and civil 
society organisations, CII–IBDN supported companies in 
moving beyond compliance towards adopting inclusive 
policies, creating accessible workplaces and enabling 
equitable employment practices for Persons with 
Disabilities (PwDs). Through policy advocacy, thought 
leadership, capacity building and action-oriented 
platforms, the Network strengthened organisational 
inclusion journeys, built disability-conﬁdent workforces 
and drove measurable and sustainable impact.
ACTION
The CII–IBDN National Conference, held alongside the 
Zero Project Conference India in New Delhi, facilitated 
insightful discussions on accessibility, inclusive 
employment and assistive technologies, inspiring 
collective action and collaboration. A unique highlight 
was the Global Ability Photography Challenge 
exhibition, alongside a dedicated technology showcase 
featuring assistive solutions for PwDs.
Translating dialogue into recognition and action, CII 
launched the CII Awards for Excellence in Disability 
Inclusion, marking a landmark step towards 
mainstreaming disability inclusion within Industry.
The awards celebrate organisations that go beyond 
compliance to embed accessibility, equity and 
opportunity into their organisational ethos, serving as 
exemplars and catalysts for systemic change. 
Seventy-eight companies from over 20 states applied 
in the inaugural edition. The awards culminated in a 
prestigious ceremony, where awards were presented 
by Shri Asim Arun, Minister of Social Welfare and SC/ST 
Welfare, Government of Uttar Pradesh, recognising 
leadership across large enterprises and MSMEs. The 
rigorous multi-stage assessment process evaluated 
organisations on inclusive governance, physical and 
digital accessibility, workplace culture, sensitisation,

CII actively strengthened India's sports ecosystem 
through initiatives focused on promoting inclusivity, 
sparking innovation and achieving excellence. 
Through dynamic platforms that encouraged 
collaboration among stakeholders, CII supported 
grassroots talent development from the ground up 
and celebrated key successes across the sports sector. 
Eﬀorts targeted areas such as enhancing corporate 
wellness programmes through sports participation, 
identifying and nurturing young talent at the 
community level and blending cutting-edge 
technology with sustainable practices for Indian 
sports. By bringing together Industry, Government 
and the sports community, these activities fostered 
meaningful discussions, inspired concrete actions and 
highlighted remarkable contributions. They 
demonstrated the immense potential of sports to 
build a healthier, more equitable society and position 
India as a global powerhouse.
SPORTS
ACTION 
CII SCORECARD 2025, the 10th edition of India's 
premier sports business conclave, was organised in 
collaboration with the Ministry of Youth Aﬀairs and 
Sports (MYAS) and aligned with the India AI Impact 
Summit. The conclave featured sessions on 
governance, artiﬁcial intelligence (AI), infrastructure 
and the presentation of the CII Sports Business 
Awards. Keynote addresses by Shri Hari Ranjan Rao, 
Secretary, MYAS and other leaders emphasised a 
National Sports Governance Act, Khelo Bharat Niti 
integration and sustainable infrastructure for India's 
2030 Commonwealth and 2036 Olympics bids. Panels 
highlighted the need for athlete data libraries, 
grassroots digitisation, Corporate Social 
Responsibility, Public Private Partnership investments 
and accessibility for para-athletes, women coaches 
and physical education educators.
The CII Sports Business Awards celebrated 
outstanding contributions across the sports 
ecosystem. Key awards included the Legacy of 
Excellence Award for long-standing contributions to 
India’s sports movement, the Grassroots Sports 
Initiative Award for empowering the marginalised girl 
child through sports and education, Best State for 
Sports Development and Best Sport Federation for 
advancing inclusivity in Indian sports.
CII also hosted the CII Golf Masters in September-an 
exclusive networking tournament designed to 
strengthen business-sport partnerships. The 
tournament saw enthusiastic participation from over 
80 players, including policymakers, senior Government 
oﬃcials, foreign embassy representatives and 
corporate leaders. More than a sporting contest, the 
Golf Masters served as a prominent platform for 
dialogue, collaboration and relationship-building 
among India’s top decision-makers committed to 
advancing the nation’s sporting economy.
Winners of CII Sports Business Awards 2025 in New Delhi
CII SPORTSCOM Industry Confederation plays a 
pivotal role in shaping India’s sports ecosystem by 
combining focused policy advocacy with 
ecosystem-building initiatives to position India as a 
sports-focused nation and a global hub for sports 
goods manufacturing. Incubated by CII, SPORTSCOM 
is a credible Industry platform engaging startups, 
manufacturers, athletes, investors and policymakers 
to align sectoral growth with national priorities.
SPORTSCOM
ADVOCACY
• Following sustained representations by CII 
SPORTSCOM, sports goods manufacturing was 
transferred from the Department for Promotion of 
Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) to the Ministry 
of Youth Aﬀairs & Sports (Notiﬁcation No SO 
3919(E)), aligning the sector with national sports 
objectives and resulting in the constitution of a NITI 
Aayog Task Force on sports goods manufacturing 
and exports, with SPORTSCOM as a member
• Through structured representations to the 
Government, CII SPORTSCOM addressed 
diﬀerential GST rates under HSN Code 9506, 
advocating rate rationalisation to ease compliance 
and improve competitiveness, which reduced GST 
on sports goods from 18% to 12% and 5%.

Vidushpat Singhania, Treasurer, SPORTSCOM Industry Confederation and Managing Partner, Krida Legal; Alok Pandey, CEO, AIC-IIT Delhi; Vivek Singh,

ACTION 
CII SPORTSCOM strengthened policy advocacy and 
ecosystem development for the sports sector through 
focused, outcome-oriented platforms. A ﬂagship 
initiative was SPORTSCOM – Giving Wings to Dreams 
Conclave, which created a dedicated forum for sports 
startups and Industry professionals to engage with 
investors, policymakers and ecosystem enablers.
The conclave enabled live startup pitching, facilitated 
funding, strategic partnerships and advanced policy 
dialogue on innovation, entrepreneurship and 
sustainable growth in Indian sport.
In collaboration with NITI Aayog, SPORTSCOM 
organised a workshop on sports goods 
manufacturing which focused on policy support, 
innovation, export competitiveness and scaling 
manufacturing capabilities. The discussions 
articulated a clear vision to position India as a global 
hub for sports goods manufacturing, with a target to 
capture 20% of the global sports equipment market 
by 2036.
Through these targeted engagements, CII 
SPORTSCOM strengthened policy alignment, 
improved the regulatory and investment 
environment and advanced India’s ambition to 
emerge as a global leader in sports manufacturing 
and innovation.

The Young Indians (Yi) initiative deepened its role as a 
platform for youth-led policy dialogue, leadership 
development and nation-building, aligning its 
initiatives with national priorities and the vision of 
Viksit Bharat@2047. Yi combined grassroots action 
with structured engagement with policymakers, 
institutions and global partners to translate youth 
aspirations into scalable, policy-relevant outcomes.
ACTION
Yi’s policy advocacy and stakeholder engagement was 
anchored through high-impact national platforms. The 
YiFi National Entrepreneurship and Finance Summit 
served as a platform to deliberate on 
entrepreneurship, ﬁnance, innovation and leadership. 
The Summit reinforced youth-led entrepreneurship as 
a key driver of economic growth and contributed to 
shaping discourse on startup ﬁnancing, IPO readiness 
and innovation-led development.
The 22nd Young Indians National Summit further 
strengthened Yi’s policy engagement by bringing 
together young leaders with senior policymakers and 
national institutions. High-level interactions with 
ministers from the Ministries of Defence and Skill 
Development & Entrepreneurship, as well as the CEO 
of NITI Aayog, underscored the role of youth 
institutions in constitutional values, leadership, 
skilling, defence preparedness and entrepreneurship. 
These dialogues reinforced Yi’s contribution to policy 
narratives around youth participation in governance, 
skills and nation-building.
Beyond national summits, Yi expanded its strategic 
partnerships to amplify policy and institutional impact. 
memorandums of understanding (MoUs) with the Abu 
Dhabi Chamber’s Youth Business Council, IIT Madras 
and Masters’ Union, along with a Letter of Intent with 
UNICEF India, strengthened cross-border startups 
collaboration, student innovation, Industry–Academia 
linkages and youth-led solutions for child rights and 
YOUNG INDIANS (Yi)
inclusive development. These partnerships positioned 
Yi as a credible youth partner in policy-aligned 
innovation and social development.
Yi’s on-ground impact reinforced the credibility of its 
policy voice. Yi engaged over 8445 Members and 
reached 1.94 lakh Thalir students, 2.59 lakh YUVA 
college students and 15,123 rural stakeholders, while 
training more than 31,000 Certiﬁed Accident First 
Responders under Yi Farishtey. Rural initiatives 
beneﬁted over 12,000 villagers, while large-scale 
climate action included 11.39 lakh Miyawaki 
plantations, 2.85 lakh mangroves, 1.58 lakh fruit trees, 
water rejuvenation and responsible e-waste 
processing. Project Masoom strengthened child safety 
through three Masoom Model Schools, directly 
impacting 965 students, parents and educators, with a 
cumulative reach of 2.51 lakh students across 
chapters. Yi’s accessibility initiatives improved 
inclusion for an annual footfall of 12.25 lakh people, 
strengthening evidence-based advocacy on inclusion 
and sustainability.
Through structured policy dialogue, national platforms 
and measurable social impact, Young Indians reinforced 
the role of youth as partners in policy, innovation and 
implementation, contributing meaningfully to India’s 
long-term development agenda.

ACTION
JRD AWARDS
The JRD Tata Awards 2025, BYST’s ﬂagship celebration 
of entrepreneurial excellence, featured thought- 
provoking sessions, an innovation exhibition and the 
launch of key knowledge resources and sustainability 
initiatives. Shri Jyotiraditya Scindia, Minister of 
Communications and Development of North Eastern 
Region graced the occasion as Chief Guest, felicitating 
outstanding Grampreneurs® from across India.
The hybrid event witnessed participation of nearly 
3000 attendees nationwide. Strategic memoranda of 
understanding (MoUs) were also exchanged, 
reinforcing BYST’s commitment to strengthening 
India’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. 
Bharatiya Yuva Shakti Trust (BYST) helps underprivileged 
youth transform business ideas into successful ventures 
with mentor support, aiming to turn job seekers into job 
creators. Over the last 33 years, BYST supported 
entrepreneurs have created over 5,00,000 jobs across 
21 clusters spread across the nation. BYST has 
empowered grassroots entrepreneurs by reaching out 
to and counselling 2.5 million youth and training nearly 
2,00,000 in entrepreneurship. Around 22,000 mentors, 
trained and certiﬁed by the National Institute of Micro, 
Small and Medium Enterprises and City & Guilds, have 
mentored 51,000 Grampreneurs®. Up to August, the 
Grampreneurs® received cumulative ﬁnancial aid worth 
INR 850 crore from eight partner nationalised banks.
BHARATIYA YUVA SHAKTI
TRUST
NEW PARTNERSHIPS
BYST partnered with two companies to strengthen 
youth entrepreneurship and employability through 
CSR-led initiatives. Genpact India Pvt Ltd supported 
the AI Digital Twin Entrepreneur Platform to enhance 
mentoring and enterprise development across 
underserved regions. Yardi Software India Pvt Ltd 
mentored 100 entrepreneurs and trained 150 
institutional mentors under the Young Grampreneur® 
Development Programme in Chhatrapati Sambhaji 
Nagar, Maharashtra.
CYBER AWARENESS AND FINANCIAL 
HYGIENE CAMPAIGN
BYST successfully facilitated a series of cyber 
awareness and ﬁnancial hygiene workshops for CII, 
covering ﬁve locations - Faridabad, Raygada, Ramgarh, 
Pune and Kolhapur. The initiative empowered over 
400 women with practical knowledge on 
cybersecurity, safe digital payments, credit 
management and ﬁnancial planning. 
BUSINESS WORKSHOP FOR 
HIGHFLIERS 
BYST Highﬂiers from Sriperumbudur and Chennai 
clusters participated in a two-day business workshop 
by the CII Centre of Excellence on Employment & 
Livelihood that covered topics like business 
fundamentals, ﬁnancial management, team building, 
marketing and leadership. Sessions included proﬁt, 
loss, risk management, cash ﬂow and sales strategy. 
Entrepreneurs gained practical insights, enhanced 
networking and leadership skills, culminating in 
testimonials, certiﬁcate distribution and addresses by 
Industry leaders.
DEVI AWARDS
Honouring transformative work in entrepreneurship 
development, The New Indian Express presented the 
Devi Awards 2025 to Lakshmi V Venkatesan, Founding 
and Managing Trustee, BYST, recognising signiﬁcant 
contributions towards nurturing young 
entrepreneurs.
L-R: Lakshmi Venkataraman Venkatesan, Founding and Managing 
Trustee, BYST; Subodh Bhargava, Chairman, Tata Communications; 
Jyotiraditya Scindia, Minister of Communication and Development of 
North Eastern Region and Shreekant Somany, Chairman and Managing 
Director, Somany Ceramics at the JRD Tata Awards 2025 in New Delhi

CWL turned its strategy of creating knowledge, 
bringing people together and working across sectors 
into real policy inﬂuence and advocacy. CWL used its 
ﬁndings to shape conversations and held 20 detailed 
roundtables in nine cities, turning research and 
practitioner insights into clear reform ideas, 
opportunities for shared learning and draft policy 
frameworks for local Governments, ministries and 
Industry groups. 
The Edge Inclusion & Competitiveness Summit 
strengthened this research to action pipeline by 
gathering leaders from diﬀerent sectors to discuss 
building inclusive and high performing organisations. 
The summit highlighted how diversity, equity and 
inclusion directly connect to productivity, talent 
attraction and risk management. A key example was 
the launch of She Moves Logistics, an initiative 
focused on increasing women’s participation and 
Established in 2023, the CII Centre for Women 
Leadership (CWL) aims to drive transformation 
towards women leadership within the economy.
CWL through its policy advocacy, capacity building 
and ground interventions works with women, 
Industry and the Government to co-create 
ecosystems that enable women to participate, grow 
and lead within the economy.
CII CENTRE FOR WOMEN
LEADERSHIP
career growth in the logistics sector. This showed 
CWL’s approach in action: identify barriers through 
research, co-create solutions with Industry and spread 
successful practices by recognising early adopters.
CWL also hosted the ﬁrst Gender Parity Business 
Awards at the summit, recognising companies that 
integrated inclusion in their business strategy, 
operations and decision-making processes. The 
awards celebrated leaders advancing equity and 
inclusion, creating incentive for companies to adopt 
and expand gender responsive policies.
CWL hosted the ﬁrst Gender Policy Symposium to 
promote data driven, inclusive policymaking in key 
areas such as public schemes, health and climate 
resilience. By bringing together leaders from Industry, 
Academia, Government and the research community, 
the symposium strengthened CWL’s policy inﬂuence 
and highlighted gaps in data, implementation and 
measurement-especially in ﬁelds where women’s 
leadership is often undervalued. 
CWL released three evidence based reports oﬀering 
clear, practical guidance for designing gender inclusive 
policies. The symposium proved to be a catalyst for 
change, showing how evidence and leadership can 
work together to drive transformative policy shifts for 
gender equity in India. It underscored the need for 
public policy that truly reﬂects women’s lived 
experiences across regions, sectors and identities.

EASTERN REGION
In 2025, CII Eastern Region (CII-ER) aligned its 
initiatives with the national theme ‘Accelerating 
Competitiveness: Globalisation, Inclusivity, 
Sustainability, Trust’. The focus was on enhancing 
competitiveness and global integration through 
sustainable, inclusive practices, while continuing policy 
advocacy, capacity building and targeted interventions 
to strengthen regional linkages with national and 
global economies.
ADVOCACY
CII-ER engaged with State Governments to support 
policy formulation and strengthen the business 
environment, providing recommendations to address 
Industry challenges, enhance competitiveness and 
promote sustainable and inclusive growth across key 
sectors.
• Consolidated Members’ perspectives into policy 
proposals to accelerate industrial growth, enhance 
competitiveness and strengthen investment 
readiness under the West Bengal Industrial Policy
• Participated in consultation with the Departments 
of Labour, Micro, Small And Medium Enterprises 
And Textiles (MSME&T) and Industry to ﬁnalise 
guidelines for night shifts for women in factories
• Supported the development of a Net Zero Carbon 
Roadmap, outlining sector-wise transition 
pathways towards a low-carbon economy
• Addressed gaps in Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) 
infrastructure in Kolkata, impacting commercial 
ﬂeets and clean mobility investments
• Coordinated with district administrations and 
stakeholders in North Bengal to operationalise the 
Rural Entrepreneur Hub (REH)
• Submitted a whitepaper to the Transport 
Department on improving last-mile connectivity in 
industrial zones, logistics hubs and rural corridors
• Supported the establishment of sector-focused 
institutions in West Bengal to strengthen technical 
expertise and operational eﬃciency.
JHARKHAND
• Recommendations were submitted on 
rationalising value-added tax (VAT) on natural gas 
as Jharkhand’s VAT rate is signiﬁcantly higher than 
other major industrial regions.
ODISHA
• Recommended improving infrastructure, access to 
credit, supply-chain linkages and regulatory 
eﬃciency, in alignment with the State’s 
development vision
• Recommended operationalising a cohesive 
Information Technology (IT) Policy framework with 
clear guidelines, digital single-window systems and 
support for MSMEs, startups and talent 
development.
BIHAR
• Developed Bihar’s Vision Document 2025, 
outlining the State’s emergence as one of India’s 
fastest-growing economies driven by policy 
reforms, infrastructure investment and strategic 
market access
• Contributed strategic inputs to strengthen ease of 
doing business (EoDB) and accelerate key policy 
reforms under the Bihar Industrial Investment 
Promotion Package 2025. Key recommendations 
included provisions on subsidised land, assured 
power supply, ﬁnancial incentives, export 
facilitation and industrial security
• Submitted key recommendations on solar 
incentives, transmission support, ease of approvals 
and biomass integration, which were accepted and 
incorporated into the Bihar New Renewable 
Energy Policy 2025.

MSMEs 
Initiatives like the Chhattisgarh MSME Conclave and 
Scaling Jharkhand MSMEs aimed at enhancing access 
to ﬁnance, strengthening capabilities and expanding 
market linkages through Industry dialogue and 
strategy development. 
The Investment Yatra – IPO Readiness and Capital 
Markets Connect, was organised in association with 
the National Stock Exchange, across Kolkata, Patna, 
Bhubaneswar and Jamshedpur to strengthen the SME 
Initial Public Oﬀering (IPO) ecosystem. MSME 
Business Connect helped MSMEs understand quality 
standards, sustainability practices and vendor 
onboarding processes of large companies and public 
sector undertakings (PSUs).
Sustainability
Sustainability initiatives focused on environmental, 
social and governance (ESG)-integration, capacity 
building and responsible Industry practices. The Green 
Industry Conclave advanced discussions on ESG 
integration, circular economy practices and 
impact-driven growth, while the Green Steel and Mining 
Summit explored decarbonisation pathways, green 
technologies, policy frameworks and best practices. 
Capacity building was strengthened through an 
eight-week ESG Masterclass. Safety and sustainability 
themes were addressed through the Safety Symposium 
and Exposition, Jharkhand Safety Talk, Odisha Corporate 
Social Responsibility (CSR) Conclave and a dedicated 
Safety and Sustainability Workshop, emphasising 
leadership-driven safety culture, technology adoption 
and alignment with regulatory frameworks.
Family Business
The Family Business Conclave delved into 
generational transition, leadership, digital 
transformation and professionalisation, highlighting 
experiences of family enterprises and their future 
growth potential.
INTERNATIONAL OUTREACH
CII expanded its international outreach to strengthen 
global partnerships and enhance export 
competitiveness. The Mining and Construction 
Equipment Division organised a delegation to 
Australia to strengthen collaboration in mining 
technology, equipment manufacturing and critical 
minerals with engagements involving Government 
representatives, senior diplomats and Industry 
Members.
Several meetings were held with inbound trade 
delegations and senior diplomats to exchange ideas 
and opportunities. Capacity building programmes 
were organised on export packaging, branding and 
export ﬁnance, while an export-import (EXIM) 
conference showcased opportunities in international 
trade and export competitiveness.
Engagement with the Singapore Economic 
Development Board further advanced bilateral trade, 
investment and business cooperation and 
programmes were organised to sensitise Members 
regarding opportunities arising from Free Trade 
Agreements.
RECOGNITION OF EXCELLENCE
The 36th Workskills Competition and 25th Supervisory 
Skills Competition promoted skill enhancement, 
motivation and excellence by recognising outstanding 
supervisory performance and encouraging continuous 
upskilling.
The Safety, Health and Environment (SHE) Awards 
recognised exemplary performance in environmental 
management, occupational health, safety and 
sustainable development through a rigorous ﬁve-star 
onsite assessment framework. The Energy 
Conservation (ENCON) Awards honoured 
organisations for sustained and systematic eﬀorts in 
improving energy eﬃciency and achieving measurable 
energy savings.
The ‘Joyee’ Initiative recognised and honoured 
caregiver institutions for their compassionate and 
sustained support to vulnerable communities.
PUBLICATIONS
Published by CII-ER, a portfolio of reports, 
whitepapers and compendiums provided policy 
insight, sectoral analysis and Industry best practices to 
support inclusive and sustainable industrial growth 
across Eastern India.
MEMBERSHIP ENGAGEMENT
CII-ER facilitated 14 Members’ Meets, 19 Road Shows 
and 19 induction sessions across ﬁve states, leading to 
a total Membership increase of 8.53%.

East India Summit

highlighted Eastern India’s emergence as an economic 
growth hub. Policymakers and Industry leaders from 
Bihar, Odisha, West Bengal and Chhattisgarh outlined 
their development visions, showcasing reforms,

regarding opportunities arising from Free Trade 
Agreements.
RECOGNITION OF EXCELLENCE
The 36th Workskills Competition and 25th Supervisory 
Skills Competition promoted skill enhancement, 
motivation and excellence by recognising outstanding 
supervisory performance and encouraging continuous 
upskilling.
The Safety, Health and Environment (SHE) Awards 
recognised exemplary performance in environmental 
management, occupational health, safety and 
sustainable development through a rigorous ﬁve-star 
onsite assessment framework. The Energy 
Conservation (ENCON) Awards honoured 
organisations for sustained and systematic eﬀorts in 
improving energy eﬃciency and achieving measurable 
energy savings.
The ‘Joyee’ Initiative recognised and honoured 
caregiver institutions for their compassionate and 
sustained support to vulnerable communities.
PUBLICATIONS
Published by CII-ER, a portfolio of reports, 
whitepapers and compendiums provided policy 
insight, sectoral analysis and Industry best practices to 
support inclusive and sustainable industrial growth 
across Eastern India.
MEMBERSHIP ENGAGEMENT
CII-ER facilitated 14 Members’ Meets, 19 Road Shows 
and 19 induction sessions across ﬁve states, leading to 
a total Membership increase of 8.53%.
Railways
The Rail Synergy Summit focused on network 
electriﬁcation, high-speed and freight corridor 
development, modernisation of stations and tracks, 
adoption of digital and artiﬁcial intelligence (AI)-based 
maintenance technologies and green ﬁnancing.
Education
The Education East Summit highlighted 
human-centred innovation to build adaptable, 
inclusive and future-ready education systems.
Energy
The Energy Conclave deliberated on the evolving energy 
landscape of Eastern India, highlighting modernisation 
of conventional power, expansion of renewables and 
green hydrogen, development of decentralised grids, 
energy-eﬃcient manufacturing innovations and 
alignment between producers and high-consumption 
sectors to support India’s Net Zero transition.
Manufacturing
Manufacturing-related engagements emphasised 
enhancing competitiveness, inclusivity and 
sustainability. Highlighting the role of Industry 4.0 in 
strengthening supply chain resilience, the Jharkhand 
Manufacturing Conclave promoted sustainable 
manufacturing practices whereas the Manufacturing 
Conclave East focused on manufacturing across 
sectors such as railways, defence, automobiles, steel, 
mining and heavy industries.
Information and Communications 
Technology (ICT)
Engagements focused on digital transformation and 
emerging technologies. ICT East explored strategies 
to strengthen India’s position as a global technology 
hub and the ‘AI: The New Engine of Enterprise’ session 
highlighted the growing role of human–AI 
collaboration in driving enterprise productivity.
Logistics
Logistics initiatives emphasised infrastructure 
development, sustainability and multimodal 
integration. Logis EAST 2025 Exhibition and 
Conference focused on infrastructure expansion, port 
eﬃciency, freight corridors, sustainability, 
MSME-integration and national initiatives such as 
Sagarmala and PM Gati Shakti. The Odisha Logistics 
Summit highlighted the development of Odisha’s 
multimodal logistics ecosystem, emphasising port-led 
growth, clean mobility and digital transformation in 
logistics.
Startups 
The Innovation Conference emphasised the role of 
technology, talent and global networks in 
strengthening India’s innovation ecosystem, 
highlighting Eastern India’s growing startups 
recognised by Department for Promotion of Industry 
and Internal Trade (DPIIT).
