pages.text:
MSMEs 
Initiatives like the Chhattisgarh MSME Conclave and 
Scaling Jharkhand MSMEs aimed at enhancing access 
to ﬁnance, strengthening capabilities and expanding 
market linkages through Industry dialogue and 
strategy development. 
The Investment Yatra – IPO Readiness and Capital 
Markets Connect, was organised in association with 
the National Stock Exchange, across Kolkata, Patna, 
Bhubaneswar and Jamshedpur to strengthen the SME 
Initial Public Oﬀering (IPO) ecosystem. MSME 
Business Connect helped MSMEs understand quality 
standards, sustainability practices and vendor 
onboarding processes of large companies and public 
sector undertakings (PSUs).
Sustainability
Sustainability initiatives focused on environmental, 
social and governance (ESG)-integration, capacity 
building and responsible Industry practices. The Green 
Industry Conclave advanced discussions on ESG 
integration, circular economy practices and 
impact-driven growth, while the Green Steel and Mining 
Summit explored decarbonisation pathways, green 
technologies, policy frameworks and best practices. 
Capacity building was strengthened through an 
eight-week ESG Masterclass. Safety and sustainability 
themes were addressed through the Safety Symposium 
and Exposition, Jharkhand Safety Talk, Odisha Corporate 
Social Responsibility (CSR) Conclave and a dedicated 
Safety and Sustainability Workshop, emphasising 
leadership-driven safety culture, technology adoption 
and alignment with regulatory frameworks.
Family Business
The Family Business Conclave delved into 
generational transition, leadership, digital 
transformation and professionalisation, highlighting 
experiences of family enterprises and their future 
growth potential.
INTERNATIONAL OUTREACH
CII expanded its international outreach to strengthen 
global partnerships and enhance export 
competitiveness. The Mining and Construction 
Equipment Division organised a delegation to 
Australia to strengthen collaboration in mining 
technology, equipment manufacturing and critical 
minerals with engagements involving Government 
representatives, senior diplomats and Industry 
Members.
Several meetings were held with inbound trade 
delegations and senior diplomats to exchange ideas 
and opportunities. Capacity building programmes 
were organised on export packaging, branding and 
export ﬁnance, while an export-import (EXIM) 
conference showcased opportunities in international 
trade and export competitiveness.
Engagement with the Singapore Economic 
Development Board further advanced bilateral trade, 
investment and business cooperation and 
programmes were organised to sensitise Members 
regarding opportunities arising from Free Trade 
Agreements.
RECOGNITION OF EXCELLENCE
The 36th Workskills Competition and 25th Supervisory 
Skills Competition promoted skill enhancement, 
motivation and excellence by recognising outstanding 
supervisory performance and encouraging continuous 
upskilling.
The Safety, Health and Environment (SHE) Awards 
recognised exemplary performance in environmental 
management, occupational health, safety and 
sustainable development through a rigorous ﬁve-star 
onsite assessment framework. The Energy 
Conservation (ENCON) Awards honoured 
organisations for sustained and systematic eﬀorts in 
improving energy eﬃciency and achieving measurable 
energy savings.
The ‘Joyee’ Initiative recognised and honoured 
caregiver institutions for their compassionate and 
sustained support to vulnerable communities.
PUBLICATIONS
Published by CII-ER, a portfolio of reports, 
whitepapers and compendiums provided policy 
insight, sectoral analysis and Industry best practices to 
support inclusive and sustainable industrial growth 
across Eastern India.
MEMBERSHIP ENGAGEMENT
CII-ER facilitated 14 Members’ Meets, 19 Road Shows 
and 19 induction sessions across ﬁve states, leading to 
a total Membership increase of 8.53%.
Annual Report 2025-26158
NORTH EASTERN REGION
CII North Eastern Region (CII-NER) played a strategic 
and multi-dimensional role in advancing economic 
development across the North-East. Its interventions 
spanned policy advocacy, enterprise growth, skill 
development and partnership facilitation, engaging 
Government, Industry and civil society. Recognising 
the region’s unique social, geographic and economic 
context, CII adopted a diﬀerentiated approach that 
aligned regional strengths with national priorities 
while addressing structural challenges related to 
connectivity, market access, skills and scale.
ADVOCACY
During the year, CII-NER pursued a focused and 
sustained policy advocacy agenda through 
engagement with Union Ministries, State 
Governments, Members of Parliament, regulators and 
development institutions. The objective was to 
address systemic gaps, improve ease of doing 
business and enhance regional competitiveness.
CII’s recommendations on the UNNATI 2024 scheme 
covered extension of the registration window, easing 
of compliance requirements, recognition of past 
investments, expansion of eligible sectors and 
enhancement of ﬁnancial outlay to accelerate 
industrial uptake. Parallel eﬀorts focused on 
strengthening micro, small and medium enterprise 
(MSME) ecosystems through improved access to 
credit and venture funding, digital market integration, 
simpliﬁed approvals, sectoral branding and incentives 
supporting sustainable and green technologies.
In the oil and gas sector, CII shared proposals to 
position the North-East as a hydrocarbon super basin. 
These emphasised advanced geological studies, 
shared infrastructure, digital enabled exploration, 
streamlined approvals and a balanced approach 
integrating energy security with environmental, social 
and governance (ESG) priorities.
L-R: Pradeep Bagla, Chairman, CII North East and Managing Director, Amrit Cements; Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General and CEO, Indian 
Institute of Corporate Aﬀairs; Hekani Jakhalu, Advisor, Industry & Commerce, Government of Nagaland; Pu Lalnghinglova Hmar, Minister of State for 
Labour, Employment, Skill Development & Entrepreneurship, Sports, Youth Services, Tourism, Excise & Narcotics, Government of Mizoram and 
R Mukundan, President Designate,CII and Managing Director & CEO, Tata Chemicals Ltd launching the report on “CSR Investments in Northeast India: 
Understanding Barriers and Way Forward” at CII Northeast CSR Connect in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26 159
Sector-speciﬁc submissions were made for bamboo, 
pineapple, agarwood and rubber, focusing on value 
chain development, regulatory harmonisation, 
Geographical Indication (GI) based branding, logistics 
strengthening, cluster development and investment 
in post harvest and processing infrastructure. 
On broader economic facilitation, CII advocated 
permanent docks along the Brahmaputra, 
strengthened leadership capacity at the Directorate 
General of Foreign Trade - Guwahati, expansion of 
airport and cargo infrastructure in Tripura and 
improved access to Chittagong Port through seamless 
cross border connectivity.
To support inclusive development, CII submitted a 
detailed framework to the Ministry of Corporate 
Aﬀairs on improving corporate social responsibility 
(CSR) governance and impact in the region, 
highlighting transparency, innovation, simpliﬁed 
procedures, state level facilitation mechanisms and 
institutional capacity building. Engagements with 
national bodies included presentations to the 16th 
Finance Commission on sectoral priorities in Tripura 
and submissions to the Reserve Bank of India 
advocating enhanced credit deployment, ﬂexible 
lending norms and interest rate optimisation to 
strengthen ﬁnancial inclusion.
ACTION
MSME DEVELOPMENT AND MARKET 
ACCESS
CII-NER focused on enabling MSMEs to access 
markets, ﬁnance, technology and institutional 
support. Platforms and sector-speciﬁc interventions 
addressed long-standing challenges related to market 
reach, quality standards, compliance and adoption of 
modern production and logistics systems, 
encouraging competitiveness and formalisation.
AGRICULTURE, PLANTATIONS AND 
ALLIED SECTORS
CII addressed gaps across production, processing and 
distribution with emphasis on post-harvest 
infrastructure, logistics, branding and export- 
readiness. Coordinated, multi stakeholder 
approaches integrating agriculture, Industry, 
logistics and trade facilitation were advocated to 
enhance farmer incomes, reduce value loss and 
strengthen agri value chains.
MANUFACTURING AND INDUSTRIAL 
DEVELOPMENT
CII-NER supported manufacturing growth and 
downstream value addition through improved 
technology adoption, quality standards, skilled 
manpower and MSME-integration. Stakeholder 
engagement facilitated consensus on productivity 
enhancing interventions, environmentally responsible 
practices and scalable industrial pathways.
ENERGY, INFRASTRUCTURE AND 
CONNECTIVITY
Recognising the strategic role of energy and 
infrastructure, CII engaged on hydrocarbons, clean 
energy, logistics and multimodal connectivity. 
Advocacy focused on positioning the region as a 
contributor to national energy security while 
leveraging infrastructure to catalyse industrial 
development and employment.
Sarbananda Sonowal, Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways at 
the CII North East Oil & Gas Conclave in Guwahati
Annual Report 2025-26160
SKILLING AND WORKFORCE 
DEVELOPMENT
Building a future-ready workforce remained a cross 
cutting priority. CII-NER promoted alignment of 
education and training systems with Industry needs, 
strengthened Industry–Academia collaboration and 
supported adoption of digital and emerging 
technologies. Initiatives addressed advanced 
manufacturing, digital capability building for MSMEs and 
improved compliance and governance.
CSR, EMERGING SECTORS AND 
INTERNATIONAL ENGAGEMENT
CII facilitated structured, impact driven CSR 
engagement by aligning corporate priorities with 
State development needs and strengthening local 
implementation capacity.
Emerging sector initiatives focused on technology, 
creativity and youth participation, while international 
engagement supported trade, investment and 
knowledge partnerships, enhancing regional visibility 
and global integration.
Taken together, CII-NER’s engagements reﬂect an 
integrated advocacy approach that spans policy 
dialogue, enterprise enablement, skilling, CSR 
facilitation, emerging sectors and international 
engagement. By grounding its work in enterprise 
realities, workforce needs and ecosystem-level 
challenges, CII bridged the gap between policy intent 
and implementation. This approach contributed to 
positioning the North-East as a region with a 
coherent, forward-looking development narrative, 
aligned with national priorities and prepared for 
sustained inclusive growth.
L-R: Sony Virdi, Chairman CII Sikkim and Founder, Zion Education Trust; M Ravikumar, Principal Director, Department of MSME, Government of Sikkim; 
Tshering Thendup Bhutia, Minister of Commerce & Industries and Tourism & Civil Aviation, Government of Sikkim; Vinod Agrawal, Past Chairman, CII 
Gujarat State Council and Founder, Arunaya Organics Pvt Ltd at Sikkim Buyer Seller Meet in Ahmedabad
Ratan Lal Nath, Minister for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, 
Government of Tripura at the 5th Tripura Pineapple Festival in 
Agartala
Annual Report 2025-26 161
Annual Report 2025-26162
NORTHERN REGION
CII Northern Region (CII-NR) advanced CII’s national 
priorities by aligning its work with the overarching 
theme of Accelerating Competitiveness, Globalisation, 
Inclusivity, Sustainability and Trust. Guided by six 
strategic focus areas-policy advocacy, growth & 
inclusiveness, strengthening micro, small and medium 
enterprises (MSMEs), membership engagement, 
innovation & sustainability and skill development-the 
Region adopted a holistic and outcome-driven 
approach to Industry development. 
With representation across seven States and three Union 
Territories, CII-NR focused on enhancing industrial 
competitiveness; enabling ease of doing business (EoDB); 
strengthening infrastructure and skills; and fostering 
inclusive and sustainable growth through structured 
Government engagement and Member-led initiatives.
ADVOCACY
Policy advocacy remained central to the Region’s 
work, with over 260 policy recommendations 
submitted, of which over 50 were accepted and 
implemented. Interactions with key dignitaries from 
Central and State Governments, along with structured 
consultations, facilitated regular dialogue between 
Industry and Government, addressing region-speciﬁc 
challenges and long-term development priorities.
• CII established and led a multi-stakeholder Task 
Force for Chandigarh International Airport, to 
enhance international air connectivity and 
strengthen regional business access
• Industry recommendations were submitted on the 
Delhi Master Plan 2041, Draft Delhi Startup Policy 
2025 and Draft Delhi Industrial Policy 2025. A joint 
Government–Industry Task Force on Real Estate 
was proposed to improve EoDB. Key 
recommendations included rationalisation of circle 
rates, Floor Area Ratio (FAR) charges, reduction in 
amalgamation charges, single-window approvals, 
incentives for green buildings, slum and housing 
re-development, conversion of leasehold plots to 
freehold, optimal utilisation of Delhi Metro Rail 
Corporation land and reduced additional FAR 
charges for hotel plots
• Seven Industry recommendations on power sector 
reforms were accepted by the Haryana State 
Government, including consideration to enhance 
the Contract Demand relaxation limit and to 
prioritise upgrades in electricity transmission 
infrastructure. A proposal was submitted for a 
joint Task Force to position Haryana as a global 
business hub
L-R: Anjali Singh, Chairperson, CII Northern Region and Executive 
Chairperson, ANAND Group; Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, Chief Minister of 
Himachal Pradesh and Harshwardhan Chauhan, Minister for Industries, 
Parliamentary Aﬀairs and Labour & Employment, Government of Himachal 
Pradesh at the Himachal Pradesh State Annual Session and Business 
Conference on Future-Ready Himachal Pradesh in Shimla
Anjali Singh with Omar Abdullah, Chief Minister, Union Territory of 
Jammu & Kashmir at the 4th Regional Council Meeting in Srinagar

pages.title: CII Annual Report 2025-26 (pages 163-166)
pages.description: CII Annual Report 2025-26 — theme: Accelerating Competitiveness: Globalisation, Inclusivity, Sustainability, Trust.
pages.text:
Annual Report 2025-26 163
• In Himachal Pradesh, policy actions were accepted 
to safeguard industrial operations. Himachal 
Pradesh State Electricity Board Limited committed 
to restoring reliable power supply in Kala Amb 
following prolonged outages. Immediate 
reinforcement and legal action were mandated for 
a 66 KVA transmission tower at Village Banvirpur, 
Baddi, undermined by illegal mining, to prevent 
blackouts, protect jobs and ensure public safety
• Policy advocacy focused on industrial revival, 
investment facilitation and EoDB in Jammu & 
Kashmir. Sector-speciﬁc engagements addressed 
challenges across manufacturing, tourism and 
services
• Industry–Government engagement was 
strengthened through a joint CII–Punjab 
Development Commission Task Force, enabling 
structured dialogue and time-bound resolution of 
industrial and infrastructure issues.
• A major outcome was the acceptance to reduce 
stamp duty and registration fees on equitable 
mortgages, beneﬁting over 14 lakh MSMEs across 
Punjab and signiﬁcantly improving access to credit
• Targeted policy representations to the Rajasthan 
State Government resulted in the resolution of 
over 20 cases related to Rajasthan Investment 
Promotion Scheme (RIPS). In addition, 
recommendations were submitted on the 
development of Green Industrial Zones and 
amendments to Schedule 8 of the Environmental 
Impact Assessment (EIA) Notiﬁcation 2006
• Policy recommendations were submitted on the 
Uttar Pradesh Electronics Manufacturing Policy, 
along with representations for the development of 
a dedicated convention infrastructure in Lucknow 
to support investment promotion, Industry 
engagement and large-scale business events
• Sustained advocacy to enable GST input credit for 
hotels and immovable properties, by treating 
them at par with plant and machinery, resulted in 
a favourable Supreme Court judgement, with the 
State Government considering its implementation 
in Uttarakhand. In parallel, Industry inputs were 
submitted on the Uttarakhand Draft IT Policy 
through consultations with the CII Regional 
Committee on Digital Transformation.
ACTION
FLAGSHIP AND KEY EVENTS
CII-NR served as the Industry Partner for the Pravasi 
Rajasthani Diwas (PRD) organised by the Government of 
Rajasthan, supporting diaspora engagement and 
investment promotion through focused B2G meetings 
during the roadshows in Hyderabad, Kolkata and Surat.
The Region convened ﬂagship conferences and conclaves, 
bringing together Industry, Government and global 
stakeholders to deliberate on priority sectors and 
emerging trends. Notable platforms included the 
Conference on Industrial Transformation, Chandigarh 
Startup Conclave, Himachal Pradesh Apple Conclave, 
International Conference on Construction Equipment, 
International Automotive Design Conclave, CFO Leadership 
Conclave, Cloud Summit and UP Logistics & Supply Chain 
Summit, among others that reinforced the Region’s role as 
a catalyst for industrial growth and innovation.
MANUFACTURING & 
COMPETITIVENESS 
States across the Region aimed at strengthening 
industrial growth, EoDB and sectoral competitiveness. 
In Rajasthan, the Industry Helpdesk provided advisory 
support on industrial concerns. In Uttar Pradesh, 
engagement with the joint CII–Railways Task Force, 
along with organising the Railway Innovation Initiative 
in collaboration with Research Designs & Standards 
Organisation (RDSO), improved logistics eﬃciency, 
technology adoption and modernisation of industrial 
processes in the Railways sector.
The Region implemented learning and manufacturing 
excellence missions, quality circle competitions, training 
and certiﬁcation programmes through masterclasses, an 
AI immersion week and vendor development initiatives.
LABOUR, INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS 
AND TAXATION
Engaging on labour and taxation reforms, a Whitepaper 
on the ‘Deﬁnition of Wages’ was prepared on Labour 
Codes, providing policy inputs to support clarity and 
compliance. An event marking eight years of GST was 
organised in collaboration with the CGST 
Commissionerate, facilitating dialogue between Industry 
and tax authorities on implementation experiences, 
challenges and the evolving GST framework.
L - R: Anjali Singh; Bhajan Lal Sharma, Chief Minister of Rajasthan; Sanjay Agarwal, Chairman, CII Rajasthan and Founder MD & CEO, AU Small Finance Bank and 
V Srinivas, Chief Secretary, Government of Rajasthan at the Rajasthan State Annual Session in Jaipur
SKILL AND TALENT DEVELOPMENT
Skill development remained central to the Region’s 
growth agenda, aligning training infrastructure and 
curricula with Industry needs. Model Career Centres 
(MCCs) bridged demand–supply gaps by providing 
career guidance and skill training.
The inauguration of the Training Lab & Classroom at 
the CII–NBCC Multi Skill Training Institute (MSTI) in 
Ghitorni, New Delhi and launch of the MCC in Dehradun 
under Project Kafal led in collaboration with National 
Career Service (NCS), strengthened the Region’s 
capacity to deliver Industry-aligned skilling programmes 
and foster inclusive economic participation.
SUSTAINABILITY AND 
ENVIRONMENT
Initiatives in climate action, resource eﬃciency and 
environmental protection strengthened sustainability 
across the Region. The Crop Residue Management 
Initiative in Punjab and Haryana addressed paddy straw 
management across eight and ﬁve districts respectively, 
encompassing around 1000 villages and engaging over 
1,50,000 farmers. CSR-led disaster relief in Himachal 
Pradesh enhanced community resilience, while 
engagements with the Korea Trade-Investment 
Promotion Agency strengthened cooperation on CSR 
and economic collaboration.
Building on these eﬀorts, Solid Resource Management 
Centres in Kharu and Chuchot Blocks, Leh were 
established by CII Foundation, in collaboration with the 
Rural Development Department, Ladakh. These 
Centres will focus on capacity building, community 
engagement and pilot solutions to strengthen the 
region’s waste management ecosystem.
COMMUNITY AND SOCIAL IMPACT
Social impact and inclusion were strengthened 
through three chapters of the Indian Women Network 
(IWN), which advanced women’s leadership and 14 
chapters of Young Indians (Yi), which supported youth 
engagement through mentorship and 
entrepreneurship programmes.
Initiatives on mental resilience and emotional wellness 
reached vulnerable groups. Kashi Samvaad in Varanasi, 
Uttar Pradesh served as a platform for structured 
community dialogue, bringing together diverse 
stakeholders to encourage social cohesion and collective 
problem-solving. Flood relief eﬀorts in Punjab mobilised 
INR 44 lakh in member contributions to support 
aﬀected communities. Inclusion eﬀorts included the 
Purple Fair for Persons with Disabilities and Pink Police 
Booths in Uttar Pradesh to enhance women’s safety.
MEMBERSHIP ENGAGEMENT 
Engaging and supporting Members remained central 
to the Region’s initiatives. As of December, CII-NR had 
2858 members, including 423 new members inducted. 
Outreach expanded into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, with 
proposed zonal oﬃces in Bhiwadi, Rajasthan; 
Pantnagar, Uttarakhand; and Yamunanagar, Haryana.
A total of 33 Members' Meets and 9 Induction 
Meetings were conducted to deepen engagement 
and capture Members’ feedback. Through 19 
Committees and six Task Forces, the Region ensured 
sectoral representation, grassroots participation and 
focused execution across policy advocacy, capacity 
building and thought leadership.
Annual Report 2025-26164
SOUTHERN REGION
South India continues to be a crucial driver of India's 
economic transformation, contributing 32% to 
national Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and 30% to 
national manufacturing Gross Value Added (GVA). 
Under the theme ‘Accelerating South India’s 
Competitiveness: Globalisation, Inclusivity, 
Sustainability, Trust,' CII Southern Region (CII-SR) 
aligned its initiatives with the national agenda to 
ensure sustainable progress across the states of 
Southern India - Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, 
Puducherry, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.
CII-SR's engagement framework operated across ten 
strategic tracks: education, people skills and 
Industry-Institute linkages; holistic sustainability, 
environmental, social and governance (ESG) and 
climate action; AI-tech adoption; digital 
transformation and Industry 4.0; embracing energy 
transition; innovation and startup ecosystem; micro, 
small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and ease of 
doing business (EoDB) with focus on manufacturing 
competitiveness; global partnerships and 
international linkages; wellbeing and healthcare; 
brand building and sectoral promotion; and tourism. 
These tracks guided targeted interventions that 
strengthened industrial competitiveness while 
fostering inclusive and sustainable development.
ADVOCACY
CII-SR achieved signiﬁcant progress in advancing Industry 
priorities through structured policy dialogue and 
sectoral consultations. One hundred ﬁfty nine policy 
recommendations were submitted to policymakers, of 
which 41 were accepted or implemented.
ANDHRA PRADESH
• The vision document for the state’s economy, ‘Swarna 
Andhra Pradesh@2047’, launched with the goal of 
achieving a USD 2.4 trillion economy by 2047
• The Andhra Pradesh–CII Joint Consultative Forum 
held two meetings chaired by Shri Nara Lokesh, 
Minister of Human Resource Development and 
Information Technology and Shri K Vijayanand, Chief 
Secretary focused on strengthening 
Government–Industry collaboration, boosting 
investments and improving EoDB
• Fire Safety Regulatory Harmonisation Policy 
proposed to reduce compliance complexity and 
enable phased implementation
• Inputs for the Industrial Sustainability and Green 
Building Promotion Policy shared to drive GreenCo and 
Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) adoption, build 
capacity and streamline environmental clearances.
L - R: Chandrajit Banerjee, Director General, CII; K Vijayanand, Chief Secretary, Government of Andhra Pradesh; Venu Srinivasan, Past President, CII and 
Chairman Emeritus, TVS Motor Company; Onkar S Kanwar, Chairperson & Managing Director, Apollo Tyres; N Chandrababu Naidu, Chief Minister of 
Andhra Pradesh; N Chandrasekaran, Executive Chairman, Tata Sons; Rajiv Memani, President, CII and Regional Managing Partner of EY Africa India region 
& Chair – EY Growth Markets Council; Dr Preetha Reddy, Executive Vice Chairperson, Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd; Dr Suchitra K Ella, Vice President, CII 
and Co-Founder & Managing Director, Bharat Biotech International Ltd; Thomas John Muthoot, Chairman, CII Southern Region and Chairman, Muthoot 
Fincorp Ltd; BVN Rao, Chairman, CII Infrastructure Council and Business Chairman, GMR Group and Murali Krishna Gannamani, Chairman, CII Andhra 
Pradesh and Founder and CEO, Fluentgrid Ltd launching the Taskforce Report ‘Towards Swarna Andhra Pradesh@2047’ in New Delhi
Annual Report 2025-26 165
KARNATAKA
• Recommended enhancing GST procedures across 
sectors emphasising simpliﬁed compliance 
through uniﬁed jurisdiction and regulatory 
alignment to reduce operational complexity 
• CII is driving the Beyond Bengaluru agenda by 
strengthening district level engagement across 
Mysuru, Mangaluru, Belagavi and 
Hubballi–Dharwad through initiatives fostering 
entrepreneurship, MSME growth and technology 
adoption, while recommending Belagavi’s inclusion 
in the State’s industrial cluster and corridor 
network to support balanced regional development
• Phased and inﬂation-linked Minimum Wage 
Reform Policy proposed to balance workforce 
welfare with MSME sustainability, emphasising 
sector-speciﬁc structures.
KERALA
• Requested interim measures under Rule 11 of the 
Kerala Government Land Assignment (Regularisation 
of Contraventions) Rules, 2025 to mitigate losses 
arising from the suspension of industrial operations
• Flexible zoning and Land Utilisation Policy 
proposed to maximise usable industrial land in the 
context of limited availability and stringent 
environmental regulations
• Twin Cities Sustainable Urbanisation Policy 
recommended for integrated urban planning, 
shared infrastructure and complementary 
industrial development across city pairs.
PUDUCHERRY
• Advocated for EoDB Implementation Policy 
resulting in the passage of EoDB Bill in September
• Recommended key Electricity Board (EB) reforms, 
including delinking of Commune Panchayat 
jurisdiction, enhancement of power infrastructure, 
increased adoption of solar energy in industries 
and simpliﬁcation of name transfer procedures.
TELANGANA
• Gig and Platform Worker’s Social Security Policy 
proposed to ensure welfare coverage while providing 
clarity on fee structures, transparency in algorithms 
and balanced representation in welfare boards
• Evidence-based wage ﬁxation recommended to link 
wage revisions with inﬂation and economic 
indicators, avoiding steep increases that 
disproportionately impact MSMEs
• Labour law rationalisation addressing Employees' 
State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) dispensary 
allocation, ﬁxed term employment frameworks and 
raising thresholds to improve workforce ﬂexibility 
and compliance eﬃciency
• Integrated skill development proposed for 
establishing Model Career Centres and Multi Skill 
Training Institutes to enhance employability.
MANUFACTURING EXCELLENCE AND 
DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
CII–SR undertook initiatives in advanced Industry 4.0, smart 
manufacturing and digital transformation to position 
South India as a global hub for advanced manufacturing 
through technology adoption and innovation.
TAMIL NADU
• Semiconductor manufacturing cluster proposed 
for Coimbatore to leverage the city's engineering 
base and precision manufacturing expertise, with 
plug-and-play infrastructure
ACTION
COMPETITIVENESS
CII-SR built competitiveness through interventions in 
technology, quality and ﬁnance, driving excellence 
through initiatives like CFO Awards, Quality Circles, 
Kaizen and Poka-Yoke competitions, alongside 
learning missions to industries of excellence, training 
programmes, certiﬁcation courses and workshops 
that collectively enhanced skills, promoted innovation 
and strengthened organisational performance.
• Technical Textiles Manufacturing and Innovation 
Park recommended under National Technical 
Textiles Mission (NTTM) to drive product 
innovation, skill development and 
Industry-Academia collaboration
• Electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure 
expansion advocated to support the State's 
dominant EV production capacity.

pages.text:
SECTORAL PROMOTION
CII-SR's sectoral initiatives strengthened industrial 
ecosystems by showcasing innovations through expos 
and summits, fostering global collaborations and 
sustainable advancements. The 5th edition of the 
Surface and Coating Expo featured 303 exhibitors 
from 17 countries and attracted over 21,000 visitors, 
promoting the adoption of cutting-edge materials and 
processes. The 11th edition of Autoserve introduced 
the inaugural International Auto Tech Exhibition and 
Conference, exploring emerging solutions in 
automotive care, thereby driving market expansion 
and technological integration.
The 3rd edition of Nilgiris Economic Dialogue (NED) was 
organised in Ooty, Tamil Nadu, bringing together 
leaders from Industry, Government, Academia and social 
development for a curated exchange to co-create a 
bold, action-oriented agenda for India. The deliberation 
focused on the themes of circularity, geopolitics, shared 
prosperity and technology-enabled progress. 
South India strengthened its global healthcare and 
wellness presence by integrating Ayurveda with 
modern medicine, highlighted by the CII Kerala Health

Summit & Expo in Ernakulam
Flagship activities included the 21st India Innovation 
Summit – CII INNOVERGE, 23rd CII TN Connect, the 
Intelligent Manufacturing Summit, Digital Green 
Manufacturing Summit, CII Karnataka Smart Factory 
Summit and CII Telangana Man’Exe.
Tourism & Global Ayurveda Summit and Trichy Medical 
Tourism Conference showcasing the region’s strong 
medical infrastructure.
To boost deep-tech research & development, exports 
and investments and to position South India as a key 
defence and aerospace production hub, CII-SR 
organised platforms like CII AeroDef Tech Summit, 
Telangana Defence and Aerospace Conclave and 
CII-SIDM Regional Defence MSME Conclave. 
In agriculture, programmes emphasised value chain 
enhancements via novel approaches in cultivation, 
processing, standards, trade prospects and regulatory 
structures. The inaugural Telangana Turmeric Value 
Chain Summit, AgriVision, Ponmanjal Turmeric 
Conclave, TN Food NxT – Roots to Retail and TN Agro 
Connect Expo convened stakeholders to chart 
pathways for sector resilience and prosperity.
CII-SR hosted Global Capability Centre (GCC) Summits 
in Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, 
positioning them as premier destinations for GCCs. 
Focus on family businesses, startups, textiles, banking 
and ﬁnance was driven through special initiatives.
MSME ENGAGEMENT
CII-SR supported MSMEs by addressing challenges in 
access to markets, ﬁnance, technology and policy, driving 
global value chain integration, Industry 4.0 and digital 
adoption and export readiness while positioning them as 
engines of inclusive growth and competitiveness.
Annual Report 2025-26 167
Flagship initiatives and buyer-seller meets such as 4th 
edition of the CII-SR MSME Procurement Summit, 8th 
edition of the CII Telangana MSME Summit, CII Puducherry 
IndEx and CII Karnataka Integrate were organised.
Capacity and capability-building workshops for MSMEs 
were organised in Tier 2 & 3 cities to enhance MSMEs 
competencies in areas such as business strategy, 
manufacturing excellence, brand building, sustainability 
and digitalisation. 
CII-SR also launched the ‘CII for MSMEs – Compendium of 
Case Studies’, showcasing how enterprises leveraged CII 
Centres of Excellence to improve productivity, quality, 
digitalisation, logistics, ESG, innovation and exports.
SUSTAINABILITY
CII-SR advanced its sustainability agenda by driving ESG 
integration, renewable energy adoption and Net Zero 
alignment, while addressing climate transition risks, 
circular economy practices, water stewardship and 
sustainable ﬁnancing.
Key platforms included the Climate Action Competition, 
CII-SR Energy Transition Summit, CII Green Mobility 
Summit, CII Tamil Nadu Renewable Energy Summit, CII 
Karnataka Annual Energy Transition Conference, CII-SR 
Clean Mobility Summit, CII Andhra Pradesh 
Sustainability Summit, 2nd edition of CII-SR AquaSouth 
Summit and CII Mysuru ESG Conference & Expo.
The 17th CII-SR EHS Excellence Awards set new 
benchmarks by recognising 279 applications across 
categories, with 30 special category awards spanning 
air quality, water management, energy footprint, 
women in environment, health and safety (EHS), road 
safety and health risk management.
INTERNATIONAL ENGAGEMENT
CII-SR strengthened South India’s global standing 
through high level engagements and strategic 
partnerships that positioned the region as a preferred 
investment destination and expanded technology and 
market access.
Business delegations to South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, 
Cambodia, Oman, Germany and Austria facilitated 
knowledge exchange on operational excellence and 
sustainable growth. A CII Industry delegation 
accompanied Governments of Andhra Pradesh, 
Karnataka, Kerala and Telangana to the World 
Economic Forum, Davos, 2026. CII-SR engaged with 
visiting ambassadors and diplomats on collaboration 
in key sectors.
FUTURE-READY WORKFORCE
CII-SR's workforce development initiatives aimed at 
aligning education and skilling with emerging 
technologies, Industry requirements and India's 
economic transformation goals. It launched the 
College Excellence Cluster, an initiative to bridge 
Academia and Industry by oﬀering students and 
faculty industrial exposure, faculty development and 
student growth programmes. 
Key platforms such as CII-SR Higher Education 
Conclave, CII Tamil Nadu EduTech Conference, CII 
Karnataka Skill Summit, CII Telangana EDU Summit 
and CII Kerala Education Conclave brought together 
academicians, policymakers and Industry leaders to 
deliberate on internationalisation of higher education, 
research led learning models and skill based curricula.
INCLUSIVE DEVELOPMENT
CII-SR advanced community welfare through 
initiatives such as waterbody restoration, prison based 
skilling, livelihood programmes and Anganwadi 
upgrades, beneﬁting thousands of families.
Young Indians (Yi) engaged around 66,000 youth 
through its 23 chapters in the Region via initiatives 
such as science and tech festivals, mental health 
awareness campaigns, rural revival programmes and 
safety & environment drives.
The Indian Women Network (IWN) organised several 
activities and initiatives under the key pillars of - 
leadership advancement through programmes for 
women in manufacturing; women in tech & women 
entrepreneurs; mentorship; policy and advocacy; and 
membership engagement and branding.
MEMBERSHIP ENGAGEMENT
Membership engagement remained central to CII-SR’s 
initiatives, through 31 Members’ Meets and 11 New 
Member Induction Sessions, taking the total 
Membership to 3626 as of December, including 519 
new Members. To strengthen connect and gather 
feedback, 650 Member Outreach Meetings were 
organised regionwide.
Annual Report 2025-26168
WESTERN REGION
India’s western region comprising Maharashtra, 
Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Goa, contributes 
approximately 26% to national GDP, combining 
industrial scale, agricultural strength and tourism. 
Maharashtra and Gujarat lead manufacturing, ﬁnance 
and trade; Madhya Pradesh anchors agriculture with 
rising Industry; and Goa is a premier tourism hub.
ADVOCACY
CII Western Region (CII-WR) collaborated with the 
Governments of Goa, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and 
Maharashtra, conducting over 215 discussions with 
policymakers. CII participated in 53 Government 
committees and Task Forces across the region. 
Numerous Union and State Ministers, Chief Ministers 
and senior secretariat oﬃcials graced interventions 
aimed at promoting investments and driving growth 
and development across states. Notable among them 
were Shri Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India 
along with Shri Nitin Gadkari, Minister of Road 
Transport and Highways and Shri Piyush Goyal, 
Minister of Commerce and Industry. 
Over 200 recommendations pursued by CII-WR 
included issue-based representations policy inputs.
GOA
• Ease of doing business (EoDB) reforms included 
removing panchayat clearances outside industrial 
estates, streamlining factory approvals, providing 
land-lease rent concessions and allowing on-site 
worker housing
• Renewable energy measures proposed revisiting 
net-metering caps, time of day (TOD) tariﬀs and 
cross-subsidy surcharge, while continuing rooftop 
solar incentives and promoting clean-energy 
propulsion
• Infrastructure upgrades sought extension of 
mineral transport timings and improvements at 
Mormugao Port
• Industry status was granted to warehousing sector in 
Goa. Acceleration of solar energy adoption was kicked 
oﬀ with targeted support for industrial solar power 
utilisation
• Policy alignment was called for by harmonising the 
Goa Deposit Refund Scheme (DRS) with the Central 
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework, 
alongside productivity-linked workforce skilling
• To fast-track maritime and shipbuilding growth, 
proposals included a Goa State Maritime Board, 
shipbuilding parks with land, infrastructure and capital 
support, a Marine Technology Institute and a Naval 
Architecture and Shipbuilding Engineering degree.
The Goa Shipbuilding Vision 2037 was released.
GUJARAT 
• A survey-based report on micro, small and medium 
enterprise (MSME) loan accessibility in Gujarat was 
released, highlighting key ﬁnancing constraints and 
policy recommendations to improve credit ﬂow to 
small businesses
• Detailed recommendations for the Gujarat Textile 
Policy 2024 focused on enhancing competitiveness, 
while inputs on the State Policy for Electronic 
Component Manufacturing (ECM) aimed to 
strengthen domestic manufacturing, value-chain 
development and investments in electronics
• Air connectivity to-and-from Bhavnagar was 
enhanced, improving access and supporting growth 
• Apparel Industry incentives from non-municipal area 
policies were extended to urban areas in Gujarat, 
boosting investment and jobs
• Recommendations were submitted to 12 Task Forces 
under Industrial Policy 2020 aimed at strengthening 
industrial growth and implementation frameworks
• A 30-member CII Gujarat Industry delegation met 
with nine Gujarat MPs during the Monsoon Session, 
submitting the ‘Swarnim Gujarat White Paper’ with 
reform-oriented recommendations to strengthen 
competitiveness, innovation and sustainable growth.

• EoDB reforms proposed included leasehold-to-

renewals, faster pre-GST closures, rationalised taxes 
and consent fees, third-party audits, uniform digital 
stamp duty, ﬂexible factory hours and stamp duty

• Recommendations accepted included MP Drone and

Scheme for MSMEs.
MAHARASHTRA
• The CII–Maharashtra Industry–Parliamentarians 
interaction facilitated structured engagement

SECTOR FOCUS
Investment promotion remained a key focus, with CII 
playing a pivotal role in facilitating 
Industry–Government engagement. CII served as the 
national partner for the Vibrant Gujarat Regional 
Conferences and the Industry Partner for Maharashtra 
 Industry–policy synergy, with focus on 
manufacturing competitiveness, MSMEs, 
infrastructure, skilling and sustainability
• Following acceptance of CII recommendations by the 
Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB), MSMEs 
were allowed ﬂexibility to retroﬁt emission-control 
devices instead of scrapping, subject to compliance 
with prescribed emission norms
• Sustained advocacy resulted in extension of 
electricity duty exemption for industrial units in 
Vidarbha and Marathwada regions
• Recommendations included simplifying tech 
transfer, e-waste, data governance and 
environmental, social and governance (ESG) 
regulations; boosting food processing and 
agri-industries via lower input and logistics costs; 
developing smart manufacturing, consumer 
durable and cold-chain clusters; enhancing port 
and airport eﬃciency; strengthening 
Industry–Academia skilling and R&D; and oﬀering 
targeted incentives for pharma, automotive, EV 
and renewable energy, including power, land, 
approvals and ﬁscal support.

SOCIETY CONNECT
Young Indians (Yi) Western Region hosted the YiFi 
Summit featuring Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, 
Minister of Tourism and Culture. Key initiatives 
included Young Indians Parliament 2.0, blood 
donation drives, road safety campaigns, cross-chapter 
learning and Yi Pune’s memorandum of 
understanding (MoU) with Maharashtra Institute of 
Technology-World Peace University (MIT-WPU ). The 
Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue promoted 
collaborative problem-solving for Viksit Bharat@2047.
CII IWN strengthened women’s leadership, focusing 
on inclusivity, skill development, innovation and 
Industry–Academia engagement. India@100 
Foundation led initiatives in education, animal 
welfare, cleanliness and volunteerism across Mumbai.
communication and interpersonal skills. MSME Clinics 
were unveiled at the 11th edition of MSME Summit to 
help MSMEs scale sustainably and globally. 
Global trade and policy engagement were 
strengthened through targeted forums and Industry 
conclaves. Policy dialogue advanced through 
roundtables on US tariﬀs, customs and free trade 
agreement (FTA) updates and the India–UK FTA, while 
the 6th Global Trade Scenario Conclave highlighted 
diversiﬁed trade routes, green ports and stronger 
Industry–logistics collaboration. The Exports Conclave, 
‘Our Gateway to Global Success,’ enabled MSMEs to 
navigate global markets and boost export readiness.
Financial sector engagement was advanced through 
key initiatives including the Mutual Fund Summit, the 
Alternative Investment Fund Summit and the Annual 
Conference on Taxation, providing platforms for 
dialogue on investment trends, regulatory updates 
and strategic opportunities for stakeholders.
The themes of sustainability and governance featured 
prominently through the Conference on ESG & 
Corporate Governance, reinforcing ESG as a strategic 
growth enabler. This was complemented by the 
Renewables & Energy Conclave and workshops 
focusing on climate change, power and ESG.
Industry Dialogue, Government of Maharashtra’s 
AI4Agri Summit and the Madhya Pradesh investment 
roadshows. The maiden Madhya Pradesh Udyog 
Mahotsav further strengthened this eﬀort through 
sectoral events focused on MSMEs, textiles and green 
logistics.
Exhibitions enabled strategic platforms for technology 
diﬀusion and ecosystem convergence. The 3rd CII 
NexGen Mobility Show reinforced a uniﬁed Industry 
vision to accelerate R&D, enhance localisation and 
strengthen collaboration in next-generation mobility 
and clean transportation. CII WireTech strengthened 
Industry convergence by showcasing technologies 
across the wire and cable value chain, with a focus on 
quality, sustainability and inclusive growth.
The 21st CII Manufacturing Summit underscored the 
alignment of Production-Linked Incentive (PLI), PM 
Gati Shakti, GST 2.0 and the National Manufacturing 
Mission to drive manufacturing competitiveness. The 
8th Hospital Tech Summit, the 13th Safety Summit, 
the 6th Global Education Conclave and the 
Conference on Wellbeing at Work and Life addressed 
evolving priorities in healthcare, education and 
workforce wellbeing. 
The CII National Conference on Sustainable 
Shipbuilding 2025 underscored India’s commitment to 
sustainable, innovative and globally competitive 
shipbuilding, while the Food Processing Conclave held 
in Nagpur highlighted eﬀorts to advance the country’s 
food processing sector and position Vidarbha as a 
leading agro industrial hub. Complementing these 
sector-focused initiatives, specialised conclaves on 
marketing and branding equipped members with 
contemporary digital strategies for building 
sustainable brand equity. 
Capability building and MSME development were 
reinforced through learning missions on 
manufacturing excellence, quality circle competitions, 
six sigma workshops, Industry 4.0 sessions, faculty 
development programmes, buyer–seller meets, 
export ﬁnance programmes for MSMEs, 
mentor–mentee initiatives and workshops on 
shopﬂoor management, new labour codes and

MEMBERSHIP CONNECT
Membership engagement was strengthened through 
58 meetings with local associations and 1635 Members 
via virtual and in-person interactions. Members were 
updated on CII services through 43 Member Meets,
18 induction sessions and 11 roadshows. 
Key interactions included Rajiv Memani, President, CII 
and Regional Managing Partner of EY Africa India 
region & Chair – EY Growth Markets Council and
Dr Suchitra K Ella, Vice President, CII and Co-Founder 
& Managing Director, Bharat Biotech International 
Limited fostering collaboration on innovation, MSME 
growth and Industry–Academia partnerships. 
Vir Advani, Deputy Chairman, CII-WR and CMD, Blue 
Star Ltd, engaged with Members across a record
12 zones; Ahmedabad, Bhopal, Indore, Kolhapur, 
Mumbai, Nagpur, Nashik, Panaji, Rajkot, Surat, Thane 
and Vadodara; underscoring an unprecedented level 
of regional outreach and engagement.
The 16 sub-committees and four Task Forces engaged 
with Members in multiple sectors and functional 
areas, consistently providing networking and learning 
opportunities. 
The CII Vidarbha Zonal Oﬃce was inaugurated in 
Nagpur by Shri Nitin Gadkari. The new oﬃce will serve 
as a vital platform for policy advocacy, enhancing MSME 
competitiveness, skilling and fostering innovation. 
INTERNATIONAL ENGAGEMENT
CII led delegations from Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and 
Maharashtra to the World Economic Forum, 
highlighting Gujarat’s focus on sports, Global 
Capability Centres (GCCs), semiconductors and 
renewable energy; Madhya Pradesh’s investment 
opportunities across manufacturing, renewables, IT, 
agriculture and logistics, including an MoU with DP 
World for the Powarkheda Multimodal Logistics and 
Food Park; and Maharashtra’s MoUs with a total 
investment value of INR 30 lakh crore which are 
expected to generate over 40 lakh jobs.
Global outreach spanned 20 countries across the 
Middle East, Asia-Paciﬁc, Europe and Latin America, 
advancing trade, investment and policy dialogue. 
These encompassed international delegations, 
interactions and Industry forums involving heads of 
state, senior leaders from Government and Industry. 
A Mumbai networking reception hosted Consul 
Generals and diplomats, alongside senior Indian 
Industry leaders, fostering informal dialogue and 
international collaboration. CII facilitated overseas 
roadshows in Spain, Switzerland, UAE, Australia, 
Singapore and South Korea to promote investments in 
the region.
Flagship Middle East engagements included the Dubai 
India Business Forum, India–UAE Business Summit, 
Abu Dhabi Investment Forum and India–Saudi 
Investment Meet, supported by high-level interactions 
with H.E. Dr Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, UAE Minister 
of Foreign Trade, Shri Piyush Goyal and Ahmed Bin 
Sulayem, Dubai Multi Commodities Centre (DMCC).
Europe-focused engagements included a dialogue 
with ODDO BHF in Germany, centred on investment 
and capital ﬂows, as well as a high-level dinner with 
the Deputy Prime Minister of Italy. 
Asia-Paciﬁc cooperation was reinforced through 
knowledge-exchange initiatives, including the Consul 
General of Japan’s visit to the CII Skill Centre and 
media engagement with senior journalists from 
Bangladesh. The Mumbai International Summit served 
as a platform for cross-border collaboration, strategic 
dialogue and global networking, further strengthening 
India’s international economic engagement.

MYCII - ONLINE SERVICES
MyCII, one of India’s largest online business resource 
platforms, provides CII stakeholders with timely

Industry. In addition, CII facilitates networking among 
Members and provides them access to approximately 9

The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) works to create and sustain an environment conducive to the 
development of India, partnering Industry, Government and civil society through advisory and consultative 
processes.
CII is a non-government, not-for-proﬁt, industry-led and industry-managed organisation, with around 9,700 
members from the private as well as public sectors, including SMEs and MNCs, and an indirect membership 
of over 365,000 enterprises from 318 national and regional sectoral industry bodies.
For more 130 years, CII has been engaged in shaping India’s development journey and works proactively on 
transforming Indian Industry’s engagement in national development. CII charts change by working closely 
with the Government on policy issues, interfacing with thought leaders, and enhancing eﬃciency, 
competitiveness, and business opportunities for industry through a range of specialised services and 
strategic global linkages. It also provides a platform for consensus-building and networking on key issues.
Through its dedicated Centres of Excellence and Industry competitiveness initiatives, promotion of 
innovation and technology adoption, and partnerships for sustainability, CII plays a transformative part in 
shaping the future of the nation. Extending its agenda beyond business, CII assists industry to identify and 
execute corporate citizenship programmes across diverse domains, including aﬃrmative action, 
livelihoods, diversity management, skill development, empowerment of women, and sustainable 
development, to name a few.
For 2025-26, CII has identiﬁed “Accelerating Competitiveness: Globalisation, Inclusivity, Sustainability, 
Trust” as its theme, prioritising ﬁve key pillars. During the year, CII will align its initiatives to drive strategic 
action aimed at enhancing India’s competitiveness by promoting global engagement, inclusive growth, 
sustainable practices, and a foundation of trust.
With 70 oﬃces, including 12 Centres of Excellence, in India, and 9 overseas oﬃces in Australia, Egypt, 
Germany, Indonesia, Singapore, UAE, UK, and USA, as well as institutional partnerships with about 250 
counterpart organisations in almost 100 countries, CII serves as a reference point for Indian industry and 
the international business community.
